## W984. Customer Water Tank & Pump System Sizing Recommendation Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests water tank and/or pump sizing recommendation at store or via mobile app |
| **Frequency** | ~3,000–4,000 consultations/month chain-wide (~15–20/store/month) |
| **Volume** | 1 system per consultation; average 1 system |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Plumbing) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Plumbing Specialist), Customer, Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

Water supply reliability is a critical concern for Philippine households and businesses, particularly in provincial areas where municipal water pressure is low or supply is intermittent. Many BuildRight customers need a complete water storage and distribution system: a water tank (polyethylene or stainless steel, ranging from 200 liters to 10,000 liters), a water pump (shallow well jet pump, deep well submersible, or pressure booster pump), piping connections, float valves, and accessories. Sizing is complex — a tank too small runs dry during supply interruptions; a tank too large wastes money and space. A pump too weak cannot deliver adequate pressure to upper floors; a pump too powerful wastes electricity and shortens pipe life. The Philippine market has additional considerations: NWRB (National Water Resources Board) regulations for well pumps, LGU requirements for water tank installations in commercial buildings, and typhoon preparedness (ensuring water supply when power is interrupted). This service drives high-value sales (a complete system averages PHP 15,000–50,000) and creates long-term customer relationships through pump maintenance and replacement parts.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Water Demand Assessment**: Sales Associate collects: (a) number of household/establishment occupants; (b) number of bathrooms, kitchen sinks, laundry areas, and garden taps; (c) number of floors in the building (affects pump head pressure requirement); (d) water source — municipal supply (with pressure/volume issues), shallow well (≤25ft depth), deep well (>25ft); (e) current water supply schedule (24/7, specific hours, intermittent); (f) available tank installation space (ground level, roof deck, inside utility room); (g) budget range | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 8–12 min |
| 2 | **Tank Sizing Calculation**: System calculates recommended tank capacity: (a) daily water consumption = occupants × 150 liters/person/day (PH standard residential); commercial/industrial uses higher factors; (b) desired storage days = 1–3 days for municipal supply backup, 1 day minimum for well systems; (c) tank capacity = daily consumption × storage days; (d) system recommends standard tank sizes (200L, 500L, 1000L, 2000L, 3000L, 5000L, 10000L) rounding up to nearest available size; (e) tank material recommendation — polyethylene (lightweight, UV-stabilized, economy), stainless steel (durable, hygienic, premium); (f) installation type — freestanding (ground level), elevated platform (roof deck), horizontal/vertical orientation based on available space | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Pump Sizing & Selection**: System calculates pump specification: (a) required flow rate (liters per minute) based on simultaneous fixture usage (typically 2–3 fixtures simultaneously in residential); (b) total dynamic head (TDH) = vertical lift (suction head + discharge head to highest fixture) + friction loss (pipe length × friction factor per pipe diameter); (c) pump type recommendation — shallow well jet pump (depth ≤25ft, PH most common), deep well submersible pump (depth >25ft), pressure booster pump (municipal supply with low pressure), automatic pump with pressure tank (for consistent pressure without cycling); (d) horsepower rating — 0.5HP (1-story, 1 bathroom), 1HP (2-story, 2–3 bathrooms), 1.5HP (large residential/commercial), 2HP+ (commercial/industrial); (e) power supply consideration — single-phase 220V (residential) vs. three-phase (commercial) | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 4 | **Accessories & Piping Recommendation**: System generates complete bill of materials: (a) PVC pipes (PVC schedule 40) — sizes based on flow rate (typically ¾" to 1¼" for residential); (b) fittings — elbows, tees, couplings, adapters, threaded connectors; (c) float valve (mechanical or electronic) for automatic tank refill; (d) gate valves/ball valves for isolation; (e) check valve (non-return) to prevent backflow; (f) pressure tank (for automatic pump systems — eliminates pump cycling); (g) pressure gauge and pressure switch; (h) pump controller (automatic dry-run protection mandatory for well pumps); (i) electrical wiring, circuit breaker, and waterproof outdoor switch; (j) pipe sealant (Teflon tape, solvent cement); (k) flexible connector hoses; (l) water filter (sediment filter recommended for well systems) | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 5 | **Customer Review, Quotation & Service Referral**: Customer reviews complete system recommendation with itemized pricing; Sales Associate: (a) presents total system cost and per-item breakdown; (b) offers installation service referral per W138 (plumber installation for complete system); (c) offers pipe cutting and threading service per W944 for custom pipe lengths; (d) creates POS quotation per W542 valid for 14 days; (e) quotation saved to customer loyalty account per W894; (f) for well pump installations: advises customer on NWRB well permit requirements and recommends licensed well driller referral | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Water system sizing calculator module (POS and mobile app) with PH-specific consumption factors
- Product catalog with tank dimensions, pump specifications, and compatibility matrix
- POS quotation module (W542) for complete system bill of materials
- Customer loyalty account integration for quotation saving (W894)
- Installation service referral (W138) for plumber installation
- Pipe cutting service (W944) for custom pipe lengths
- Real-time inventory availability per store for bulky items (tanks, pumps)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Oversizing/undersizing risk**: Incorrect sizing wastes customer money (oversized pump/tank) or fails to deliver adequate water supply (undersized); calculator must use conservative PH residential consumption factors and account for peak simultaneous usage; Sales Associate training on PH plumbing standards per W51 mitigates
- **Power outage vulnerability**: Water pumps require electricity; during typhoons when power is frequently interrupted, pumped water systems fail; Sales Associate should recommend: (a) oversized tank for gravity-fed emergency supply; (b) generator compatibility for pump operation during outages per W913; (c) manual pump backup option for critical installations
- **Well water quality**: Shallow well water in PH may contain contaminants (bacteria, iron, manganese); Sales Associate should recommend water testing and filtration; BuildRight does not provide water testing services but can refer customers to accredited testing laboratories
- **Bulky item logistics**: Water tanks (especially 1000L+ sizes) and large pumps are bulky and heavy; store storage space is limited; delivery scheduling per W5D is mandatory for tanks above 500L; loading assistance per W950 required
- **Competitive pricing sensitivity**: Water tanks and pumps are commodity items with price-transparent online competition; BuildRight's value-add is the professional sizing service, complete system recommendation, and installation referral — not lowest price on individual items

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Plumbing Specialist)**: Water system consultations consume ~1.5–2.5 hours/day at 15–20 consultations; absorbed by existing Plumbing Department Sales Associate with plumbing product certification per W51
- **Training**: 12-hour water system sizing and pump selection certification per W51; includes TDH calculation, PH residential plumbing standards, and accessory cross-selling
- **No incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Water demand assessment: 8–12 min
- Tank sizing calculation: 3–5 min
- Pump sizing & selection: 5–8 min
- Accessories & piping recommendation: 5–8 min
- Customer review & quotation: 5–10 min
- **Total per consultation**: 26–43 min of staff time

## W985. Store-Level Customer Aircon Sizing & BTU/Horsepower Calculation Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests aircon sizing recommendation at store appliance section or via mobile app |
| **Frequency** | ~8,000–10,000 calculations/month chain-wide (~40–50/store/month); peaks March–May (PH summer) |
| **Volume** | 1–3 rooms per consultation; average 1.6 rooms |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Home Appliances) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Appliance Specialist), Customer, Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

Air conditioning is the highest-value appliance category for BuildRight Depot and a necessity in the Philippine tropical climate where temperatures regularly exceed 33°C with 70–90% humidity. Correct sizing is critical: an undersized aircon runs continuously without reaching target temperature (wasting electricity and shortening compressor life), while an oversized aircon cycles on/off too frequently (causing temperature swings, poor humidity removal, and wasted energy). Philippine residential rooms present unique sizing challenges: high ceilings (2.7–3.5m common in PH construction), large windows (poor insulation), concrete walls (thermal mass retention), and heat-generating appliances (kitchens). The Philippine market uses both BTU/hr (international) and HP/horsepower (local terminology) ratings interchangeably — 1HP ≈ 9,000 BTU, 1.5HP ≈ 12,000 BTU, 2HP ≈ 18,000 BTU. Inverter technology has transformed the market (30–50% energy savings over conventional units) but adds complexity to sizing recommendations. This service is a major differentiator during the March–May summer peak when aircon sales can account for 15–20% of total store revenue.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Room Assessment & Data Collection**: Sales Associate collects room parameters: (a) room dimensions — length × width × ceiling height (meters); (b) room type — bedroom, living room, kitchen, office, commercial space; (c) window area and orientation — north/south/east/west facing; window type (jalousie, sliding, awning, fixed glass); glass type (clear, tinted, reflective); presence of curtains/blinds; (d) wall material — concrete hollow block (CHB, most common in PH), wood frame, gypsum board partition; (e) insulation — none (typical PH residential), foam panel, fiberglass; (f) room occupancy — number of people typically in room; (g) heat sources — direct sunlight exposure, number of heat-generating appliances (refrigerator, oven, computer, TV); (h) floor level — ground floor, upper floor, top floor (roof heat gain); (i) existing electrical capacity — dedicated circuit available? Amperage of circuit breaker? | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 8–12 min |
| 2 | **BTU/HP Calculation & Unit Recommendation**: System calculates: (a) base cooling load = room area (sqm) × 500 BTU/sqm (PH tropical baseline for typical residential); (b) adjustments — ceiling height > 2.7m (+10%), west-facing window (+10%), large window area > 40% of wall (+10%), kitchen/heat sources (+4,000 BTU), top floor under roof (+15%), poor insulation (+10%); each occupant beyond first (+600 BTU); (c) total required BTU = base load + adjustments; (d) recommended unit size — 0.5HP/5,000BTU (small bedroom ≤10sqm), 0.75HP/7,000BTU (bedroom 10–14sqm), 1HP/9,000–10,000BTU (bedroom 14–18sqm), 1.5HP/12,000BTU (master bedroom/living room 18–25sqm), 2HP/18,000BTU (living room 25–35sqm), 2.5HP/24,000BTU (large living room 35–50sqm), cassette/duct type ≥3HP (commercial); (e) unit type recommendation — window type (economy, easy installation, typical PH), split type (inverter, quieter, more efficient), portable (rental/temporary), floor-mounted (large rooms), cassette/duct (commercial); (f) inverter vs. conventional recommendation — inverter recommended for rooms used ≥8 hours/day (bedrooms, offices); conventional acceptable for intermittent use (living rooms, guest rooms) | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Electrical Compatibility Check**: Sales Associate verifies: (a) required electrical load — unit wattage (typically 700W–2,500W depending on HP rating); (b) customer's circuit breaker amperage — standard PH residential circuit is 20A/30A; (c) dedicated circuit requirement — units ≥1.5HP require dedicated circuit; (d) wiring gauge — units ≥1HP require 2.0mm² AWG14 wire minimum; ≥2HP require 3.5mm² AWG12; (e) Meralco/utility provider demand — some areas have limited residential electrical capacity; (f) system flags if customer's electrical infrastructure is incompatible and recommends licensed electrician referral per W989 | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 4 | **Cross-Sell Accessories & Services**: Sales Associate recommends: (a) aircon installation service per W138 (professional installation with copper piping, drainage hose, and electrical connection); (b) wall bracket/concealed mount for split-type outdoor unit; (c) aircon cover (off-season protection during Nov–Feb when usage drops); (d) air filter replacement schedule (clean monthly, replace quarterly); (e) voltage regulator/AVR (recommended for areas with unstable voltage — common in provincial PH); (f) drain hose and condensate pump (for units without gravity drainage); (g) extended warranty registration per W935; (h) electrical supplies per W991 (wiring, circuit breaker, outlet) if customer needs electrical upgrade | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 5 | **Quotation & Order Processing**: Customer reviews recommendations; Sales Associate: (a) presents total cost including unit, accessories, and installation; (b) creates POS quotation per W542 valid for 7 days (aircon pricing is volatile during summer peak); (c) for split-type units: coordinates installation scheduling per W138 with 2–5 day lead time; (d) for window-type units: customer may self-install or request installation service; (e) processes sale or saves quotation to customer loyalty account per W894; (f) system registers unit serial number at POS for warranty activation per W33 | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Aircon sizing calculator module (POS and mobile app) with PH-specific heat load factors
- Product catalog with aircon specifications (BTU, HP, wattage, EER, dimensions, weight)
- Electrical compatibility checker module integrated with product catalog
- POS quotation module (W542) for itemized recommendation
- Installation service scheduling per W138
- Serial number registration at POS for warranty per W33 and product registration per W935
- Customer loyalty account integration for quotation saving (W894)
- Real-time inventory availability with seasonal stock monitoring

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Summer stock-outs**: Aircon demand during March–May peak can exceed supply, especially for popular inverter models (1HP and 1.5HP); Category Manager must pre-position seasonal stock per W960; emergency procurement per W60 may be needed for unexpected demand spikes; Sales Associate must manage customer expectations on stock availability and delivery lead times
- **Electrical incompatibility**: Many PH homes (especially older construction) have insufficient electrical capacity for aircon installation; customers who purchase without checking may require costly electrical upgrades; the electrical compatibility check in Step 3 mitigates this risk
- **Installation quality**: Poor installation (undercharged refrigerant, kinked copper piping, improper drainage, inadequate sealing) causes performance issues and customer complaints; installation partner quality audit per W213 ensures installer standards
- **Price transparency**: Aircon prices are highly visible online (Lazada, Shopee, manufacturer websites); customers frequently compare prices on mobile phones while in-store; Sales Associate must emphasize BuildRight's value-add (professional sizing, installation service, warranty support, after-sales service) rather than competing purely on unit price
- **Return complexity**: Installed aircons cannot be easily returned; clear sizing verification in Steps 1–2 and customer sign-off before installation reduce return disputes; manufacturer defects handled through warranty per W33

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Appliance Specialist)**: Aircon consultations consume ~3–4 hours/day during summer peak (March–May), ~1 hour/day off-season; absorbed by existing Appliance Section Sales Associate with aircon product certification per W51
- **Training**: 8-hour aircon sizing and product knowledge certification per W51; includes heat load calculation, inverter technology, and PH electrical requirements
- **No incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Room assessment & data collection: 8–12 min
- BTU/HP calculation & recommendation: 3–5 min
- Electrical compatibility check: 3–5 min
- Cross-sell accessories & services: 5–8 min
- Quotation & order processing: 5–10 min
- **Total per consultation**: 24–40 min of staff time

## W986. Store-Level Customer Rebar Cutting, Bending & Fabrication Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer (contractor, builder, or homeowner) requests rebar cutting, bending, or custom fabrication at store |
| **Frequency** | ~5,000–7,000 transactions/month chain-wide (~25–35/store/month) |
| **Volume** | Average 50–200 pieces per transaction; 1–3 bar sizes per order |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Lumber & Building Materials) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Steel Specialist), Customer, Receiving Clerk (steel inventory), Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

Steel reinforcement bars (rebar) are the structural backbone of Philippine construction, used in virtually every residential, commercial, and infrastructure project. Rebar is sold in standard 6-meter (20ft) lengths in sizes ranging from 10mm (Grade 33, light residential) to 25mm (Grade 60, structural/commercial). Contractors frequently need rebar cut to specific lengths (for stirrups, ties, and column dowels) or bent into hooks, L-shapes, U-shapes, and custom profiles for beam and column reinforcement. Manual rebar cutting and bending at construction sites is labor-intensive and imprecise; BuildRight's in-store cutting and bending service saves contractor labor time, ensures dimensional accuracy, and increases store revenue through cutting/bending fees and associated sales (tie wire, chair supports, spacers, concrete, cement). The service is particularly valuable for small-to-medium contractors who do not own rebar fabrication equipment. Post-typhoon reconstruction surges create massive demand spikes for rebar fabrication services.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Order Intake & Specification**: Customer provides rebar specifications: (a) rebar size (10mm, 12mm, 16mm, 20mm, 25mm) and grade (Grade 33, Grade 40, Grade 60); (b) cut lengths — specify number of pieces and length per piece (in cm or inches); (c) bend requirements — hook (90° or 180°, standard hook length = 6× bar diameter), L-bend (specify angle and leg lengths), U-shape (specify width and leg lengths), stirrup (specify dimensions for rectangular/ square ties); (d) quantity per specification; (e) reference to structural plan if available (Sales Associate can interpret simple rebar schedules); Sales Associate creates service work order (SWO) per W544 | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 8–15 min |
| 2 | **Feasibility Check & Quotation**: Sales Associate confirms: (a) rebar size availability — system checks real-time inventory per store; (b) bending feasibility — minimum bend radius = 3× bar diameter for Grade 33, 4× bar diameter for Grade 60 (PH structural engineering standard per NSCP); tight bends risk bar fracture; (c) maximum pieces per order — store capacity: ~200 pieces/hour for cutting only, ~100 pieces/hour for cutting + bending; (d) system generates quotation: rebar material cost (per piece at standard 6m length) + cutting fee (per cut) + bending fee (per bend) + waste factor (offcuts <1m are scrap per W443); quotation valid for 3 days | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 3 | **Order Acceptance & Payment**: Customer accepts quotation; Sales Associate processes payment at POS — material cost + cutting fee + bending fee in single transaction; POS prints SWO receipt with: order number, rebar specifications, cut/bend details, promised ready time (standard: 2–4 hours for orders ≤100 pieces; next day for larger orders); system allocates rebar from inventory and creates fabrication instruction for Steel Specialist | Sales Associate / Cashier | Department Supervisor | 5 min |
| 4 | **Rebar Cutting & Bending Execution**: Steel Specialist retrieves rebar from yard storage per W3B; dons PPE per W140 (cut-resistant gloves, safety goggles, steel-toe boots, hard hat); performs operations: (a) cutting — uses hydraulic rebar cutter (capacity: up to 25mm); cuts to specified lengths with ±5mm tolerance; (b) bending — uses hydraulic rebar bender (capacity: up to 25mm); bends to specified angles and dimensions with ±3° angular tolerance; (c) sorts and bundles finished pieces by specification with tie wire; (d) tags each bundle with SWO number and customer name; (e) records waste offcuts — pieces <1m dispositioned to scrap per W443; (f) for orders exceeding same-day capacity: queues remaining work for next morning and notifies customer of pickup time | Sales Associate (Steel Specialist) | Department Supervisor | 15–45 min (depends on order size) |
| 5 | **Quality Inspection & Customer Handover**: Steel Specialist inspects: (a) dimensional accuracy — lengths ±5mm, bend angles ±3°; (b) bar integrity — no cracks, kinks, or excessive deformation at bends; (c) quantity per specification; failed inspection → re-cut/re-bend from new bar, waste piece to scrap; customer inspects finished pieces and signs acceptance on SWO; system closes SWO and posts sale; customer loads rebar at yard loading zone per W438; vehicle loading assistance per W950 provided for heavy orders | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 6 | **Daily Station Cleanup & Waste Disposal**: At end of day: Steel Specialist cleans rebar cutting/bending station; applies rust preventive to cutter and bender blades; collects steel offcuts in scrap bin; steel scrap sold to recycler per W443 (salvage monetization); system records daily scrap weight for inventory reconciliation; rebar fabrication tools inspected — hydraulic fluid levels, blade sharpness, bender pin condition | Sales Associate (Steel Specialist) | Department Supervisor | 15 min/day |

### System Touchpoints
- POS service work order module (W544) for order creation and payment
- Real-time inventory availability check per rebar size, grade, and store
- Inventory allocation and consumption posting with waste factor
- Quotation generation with dynamic pricing (material + cutting fee + bending fee)
- Yard inventory management per W3B for outdoor steel storage
- Vehicle loading assistance per W950 at yard loading zone
- Scrap disposition tracking per W443 for steel offcuts
- PPE compliance tracking per W140

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Safety risk**: Rebar cutting and bending involves hydraulic equipment with significant pinch/crush points; mandatory PPE enforcement, equipment guard maintenance, and incident reporting per W140 mitigate; steel toe boots mandatory in yard area; first aid kit per W501 accessible at yard station
- **Tolerance disputes**: Contractors may have strict tolerance requirements for structural rebar (especially for NSCP-compliant engineering projects); Sales Associate must clearly communicate ±5mm length and ±3° bend tolerance at quotation stage; custom tolerances available with manual verification at additional cost
- **Waste factor**: Standard 6-meter bars cut to non-standard lengths generate 5–20% waste depending on cut pattern; system must optimize cutting sequence to minimize waste (nesting algorithm); waste cost either absorbed in cutting fee or passed to customer depending on cut pattern complexity
- **Weather exposure**: Rebar fabrication is performed in the outdoor yard area; rain prevents safe operation of hydraulic equipment; during rainy season (June–October), covered fabrication area or rescheduling may be required; customer must be informed of potential delays during inclement weather
- **Queue management**: During peak construction season (January–May, post-typhoon reconstruction), wait times for fabrication can exceed 4 hours; queue management system with SMS notification when order is ready improves customer experience

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Steel Specialist)**: Rebar fabrication consumes ~3–5 hours/day at 25–35 orders; absorbed by existing Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor or Sales Associate with steel fabrication certification per W51
- **Training**: 16-hour rebar cutting and bending certification per W51; includes hydraulic equipment operation, NSCP bend radius standards, and safety protocols
- **No incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Order intake & specification: 8–15 min
- Feasibility check & quotation: 5–8 min
- Order acceptance & payment: 5 min
- Cutting & bending execution: 15–45 min
- Quality inspection & handover: 5–10 min
- Daily cleanup: 15 min
- **Total per transaction**: 38–83 min of staff time (varies heavily by order size)

## W987. Customer Fence & Gate Material Estimation & Design Recommendation Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests fence/gate material estimation at store or via mobile app |
| **Frequency** | ~3,500–4,500 estimations/month chain-wide (~17–22/store/month) |
| **Volume** | 1 fence/gate project per estimation; average perimeter 30–80 linear meters |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Lumber & Building Materials) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Steel/Hardware Specialist), Customer, Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

Property fencing is a near-universal requirement in the Philippines for security, boundary demarcation, and privacy. Unlike developed markets where pre-fabricated fence panels are standard, Philippine residential fencing is predominantly custom-built using hollow block (CHB) walls, steel picket fences, or a combination (CHB base with steel grill upper portion). Gate fabrication is almost entirely custom — made-to-measure steel swing gates or sliding gates that must match the fence style and opening width. The material estimation requires calculating posts (steel tubular or concrete), fencing material (CHB, steel bars, wire mesh, or pre-painted sheets), footings (concrete, rebar), gate frames, hinges, latches, and paint/finishing. Errors in estimation cause project delays (customer must return for additional materials) or over-purchasing (especially concrete and steel which are difficult to return). This service is particularly valuable for BuildRight's trade customer segment (30% of revenue) — contractors who quote fence/gate projects need accurate material lists and pricing to prepare competitive bids.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Scope & Site Intake**: Customer provides project details: (a) total fence perimeter (linear meters); (b) fence height (typical PH residential: 1.8m–2.4m); (c) fence type — CHB hollow block wall, steel picket/tubular, welded wire mesh on steel frame, pre-painted corrugated on steel frame, chain-link, or combination; (d) gate requirements — number of gates, gate opening width (pedestrian: 1.0–1.2m, vehicle: 3.0–5.0m), gate type (swing single, swing double, sliding); (e) ground conditions — flat, sloped, rocky (affects footing depth and concrete volume); (f) existing structures — retaining walls, existing posts; (g) style/aesthetic preference (decorative spear tops, flat top, arch top) | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |
| 2 | **Material Quantity Calculation**: System calculates: (a) posts — steel tubular posts (2" round or square) spaced at 2.0–2.5m centers; post count = perimeter ÷ spacing + 1; gate posts use heavier 3" or 4" tubular; post length = fence height + 0.6m footing depth; (b) horizontal rails — 2–3 runs per fence section (bottom, middle, top) in steel tubular (1" round or 1½" rectangular); total rail length = perimeter × number of runs; (c) infill material — steel pickets (quantity = section length ÷ picket spacing, typically 10–15cm); or CHB (blocks per sqm ≈ 12.5 for standard 8"×16"×4" at 10mm joint); or welded wire mesh (rolls in 25m lengths × fence height); (d) concrete for footings — post footing volume (0.3m depth × 0.2m diameter × post count) + gate post footing (0.6m depth × 0.3m diameter × gate post count); (e) rebar for footings — 2–3 pieces of 12mm rebar per post footing; (f) gate frame — steel tubular frame sized to opening, cross-braced; (g) gate hardware — heavy-duty hinges (2–3 per gate), latch/lock set, drop bolt (for double gates), gate wheel (for sliding gates), guide track and rollers (for sliding gates); (h) paint/finish — primer + 2 coats enamel paint, estimated liters based on total steel surface area; (i) miscellaneous — cement (for CHB mortar), sand, tie wire, welding rods (if customer fabricates on-site), bolts and anchors | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Gate Fabrication Recommendation**: For custom steel gates: (a) system generates gate frame cutting list — top rail, bottom rail, vertical stiles, diagonal braces; (b) if customer has welding capability: provide material list only; (c) if customer needs fabricated gate: offer BuildRight's welding/fabrication service per W988 with 3–5 day lead time; (d) gate design options — flat top, arch top, spear top (decorative), vertical bar, horizontal slat; (e) gate weight estimate for hinge/hardware selection | Sales Associate / System | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 4 | **Cross-Sell Security & Automation Accessories**: Sales Associate recommends: (a) padlock or mortise lock for gate (hardware section); (b) automatic gate operator (sliding or swing) for vehicle gates; (c) solar-powered gate operator (for areas without electrical access to gate); (d) CCTV camera at gate entrance per W207; (e) outdoor lighting (solar flood lights, sensor lights) for fence perimeter; (f) anti-climb devices for high-security applications; (g) paint color matching per W981 for fence/gate aesthetic coordination | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 5 | **Quotation & Order Processing**: Customer reviews complete material list; Sales Associate: (a) presents itemized materials with quantities and pricing; (b) creates POS quotation per W542 valid for 14 days; (c) for large orders (CHB, cement, sand, steel): schedules delivery per W5D or W980 for construction site delivery; (d) offers rebar cutting/bending service per W986 for footing reinforcement; (e) offers welding/fabrication service per W988 for gate fabrication; (f) quotation saved to customer loyalty account per W894; (g) for trade customers: quotation can be converted to project quotation per W162 for bid submission | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Fence/gate estimation calculator module (POS and mobile app) with PH-standard fencing parameters
- Product catalog with fencing materials, steel tubular specifications, and gate hardware compatibility
- POS quotation module (W542) for itemized material list
- POS project quotation (W162) for trade customer bid submissions
- Delivery scheduling (W5D, W980) for heavy materials to construction site
- Rebar cutting/bending service (W986) for footing reinforcement
- Welding/fabrication service (W988) for gate fabrication
- Customer loyalty account integration for quotation saving (W894)
- Real-time inventory availability for steel and construction materials

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Site condition variability**: Customer-described ground conditions frequently differ from actual (hardpan, water table, buried obstructions); Sales Associate must recommend +10% contingency on concrete and footing materials and advise customer to verify site conditions before purchasing full quantity
- **Gate sizing accuracy**: Gate opening measurements must be exact (±5mm) for proper gate fit; customer-provided measurements are often inaccurate; Sales Associate must emphasize precise measurement and recommend professional measurement per W442 for large/expensive gates
- **Structural adequacy**: Fence height, post spacing, and footing depth must be adequate for wind load (critical in typhoon-prone PH); Sales Associate cannot provide structural engineering advice (liability); must recommend consulting a structural engineer for fences >2.4m height or in high-wind zones per NSCP
- **Theft risk on construction site**: Steel and construction materials delivered to site are vulnerable to theft (common in PH construction); advise customer to schedule delivery close to installation date and secure materials on-site
- **Competitive pricing**: Fencing is a commodity market with many local steel suppliers offering lower prices; BuildRight's differentiation is the complete estimation service, gate fabrication, and delivery coordination

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Steel/Hardware Specialist)**: Fence estimations consume ~2–3 hours/day at 17–22 consultations; absorbed by existing Lumber & Building Materials Sales Associate with fencing product certification per W51
- **Training**: 8-hour fence/gate material estimation and steel product knowledge certification per W51
- **No incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Project scope & site intake: 10–15 min
- Material quantity calculation: 5–8 min
- Gate fabrication recommendation: 5–8 min
- Cross-sell accessories: 5–8 min
- Quotation & order processing: 5–10 min
- **Total per estimation**: 30–49 min of staff time

## W988. Store-Level Customer Welding & Custom Metal Fabrication Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests custom metal fabrication or welding service at store |
| **Frequency** | ~2,500–3,500 transactions/month chain-wide (~12–17/store/month) |
| **Volume** | 1–5 pieces per transaction; average 2.3 pieces |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Lumber & Building Materials) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Welder/Fabricator), Customer, Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

Custom metal fabrication is a high-demand service in the Philippine hardware retail market, driven by the prevalence of custom-built residential and commercial construction. Customers frequently need steel gates (per W987), window grills, stair railings, canopy frames, mezzanine frames, shelf brackets, machine guards, and various structural components fabricated to specific dimensions. Unlike standard merchandise, these items are made-to-order and require skilled labor (certified welder), specialized equipment (MIG/TIG welder, angle grinder, cutting torch, bending machine), and raw material inventory (steel tubular, flat bar, angle bar, square bar, steel plate). BuildRight's in-store welding service differentiates it from competitors who sell raw materials only and drives significant incremental revenue through fabrication fees and associated material sales. The service also supports other workflows — W986 (rebar bending), W987 (gate fabrication), and W946 (screen fabrication) — creating an integrated value-added service hub at each store.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Request & Specification Intake**: Customer provides fabrication requirements: (a) item description (gate, window grill, railing, frame, bracket, etc.); (b) dimensions — overall width, height, depth; member sizes and spacing; (c) material type — mild steel round tube (1", 1½", 2"), square tube (1", 1½", 2"), flat bar (⅜", ½", ¾"), angle bar (1", 1¼", 1½"), solid round bar, steel plate; (d) design — customer sketch, photograph of similar item, reference to existing structure, or description; (e) finish — raw steel (customer paints), primer only, primer + paint (BuildRight paints); (f) quantity; (g) any reference drawing or photo | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |
| 2 | **Feasibility Check & Quotation**: Sales Associate confirms: (a) material availability — system checks real-time inventory per store; (b) fabrication complexity — simple (straight cuts, basic welds) vs. moderate (curves, patterns, ornamental) vs. complex (structural load-bearing, multi-component assemblies); (c) equipment capability — MIG welder (up to 6mm mild steel), angle grinder (cutting and finishing), drill press (hole drilling); stores do not perform CNC plasma cutting or heavy structural fabrication (those are referred to external fabricators); (d) estimated fabrication time — simple items: 1–3 hours; moderate: 3–8 hours; complex: 1–3 days; (e) system generates quotation: material cost (raw steel per length/piece) + fabrication fee (per hour or per piece based on complexity) + finish fee (primer/paint per sqm) + consumables (welding wire, gas, grinding discs); quotation valid for 7 days | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 8–12 min |
| 3 | **Order Acceptance & Payment**: Customer accepts quotation; Sales Associate creates service work order (SWO) in POS per W544; customer pays at POS — minimum 50% deposit for fabrication orders (balance on completion); POS prints SWO receipt with: order number, fabrication specifications, material list, promised completion date; system allocates raw material from inventory and creates fabrication job for Welder | Sales Associate / Cashier | Department Supervisor | 5 min |
| 4 | **Fabrication Execution**: Welder/Fabricator retrieves raw material from yard storage per W3B; dons PPE per W140 (welding helmet, leather gloves, leather apron, safety goggles, steel-toe boots); performs fabrication: (a) cutting — measures and marks material per SWO dimensions; cuts using angle grinder with cutting disc or hacksaw for small items; (b) fitting — assembles pieces per design, clamps in position, verifies dimensions; (c) welding — MIG welds all joints with appropriate wire feed speed and voltage settings; 2-pass minimum for structural joints; (d) grinding — grinds weld beads flush where required for aesthetic finish; removes slag and spatter; (e) drilling — drills mounting holes per customer specification; (f) finish application — applies primer (zinc chromate) and/or enamel paint if included; (g) tags finished item with SWO number | Sales Associate (Welder/Fabricator) | Department Supervisor | 1–8 hours (varies by complexity) |
| 5 | **Quality Inspection & Customer Handover**: Welder inspects: (a) dimensional accuracy — ±3mm for overall dimensions; (b) weld quality — full penetration, no porosity, no undercut, no cracks; visual inspection per AWS D1.1 (basic level); (c) finish quality — even primer/paint coverage, no rust, no grinding marks on visible surfaces; (d) structural adequacy — visual check for proper joint design and adequate weld size; failed inspection → rework or re-fabricate; customer inspects finished item and signs acceptance on SWO; customer pays remaining balance; system closes SWO and posts sale; customer loads item at yard loading zone per W438 | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 5–15 min |
| 6 | **Daily Station Cleanup & Safety Compliance**: At end of day: Welder cleans fabrication station; disconnects welding equipment; stores flammable materials (paint, thinner, welding gas) in fire-rated cabinet; cleans grinding dust and metal shavings (non-hazardous metal waste per W82); checks fire extinguisher (CO2 type, mandatory at welding station per BFP requirements per W476); inspects welding cables, ground clamp, and regulator for damage; ventilation check — welding station must have adequate natural or mechanical ventilation per DOLE standards | Sales Associate (Welder/Fabricator) | Department Supervisor | 20 min/day |

### System Touchpoints
- POS service work order module (W544) for order creation, deposit, and balance payment
- Real-time inventory availability for steel raw materials per store
- Inventory allocation and consumption posting with waste factor
- Quotation generation with dynamic pricing (material + fabrication fee + finish)
- Yard inventory management per W3B for outdoor steel storage
- Vehicle loading assistance per W950 at yard loading zone
- Fire safety compliance per W476 (fire extinguisher at welding station)
- PPE compliance tracking per W140

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Welding safety**: Arc welding produces UV radiation (flash burn risk), fumes (metal particulate and gas exposure), fire risk (sparks ignite flammable materials), and electrical hazard; mandatory PPE, fire-rated storage, CO2 fire extinguisher, and proper ventilation per DOLE standards are non-negotiable; Welder must hold valid welding certification per TESDA (Technical Education and Skills Development Authority)
- **Structural liability**: BuildRight provides custom fabrication as a service but does not certify structural adequacy of fabricated items; SWO and quotation must clearly state that fabricated items are "for general purpose use" and that "structural engineering certification is the customer's responsibility for load-bearing applications"; disclaimer reviewed and approved by Legal per W230
- **Lead time variability**: Complex fabrication orders may take 1–3 days; customers accustomed to retail instant gratification may be impatient; Sales Associate must set clear expectations at order intake and provide SMS notification when order is ready
- **Skill dependency**: Welding quality depends on Welder skill level; each store must have at least one TESDA-certified welder; if welder is absent, fabrication service is suspended; cross-training per W51 mitigates but cannot fully substitute for certified welding competency
- **Material waste**: Steel cutting generates 3–8% waste (offcuts); pricing must absorb waste cost within fabrication fee to avoid customer disputes; waste steel sold to recycler per W443

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Welder/Fabricator)**: 1 per store designated as primary Welder with TESDA NC-II Welding certification; fabrication consumes ~4–6 hours/day at 12–17 transactions; absorbed by existing Lumber & Building Materials Sales Associate with welding certification per W51
- **Training**: TESDA NC-II Welding certification (160 hours initial); 16-hour annual refresher per W51; includes MIG welding techniques, blueprint reading, and safety protocols
- **No incremental headcount** (welding equipment capital investment per store: ~PHP 80,000–120,000 for MIG welder, grinder, drill press, and PPE)

### Time Estimate
- Specification intake: 10–15 min
- Feasibility check & quotation: 8–12 min
- Order acceptance & payment: 5 min
- Fabrication execution: 1–8 hours (varies by complexity)
- Quality inspection & handover: 5–15 min
- Daily cleanup: 20 min
- **Total per transaction**: 30–55 min of customer-facing staff time + fabrication time (background)

## W989. Customer Plumbing System Layout Design & Material Takeoff Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer (homeowner, contractor, or plumber) requests plumbing layout design and material takeoff at store |
| **Frequency** | ~2,000–3,000 consultations/month chain-wide (~10–15/store/month) |
| **Volume** | 1 project per consultation; ranges from single-bathroom renovation to full-house plumbing |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Plumbing) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Plumbing Specialist), Customer, Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

Plumbing system design for new construction or renovation is a complex material estimation challenge that goes far beyond simple pipe length calculations. A complete residential plumbing system includes water supply lines (hot and cold), drainage/waste/vent (DWV) lines, fixture connections, water heater installation, and septic tank connection. Philippine plumbing follows the National Plumbing Code of the Philippines (NPCP) which mandates specific pipe sizes, vent configurations, and trap requirements. Customers — especially DIY homeowners and small contractors — frequently underestimate material requirements, leading to multiple store trips and project delays. A professional material takeoff service that generates a complete bill of materials based on the floor plan drives higher-value sales, reduces returns and exchanges, and positions BuildRight as a one-stop shop for plumbing projects. The service integrates with W984 (water tank/pump sizing), W944 (pipe cutting), and W138 (installation service referral) to create a complete plumbing project support ecosystem.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Scope & Floor Plan Intake**: Customer provides: (a) floor plan — hand-drawn sketch, builder's blueprint, or photo of floor plan showing fixture locations (toilet, lavatory, kitchen sink, shower, bathtub, washing machine, water heater, outdoor tap); (b) building type — single-story, two-story, three-story; (c) water source — municipal supply, water tank with pump per W984, deep well; (d) water heater type — tankless (point-of-use), storage tank (central), solar water heater; (e) project type — new construction, renovation (replacing existing plumbing), extension (adding bathroom/kitchen); (f) number of bathrooms, kitchen, laundry area, utility sink; Sales Associate marks fixture locations on system layout tool | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 12–18 min |
| 2 | **Plumbing Layout Design & Pipe Routing**: System generates: (a) water supply layout — main supply line from source (typically 1" PVC or PPR) branching to ¾" lines to bathrooms and kitchen, then ½" branches to individual fixtures; (b) drainage layout — 3" or 4" main drain line from toilets, 2" from showers and sinks, with cleanout access points at code-required intervals; (c) vent layout — main vent stack (2" minimum) through roof, with auxiliary vents per NPCP requirements (within 1.5m trap arm distance); (d) hot water supply routing (if water heater specified) — ½" PPR or CPVC with insulated runs for energy efficiency; (e) fixture connection points — exact locations for shut-off valves, angle stops, P-traps, and supply adapters | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Material Takeoff & Quantity Calculation**: System calculates complete bill of materials: (a) supply pipes — PVC schedule 40 or PPR (PN20), lengths by diameter (½", ¾", 1"); (b) DWV pipes — PVC schedule 40, lengths by diameter (1½", 2", 3", 4"); (c) fittings — elbows (90° and 45°), tees, couplings, reducers, adaptors, by pipe material and diameter; (d) valves — gate valves (main shut-off), angle stops (per fixture), check valves (if water pump per W984); (e) fixtures — toilets (close-coupled or wall-hung), lavatories, kitchen sinks, shower sets (per W997 compatibility check); (f) water heater and accessories per customer selection; (g) drain components — P-traps, sanitary tees, cleanouts, closet flanges; (h) sealants — solvent cement (PVC), Teflon tape, plumber's putty, silicone sealant; (i) support/hangers — pipe clamps, brackets, stud anchors; (j) insulation — foam pipe insulation for hot water lines; (k) septic tank connection pipe and fittings (per W998 if new construction) | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Code Compliance Review & Recommendations**: Sales Associate reviews: (a) NPCP compliance — vent stack requirements, trap arm distances, pipe sizing adequacy, cleanout placement; (b) recommends upgrades — PPR over PVC for hot water lines (higher temperature rating), water hammer arrestors for washing machine/dishwasher connections, accessible shut-off valves for maintenance, backflow preventer if connected to municipal supply; (c) for multi-story buildings — pressure reducing valve may be needed for upper floors, booster pump per W984 for insufficient municipal pressure; (d) advises customer that plumbing layout is a material estimation aid, not a stamped engineering drawing; recommends licensed plumber for installation per W138 | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 5 | **Quotation & Order Processing**: Customer reviews complete material list with pricing; Sales Associate: (a) presents itemized materials grouped by category (supply, DWV, fixtures, accessories); (b) offers pipe cutting service per W944 for custom-length PVC/PPR pipes; (c) offers fixture compatibility check per W997 to ensure all bathroom/kitchen fixtures work together; (d) offers water tank/pump sizing per W984 if customer needs storage/distribution system; (e) creates POS quotation per W542 valid for 14 days; (f) for large orders: schedules delivery per W5D for heavy/bulky items; (g) quotation saved to customer loyalty account per W894 | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Plumbing layout design tool (POS and mobile app) with drag-and-drop fixture placement
- Material takeoff engine with NPCP-compliant pipe sizing and fitting count logic
- Product catalog with plumbing fixture specifications and compatibility matrix
- POS quotation module (W542) for itemized bill of materials
- Pipe cutting service integration (W944) for custom pipe lengths
- Fixture compatibility checker (W997) for bathroom/kitchen bundles
- Water tank/pump sizing integration (W984) for water distribution systems
- Customer loyalty account integration for quotation saving (W894)
- Real-time inventory availability for plumbing materials

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Design accuracy**: The system-generated layout is an estimation tool, not a replacement for a professional plumber's as-built layout; wall chases, slab penetrations, and existing pipe routing may differ from assumed paths; Sales Associate must clearly communicate that quantities are estimates and recommend purchasing 5–10% contingency on pipes and fittings
- **Code compliance disclaimer**: BuildRight is not providing professional plumbing engineering services; the material takeoff is a customer convenience and must not be represented as code-compliant design; licensed plumber sign-off is required for building permit applications per LGU requirements per W54
- **Material substitution**: If specific brands or models are out of stock, Sales Associate must recommend equivalent alternatives with matching specifications (pipe diameter, pressure rating, temperature rating); substitution without proper specification matching can cause installation failures
- **Return volume**: Plumbing projects generate higher return rates than typical merchandise due to estimation overages and design changes; clear return policy communication (30-day return for unused PVC/PPR pipes and fittings per W12) and accurate estimation reduce return friction

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Plumbing Specialist)**: Plumbing consultations consume ~2–3 hours/day at 10–15 consultations; absorbed by existing Plumbing Department Sales Associate with plumbing product certification per W51
- **Training**: 16-hour plumbing system design and NPCP basics certification per W51; includes pipe sizing, fixture specification, and material takeoff techniques
- **No incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Project scope & floor plan intake: 12–18 min
- Layout design & pipe routing: 5–10 min
- Material takeoff & quantity calculation: 3–5 min
- Code compliance review: 5–10 min
- Quotation & order processing: 5–10 min
- **Total per consultation**: 30–53 min of staff time

## W990. Customer Solar Panel System Sizing & ROI Calculator Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer inquires about solar panel system at store or via mobile app |
| **Frequency** | ~1,500–2,500 consultations/month chain-wide (~7–12/store/month); growing 30–40% annually |
| **Volume** | 1 system per consultation |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Electrical) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Electrical Specialist), Customer, Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

The Philippines has among the highest residential electricity rates in Southeast Asia (PHP 9–12/kWh average, higher than Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia), making solar energy increasingly attractive for homeowners and businesses. The Net Metering program under the Renewable Energy Act (RA 9513) allows grid-tied solar systems to export excess energy back to the utility (Meralco, VECO, Davao Light, etc.) at a feed-in tariff, effectively spinning the meter backward. However, solar system sizing is complex — it requires analyzing the customer's electricity consumption, roof orientation and shading, available mounting area, local solar irradiance (averaging 4.5–5.5 kWh/m²/day in the Philippines), and financial parameters (system cost, electricity rate trajectory, payback period, ROI). BuildRight sells solar panels (mono/poly-crystalline, 400W–550W), inverters (string and micro-inverter), mounting structures, batteries (optional for hybrid systems), and electrical accessories. This consultation service drives high-value sales (residential systems average PHP 80,000–300,000) and positions BuildRight as a solar energy partner rather than just a component supplier.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Energy Consumption Assessment**: Sales Associate collects: (a) average monthly electricity bill (PHP and kWh) — from customer's utility bill; (b) peak monthly consumption (typically March–May due to aircon usage per W985); (c) electricity rate per kWh from utility; (d) roof type — metal GI sheet (most common in PH, easiest mounting), concrete slab, clay tile; (e) roof orientation — north-facing, south-facing (optimal in PH), east/west-facing, flat; (f) available roof area (sqm) — unshaded area between 9AM–3PM; (g) roof condition and structural adequacy for panel weight (~15 kg/m²); (h) building type — single-story residential, multi-story, commercial; (i) 3-phase or single-phase electrical supply | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |
| 2 | **System Sizing Calculation**: System calculates: (a) system size (kWp) = monthly consumption (kWh) ÷ 30 days ÷ peak sun hours (4.5 for PH) ÷ system efficiency (0.75–0.80 derating factor for temperature, inverter, wiring losses); example: 500 kWh/month → 500 ÷ 30 ÷ 4.5 ÷ 0.77 ≈ 4.8 kWp system; (b) number of panels = system size ÷ panel wattage (500W panels: 4,800W ÷ 500W ≈ 10 panels); (c) required roof area = panels × panel area (2.0m² per 500W panel) = 20 sqm minimum; (d) inverter size = system size × 1.0–1.2 (slight oversizing for peak production); (e) annual energy production = system size × peak sun hours × 365 × derating = estimated kWh/year; (f) self-consumption ratio — estimated % of solar energy consumed directly vs. exported to grid; (g) battery sizing (optional hybrid system) = critical loads × desired backup hours | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Financial ROI Analysis**: System calculates: (a) total system cost = panels + inverter + mounting structure + electrical accessories + installation labor (per W138); (b) annual savings = annual production × self-consumption ratio × electricity rate + annual export × feed-in tariff; (c) simple payback period = total cost ÷ annual savings (typical PH residential: 4–6 years); (d) 25-year net savings = annual savings × 25 years × electricity rate escalation (3–5%/year assumed) − total cost − maintenance costs (inverter replacement at year 10–12); (e) internal rate of return (IRR); (f) comparison table: cash purchase vs. bank financing (partner bank per W966) with monthly amortization vs. monthly savings; (g) environmental impact — CO₂ avoided = annual production × 0.6 kg CO₂/kWh (PH grid emission factor) | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Product Selection & Quotation**: Sales Associate presents: (a) system components — panels (Tier 1 brand recommendation), inverter (string inverter for simple roofs, micro-inverter for complex/shaded roofs), mounting kit, AC/DC disconnect, circuit breaker, cables and connectors; (b) optional battery bank for hybrid/off-grid capability; (c) total system cost with itemized pricing; (d) installation service referral per W138 with certified solar installer; (e) net metering application assistance — advise customer on utility net metering application process (BuildRight provides checklist and required technical documents but does not file the application); (f) LGU electrical permit requirements per W54; (g) creates POS quotation per W542 valid for 30 days (solar equipment pricing is relatively stable) | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 8–12 min |
| 5 | **Documentation & Follow-Up**: For customers who proceed: (a) system generates technical summary document with system specifications, layout diagram, and ROI analysis for customer's records; (b) Sales Associate schedules site assessment per W442 (technical survey for roof condition, shading analysis, and electrical panel compatibility) before final installation commitment; (c) quotation saved to customer loyalty account per W894; (d) system registers follow-up task for Sales Associate to contact customer in 7 days if quotation not converted to sale; (e) for net metering customers: provides utility application checklist and list of required documents | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Solar system sizing calculator module (POS and mobile app) with PH-specific solar irradiance data
- Financial ROI analysis engine with configurable electricity rate and escalation parameters
- Product catalog with solar panel, inverter, and battery specifications and compatibility matrix
- POS quotation module (W542) for itemized system cost
- Site assessment scheduling per W442
- Installation service referral per W138 with certified solar installer
- Construction loan referral per W966 for financing option
- Customer loyalty account integration for quotation saving (W894)
- LGU permit guidance per W54

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Roof structural adequacy**: Solar panels add ~15 kg/m² to the roof; older PH residential roofs (especially those with lightweight trusses) may not support the additional load without reinforcement; site assessment per W442 is mandatory before installation commitment; structural engineer referral recommended for roofs >10 years old
- **Shading losses**: Even partial shading of one panel can significantly reduce string inverter system output; micro-inverter systems mitigate but increase cost; accurate shading analysis during site assessment is critical for setting realistic production expectations
- **Utility interconnection delays**: Net metering applications with Meralco and other utilities can take 30–90 days for approval and meter installation; customers must be informed that savings only begin after interconnection is complete; BuildRight cannot control utility timelines
- **After-sales support**: Solar systems are 25-year investments; customers expect ongoing support for warranty claims per W33, inverter replacements, and system monitoring; BuildRight must maintain qualified solar service partner network per W213
- **Regulatory changes**: The Renewable Energy Act and net metering rules may evolve; ERC (Energy Regulatory Commission) and DOE regulations may affect feed-in tariffs and interconnection requirements; Category Manager must monitor regulatory environment per W114

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Electrical Specialist)**: Solar consultations consume ~1.5–2.5 hours/day at 7–12 consultations; absorbed by existing Electrical Department Sales Associate with solar product certification per W51
- **Training**: 24-hour solar system design and sales certification per W51; includes solar PV fundamentals, PH net metering regulations, ROI calculation, and sales techniques
- **No incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Energy consumption assessment: 10–15 min
- System sizing calculation: 5–8 min
- Financial ROI analysis: 3–5 min
- Product selection & quotation: 8–12 min
- Documentation & follow-up: 5–8 min
- **Total per consultation**: 31–48 min of staff time

## W991. Customer Electrical Circuit Design & Residential Load Planning Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests electrical circuit planning assistance for new construction or renovation |
| **Frequency** | ~2,000–3,000 consultations/month chain-wide (~10–15/store/month) |
| **Volume** | 1 project per consultation |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Electrical) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Electrical Specialist), Customer, Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

Electrical wiring is a core category for BuildRight Depot, with copper wire, circuit breakers, panels, switches, and outlets representing a significant revenue segment. Philippine residential electrical design follows the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), which mandates specific circuit configurations, wire sizing, grounding requirements, and safety devices. Typical PH residential construction requires 6–12 dedicated circuits (lighting, convenience outlets, aircon, kitchen, water heater, etc.) with proper wire sizing (THHN/THWN copper wire in EMT conduit or PVC modular). Customers — especially DIY homeowners and small contractors — frequently underestimate wire lengths, forget accessories (junction boxes, connectors, ground rods), or select incorrect wire gauge (a fire hazard). A professional circuit design and material takeoff service increases safety, drives complete-circuit sales (rather than piecemeal purchases), and reduces return trips. The service integrates with W985 (aircon sizing) for aircon circuit requirements and W990 (solar panel system) for solar interconnection.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Building Assessment & Load Inventory**: Sales Associate collects: (a) floor plan with room layout (hand-drawn or photo); (b) number of rooms and room types (bedrooms, living room, kitchen, bathrooms, garage, laundry); (c) planned appliances and equipment per room — aircon (per W985 with HP rating), water heater, electric stove/induction cooker, refrigerator, washing machine, microwave, water pump (per W984 with HP rating), lighting fixtures, number of convenience outlets per room; (d) building type — single-story, two-story; (e) service entrance — overhead or underground, existing panel amperage (typically 60A or 100A for PH residential); (f) project type — new construction, renovation, extension | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |
| 2 | **Circuit Design & Load Calculation**: System designs circuits per PEC guidelines: (a) lighting circuits — 1 circuit per 800W of lighting load, 2.0mm² THHN wire (minimum), 15A circuit breaker; (b) convenience outlet circuits — 1 circuit per 6 outlets maximum, 2.0mm² THHN wire, 20A circuit breaker, GFCI protection for wet areas (bathrooms, kitchen, outdoor); (c) dedicated appliance circuits — aircon: 1 circuit per unit, 3.5mm² THHN for 1HP, 5.5mm² THHN for 2HP, 30A circuit breaker; water heater: dedicated circuit, 3.5mm² THHN, 30A circuit breaker; electric stove: dedicated circuit, 8.0mm² THHN, 40–50A circuit breaker; water pump: dedicated circuit per W984 pump HP rating; (d) total connected load (watts) and computed load per PEC demand factors; (e) main breaker and panel size recommendation — 100A panel for standard residential, 200A for large residential with multiple aircon units; (f) service entrance wire size — based on computed load and distance from utility meter | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Material Takeoff & Quantity Calculation**: System generates complete bill of materials: (a) wire — THHN/THWN copper wire by gauge (2.0mm², 3.5mm², 5.5mm², 8.0mm²) with estimated lengths per circuit × 1.15 waste factor; (b) circuit breakers — quantity and amperage per circuit design, including main breaker; (c) panel board — load center with sufficient breaker slots; (d) conduit — PVC conduit or EMT by diameter with fittings; (e) junction boxes — quantity by type (round, square, octagonal); (f) switches — single-pole, 3-way, 4-way by quantity per room; (g) outlets/convenience outlets — standard, GFCI (wet areas), grounded, by quantity; (h) connectors and accessories — wire nuts, cable ties, ground rod, ground wire, terminal lugs, EMT connectors, PVC cement, electrical tape; (i) safety devices — surge protector, AFCI breakers (recommended for bedrooms); (j) lighting fixtures — quantity per room (if customer selects) | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Code Compliance Review & Safety Recommendations**: Sales Associate reviews: (a) PEC compliance — circuit breaker sizing, wire gauge adequacy, grounding requirements (8ft ground rod mandatory per PEC), GFCI placement in wet areas; (b) recommends safety upgrades — whole-house surge protector (critical in typhoon-prone PH with frequent lightning), AFCI breakers for bedrooms (arc fault protection), smoke detectors per floor, CO detector if gas appliances present; (c) advises customer that material list is a planning aid, not a professional electrical engineering design; recommends licensed electrician for installation per W138 and PEC compliance certification; (d) for renovation projects: advises on aluminum-to-copper transition safety and knob-and-tube wiring hazards (common in older PH homes) | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 5 | **Quotation & Order Processing**: Customer reviews complete material list; Sales Associate: (a) presents itemized materials grouped by circuit; (b) offers wire cutting service for custom-length wire runs; (c) offers lighting fixture selection per W997 for bathroom/kitchen fixture coordination; (d) creates POS quotation per W542 valid for 14 days; (e) for large orders (full-house rewiring): schedules delivery per W5D for heavy items (panel, conduit, wire rolls); (f) quotation saved to customer loyalty account per W894 | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Electrical circuit design tool (POS and mobile app) with PEC-compliant circuit sizing engine
- Material takeoff engine with wire length estimation and conduit routing logic
- Product catalog with electrical material specifications and compatibility matrix
- Aircon circuit requirement integration per W985
- Water pump circuit requirement integration per W984
- Solar interconnection integration per W990
- POS quotation module (W542) for itemized bill of materials
- Customer loyalty account integration for quotation saving (W894)
- Real-time inventory availability for electrical materials

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Fire safety liability**: Incorrect wire gauge or circuit breaker sizing creates fire hazard; Sales Associate must clearly communicate that material recommendations are based on standard PEC guidelines and that a licensed electrician must verify and approve all installations; disclaimer approved by Legal per W230
- **Concealed wiring estimation**: Wire length estimates are based on straight-line routing with 15% waste factor; actual wire runs through walls, ceilings, and conduit bends may differ significantly; customer must understand that wire lengths are estimates and additional wire may be needed during installation
- **Aluminum vs. copper**: Some older PH homes have aluminum wiring; mixing aluminum and copper (without proper CO/ALR connectors) creates connection failure risk; Sales Associate must ask about existing wire material and recommend proper transition connectors
- **Utility coordination**: Service entrance upgrades (from 60A to 100A or 200A panel) require coordination with the utility provider (Meralco, VECO, etc.); customer must file a service upgrade request with the utility; BuildRight provides materials only

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Electrical Specialist)**: Electrical consultations consume ~2–3 hours/day at 10–15 consultations; absorbed by existing Electrical Department Sales Associate with electrical product certification per W51
- **Training**: 12-hour residential electrical design and PEC basics certification per W51; includes circuit sizing, wire gauge selection, and safety device recommendations
- **No incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Building assessment & load inventory: 10–15 min
- Circuit design & load calculation: 5–10 min
- Material takeoff & quantity calculation: 3–5 min
- Code compliance review: 5–10 min
- Quotation & order processing: 5–10 min
- **Total per consultation**: 28–50 min of staff time

## W992. Customer Garden & Landscape Design Consultation & Material Estimation Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests garden/landscape design assistance at store garden section or via mobile app |
| **Frequency** | ~2,000–3,000 consultations/month chain-wide (~10–15/store/month); peaks March–May (PH summer) |
| **Volume** | 1 project per consultation |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Garden & Outdoor) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Garden Specialist), Customer, Category Manager (pricing) |

### Background

The Garden & Outdoor category, while representing only 3% of active SKUs (~1,050 items), is a high-growth segment with strong cross-sell potential to higher-margin categories (pavers, outdoor lighting, irrigation, furniture, paint). Philippine residential garden projects range from simple container gardening on balconies (condominium dwellers) to full landscape design with hardscaping (pavers, retaining walls, water features) and softscaping (plants, trees, turf, ground cover). The tropical Philippine climate is ideal for year-round gardening, but also presents challenges — intense monsoon rains, typhoons, and high humidity affect plant selection and drainage design. Customers typically underestimate the scope of a landscaping project (drainage, soil preparation, irrigation) and the total material cost. A professional design consultation with material estimation drives larger, more complete purchases and differentiates BuildRight from standalone garden centers (which are rare in provincial PH).

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Scope & Site Assessment**: Customer provides: (a) garden area dimensions (length × width in meters); (b) current condition — bare soil, lawn, existing plants, concrete/paved; (c) sun exposure — full sun (6+ hours), partial shade (3–6 hours), full shade (<3 hours); (d) soil type — clay (common in PH), sandy, loam, rocky (customer observation or soil test kit); (e) drainage — standing water after rain, good drainage, sloped; (f) project type — new garden, garden renovation, container/balcony garden, vegetable garden, ornamental garden, xeriscaping (drought-resistant); (g) budget range; (h) maintenance commitment — low (weekend gardener), medium, high (daily attention); (i) existing structures — pergola, fence per W987, walkway, patio | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |
| 2 | **Garden Design & Plant Selection**: Sales Associate designs: (a) functional zones — patio/seating area, planting beds, walkway, lawn area, vegetable patch, utility area (compost, hose storage); (b) hardscape plan — paver type (concrete pavers, natural stone, permeable pavers), walkway width (0.9–1.2m), edging material, retaining wall (if slope requires); (c) softscape plan — plant selection based on PH hardiness, sun exposure, and maintenance level: shade trees (narra, acacia, fire tree), ornamental shrubs (bougainvillea, ixora, santan), ground cover (carabao grass, Korean grass), flowering plants (gumamela, sampaguita, orchids), vegetables (tomato, chili, pechay, okra); (d) irrigation plan — drip irrigation system (water-efficient), sprinkler heads, timer/controller, rain sensor; (e) drainage plan — French drain or surface drainage to prevent standing water during monsoon | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |
| 3 | **Material Takeoff & Quantity Calculation**: System calculates: (a) hardscape materials — pavers (area ÷ paver coverage + 5% waste), edging (linear meters), base material (gravel/sand per sqm depth), polymeric sand (for joints), retaining wall blocks (if applicable); (b) soil amendments — garden soil (cubic meters based on bed area × 0.15m depth), compost/organic matter, fertilizer (NPK ratio based on plant selection); (c) plants — quantity based on spacing requirements per species; (d) irrigation — drip line length, emitter quantity, connector fittings, timer, filter, pressure regulator; (e) landscape fabric (sqm for weed barrier under pavers and planting beds); (f) mulch (cubic meters based on bed area × 0.05m depth); (g) accessories — garden hose, hose reel, sprinkler, pruning shears, gloves, pots and planters (for container garden) | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Cross-Sell Outdoor Living Products**: Sales Associate recommends: (a) outdoor lighting — solar path lights, garden spotlights, string lights; (b) outdoor furniture — garden bench, dining set, lounge chairs; (c) water feature — fountain kit, small pond liner, water pump per W984; (d) pest control — organic insecticide, snail bait, mosquito control; (e) garden tools — shovel, rake, trowel, wheelbarrow, pruning saw; (f) vertical garden system (for small spaces/condominiums); (g) shade structure — pergola kit, shade sail, umbrella | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 5 | **Quotation & Order Processing**: Customer reviews design and material list; Sales Associate: (a) presents itemized materials grouped by category (hardscape, softscape, irrigation, accessories); (b) creates POS quotation per W542 valid for 14 days; (c) for hardscape materials (pavers, gravel, sand): schedules delivery per W5D; (d) offers garden installation service referral per W138 (landscaping contractor); (e) offers fencing service per W987 if garden boundary fencing needed; (f) quotation saved to customer loyalty account per W894; (g) provides seasonal planting calendar specific to customer's PH region | Sales Associate / Customer | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Garden design tool (POS and mobile app) with drag-and-drop zone layout
- Plant database with PH hardiness zones, sun requirements, spacing, and mature size
- Material takeoff engine with hardscape and softscape quantity calculations
- Product catalog with garden/outdoor product specifications
- POS quotation module (W542) for itemized material list
- Delivery scheduling (W5D) for heavy hardscape materials
- Installation service referral (W138) for landscaping
- Customer loyalty account integration for quotation saving (W894)
- Seasonal planting calendar per PH region

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Plant survival guarantee**: BuildRight does not guarantee plant survival after purchase; plants are living products affected by customer care, weather, soil conditions, and pest damage; Sales Associate must provide care instructions and recommend appropriate soil amendments and fertilizers; returns only accepted within 7 days for plants that arrive damaged from transport
- **Seasonal plant availability**: Tropical plants have varying availability throughout the year; specific species may be out of stock; Sales Associate must offer equivalent alternatives and explain seasonal planting windows
- **Drainage issues**: Poor drainage is the #1 cause of garden project failure in PH (monsoon flooding kills plants and damages hardscape); drainage assessment must be thorough in Step 1; French drain or surface drainage must be included in material list if any standing water risk exists
- **Scope creep**: Garden projects tend to expand as customers see the full material list; Sales Associate must anchor to customer's stated budget and offer phased implementation (Phase 1: hardscape and irrigation; Phase 2: planting and finishing) to avoid sticker shock

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Garden Specialist)**: Garden consultations consume ~1.5–2.5 hours/day at 10–15 consultations; absorbed by existing Garden & Outdoor Department Sales Associate with garden product certification per W51
- **Training**: 8-hour garden design and PH plant knowledge certification per W51; includes tropical plant selection, hardscape basics, and irrigation design
- **No incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Project scope & site assessment: 10–15 min
- Garden design & plant selection: 10–15 min
- Material takeoff & quantity calculation: 5–8 min
- Cross-sell outdoor living products: 5–8 min
- Quotation & order processing: 5–10 min
- **Total per consultation**: 35–56 min of staff time
