## W1018. Customer Project Progress Payment Verification & Invoice Matching

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Project milestone completion triggers progress billing per project contract terms |
| **Frequency** | ~300–500 progress billing events/month across all active B2B projects |
| **Volume** | 1–3 milestone invoices per project per month; ~150–200 active projects at any time |
| **Owner** | Project Account Manager |
| **Participants** | Project Coordinator, Delivery Supervisor, Customer Project Manager, AR Analyst, Credit Manager |

### Background

BuildRight Depot's project-based B2B sales (W162–W166) involve staged deliveries and progress billing for large construction and renovation projects. A typical corporate project: (a) contract signed for PHP 5–50M in materials over 3–12 months; (b) materials delivered in phases aligned with construction milestones (foundation, structural, finishing); (c) billing tied to delivery milestones with progress payment terms (e.g., 30% on contract signing, 30% at structural completion, 30% at finishing, 10% retention payable 90 days after project completion per W165). Each progress billing must be matched against: delivered quantities (GR per project site), contracted prices (project price book per W163), and any approved change orders (W792). Verification is critical because: (a) billing ahead of delivery violates PFRS 15 revenue recognition (revenue must be earned before recognized); (b) billing below delivery value creates cash flow pressure; (c) mismatched billing causes customer disputes and delayed payment. Philippine B2B projects frequently experience scope changes, quantity adjustments, and delivery discrepancies — this workflow ensures accurate, timely billing that maintains customer trust and protects BuildRight's revenue.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Milestone Delivery Verification**: Project Coordinator confirms milestone delivery completion: (a) all scheduled deliveries for the milestone period have been completed per W164 (Staged Project Delivery); (b) delivery receipts signed by customer's project representative at each site; (c) Goods Receipt confirmed in system per delivery; (d) any delivery discrepancies (short quantities, damaged items) resolved per W500 (Transfer Order In-Transit Damage); (e) change orders (W792) executed during the milestone period are completed and signed off by customer; (f) Project Coordinator certifies milestone delivery completion with supporting documentation | Project Coordinator | Project Account Manager | 30–60 min per milestone |
| 2 | **Progress Invoice Generation**: AR Analyst generates progress invoice: (a) system aggregates all GR-confirmed deliveries for the milestone period; (b) quantities matched against project contract price book (W163) — unit prices, applicable discounts, and terms; (c) change order items priced per approved change order (W792) — including margin re-impact assessment; (d) retained amounts per contract terms (e.g., 10% retention) deducted from current billing and tracked separately; (e) VAT computed per BIR requirements (12% output VAT on taxable items); (f) invoice generated: itemized by material category with delivery dates, quantities, unit prices, and totals; (g) BIR-registered sales invoice per DOC-002 with project reference and milestone number | AR Analyst / System | Project Account Manager | 20–40 min per invoice |
| 3 | **Internal Three-Way Verification**: Before sending to customer: (a) AR Analyst performs three-way match: **Contract Price Book** × **Actual Deliveries (GR)** × **Progress Invoice**; (b) verify: all delivered items are invoiced (no unbilled deliveries), all invoiced items were delivered (no unbilled delivery), quantities match (no quantity discrepancy), prices match contract (no pricing errors); (c) flag exceptions: items delivered but not in contract (change order items — verify approved), items in contract but not yet delivered (backorder — do not bill); (d) Project Account Manager reviews and approves invoice; (e) Credit Manager verifies total outstanding exposure remains within approved credit limit per W572 | AR Analyst / Project Account Manager | Credit Manager | 15–30 min per invoice |
| 4 | **Customer Invoice Presentation & Dispute Resolution**: (a) invoice delivered to customer Project Manager with supporting delivery receipts and GR documentation; (b) customer reviews against their own project records; (c) if customer disputes: handled per W1022 (Trade Account Statement Dispute); (d) common disputes: quantity discrepancy (customer says they received less than invoiced), quality issue (customer claims damaged items should not be billed), price dispute (customer claims agreed price differs from invoiced); (e) AR Analyst investigates with Project Coordinator: delivery documentation, site photos, GR sign-off; (f) if dispute valid: credit memo issued per W101; if dispute rejected: provide evidence to customer; (g) SLA: dispute resolution within 10 business days | AR Analyst / Project Account Manager | Credit Manager | 15–60 min per dispute |
| 5 | **Payment Collection & Retention Management**: (a) customer pays progress invoice per contract terms (typically Net 30 from invoice date); (b) payment collected per W108 (AR & Collections); (c) retention amounts tracked in separate retention receivable account; (d) retention released per contract terms (typically 90 days after project completion and sign-off per W793); (e) final retention release triggers: project completion certificate from customer, no outstanding claims or disputes, all warranties registered per W1016; (f) project margin analysis: actual revenue vs. contract value, actual COGS, gross margin %, margin impact of change orders per W918 | AR Analyst / Credit Manager | Credit Manager | 10–20 min per payment |

### System Touchpoints
- Project management module with milestone tracking (W162–W166)
- Delivery receipt and GR system with project tagging
- Contract price book module (W163)
- Change order management (W792) with margin impact tracking
- Progress billing module with automated invoice generation
- Three-way match engine (contract × delivery × invoice)
- Credit limit monitoring (W572, W888)
- AR aging and collection system (W108, W889)
- Retention receivable tracking with automated release scheduling
- BIR-compliant sales invoice generation (DOC-002)
- Project profitability analytics (W918)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Billing lag**: Manual milestone verification and invoice generation can take 5–10 business days after milestone completion, delaying cash collection; system automation of invoice generation (step 2) reduces billing cycle to 2–3 days
- **PFRS 15 revenue recognition**: Progress billing must be matched to actual delivery completion per PFRS 15; billing ahead of delivery (common in Philippine construction practice where "down payments" are requested) must be recorded as customer deposit (W94) and not recognized as revenue until delivery occurs
- **Retention collection risk**: 10% retention across 150–200 active projects represents PHP 50–100M in outstanding retention receivables; retention is at risk if customer disputes project quality or becomes insolvent before retention release; Credit Manager should monitor retention aging and escalate overdue retention per W108
- **Scope creep and unbilled work**: Change orders executed verbally without formal documentation per W792 lead to unbilled work; Project Coordinator must document all scope changes before execution and obtain customer sign-off before delivery

### Staffing Implication
- **AR Analyst**: Progress billing adds ~20–40 min per invoice; at ~300–500 invoices/month, this is ~100–330 hours/month; distributed across AR team
- **Project Account Manager**: Verification and approval adds ~15–30 min per invoice
- **No incremental headcount** (absorbed by existing Finance & Accounting team of 37 staff)

### Time Estimate
- Delivery verification: 30–60 min per milestone
- Invoice generation: 20–40 min per invoice
- Internal verification: 15–30 min per invoice
- Customer presentation: 15–60 min per dispute
- Payment collection: 10–20 min per payment
- **Total per progress billing event**: 90–210 min

## W1027. Customer AI-Powered Chatbot & Virtual Shopping Assistant Operations

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer initiates chat on buildright.com.ph, mobile app, or social media messenger (Facebook Messenger, Viber) |
| **Frequency** | ~60,000–80,000 chatbot interactions/month (~2,000–2,600/day) |
| **Volume** | 1 session per interaction; ~40% resolve without human agent |
| **Owner** | Ecommerce Operations Manager |
| **Participants** | Customer, AI Chatbot (system), Human Agent (escalation), Product Content Manager, IT AI/ML Engineer |

### Background

BuildRight Depot's digital channels serve ~42,900 ecommerce orders/month plus ~200,000+ website/app visitors browsing the 35,000 SKU catalog. Customer inquiries span product availability ("Is Makita HR2470 hammer drill available at Davao Buhangin branch?"), pricing ("How much is Wilcon 4×8 plywood?"), product comparison ("Bosch vs DeWalt angle grinder for concrete cutting?"), order status ("Where is my order #BR20260608-1234?"), and technical questions ("What size circuit breaker for 1.5HP aircon?"). The call center (30 agents) and customer service email handle ~15,000–20,000 inquiries/month (W259), with average handle time of 5–8 minutes per inquiry. An AI-powered chatbot trained on BuildRight's product catalog, store inventory, pricing, and order data can resolve 35–45% of inquiries without human agent involvement, reducing call center volume by ~6,000–8,000 interactions/month and providing 24/7 self-service support (critical for Filipino customers who browse and chat late evening, 8PM–12AM peak). This workflow manages the chatbot operations, content training, escalation to human agents, and continuous improvement. This is distinct from W200 (AI personalization engine) and W735 (customer onboarding journey); it focuses on conversational AI customer support.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Inquiry Intake & Intent Classification**: Customer initiates chat via any channel: (a) buildright.com.ph chat widget, (b) BuildRight mobile app, (c) Facebook Messenger, (d) Viber; (e) system identifies customer (if logged in via loyalty account) with purchase history, store preference, and active orders; (f) AI chatbot processes customer message using natural language understanding (NLU): classifies intent into one of ~25 predefined categories: product_availability, price_inquiry, product_comparison, order_status, delivery_tracking, return_refund, installation_inquiry, store_location_hours, loyalty_points, payment_issue, technical_specification, project_advice, bulk_order, trade_account, complaint, promotion_inquiry, and others; (g) for multi-intent messages ("Is the Bosch drill available and how does it compare to DeWalt?"), system decomposes into sequential sub-intents | System (AI Chatbot) | Ecommerce Operations Manager | < 5 sec (automated) |
| 2 | **Automated Response & Self-Service Resolution**: Based on classified intent: (a) **Product availability**: chatbot queries real-time store inventory (customer's nearest store from profile or asked); responds with availability, quantity on hand, and aisle location (e.g., "The Bosch GSB 550 Impact Drill is available at BuildRight Davao Buhangin — 7 units in stock, Aisle 4, Power Tools section. Want me to reserve one for pickup?"); (b) **Price inquiry**: responds with current SRP, any active promotions, trade price (if trade account), and competitor price match eligibility per W61; (c) **Product comparison**: generates side-by-side comparison card with specifications, price, customer ratings, and recommendation based on customer's stated use case; (d) **Order status/delivery tracking**: retrieves order from system, provides current status and estimated delivery date per W592; (e) **Technical specification**: responds with product specs from PIM (W50) including dimensions, weight, power requirements, compatible accessories; (f) **Store location/hours**: responds with store address, operating hours, phone number, and Google Maps link; (g) system attempts to resolve within 3 conversational turns; if resolved, customer rates interaction (1–5 stars) and session ends | System (AI Chatbot) | Ecommerce Operations Manager | 1–3 min (customer interaction) |
| 3 | **Human Agent Escalation**: If chatbot cannot resolve within 3 turns, or customer requests human agent, or intent is flagged as high-complexity (complaint, trade account application, project pricing): (a) system transfers chat to available human agent with full conversation history and customer context; (b) customer sees "Connecting you to a BuildRight team member..." message; (c) target transfer time: < 30 seconds during operating hours (8AM–10PM); outside hours, system offers callback or email ticket creation per W258; (d) human agent resolves per existing workflows: complaints (W41), credit application (W886), delivery issue (W1004), product question (W112); (e) upon resolution, agent tags conversation for chatbot training: "resolved by human" with intent category and resolution method — feeds step 5 | Human Agent | Customer Service Supervisor | 5–15 min per escalation |
| 4 | **Product Content & Knowledge Base Maintenance**: Product Content Manager maintains chatbot knowledge base: (a) weekly: review new product launches (W564) and update product database with specifications, comparison data, FAQs, and recommended use cases; (b) weekly: review and update promotional information, pricing changes, and store-level inventory availability logic; (c) monthly: review chatbot response accuracy metrics and identify knowledge gaps (topics where chatbot frequently escalates to human); (d) quarterly: comprehensive knowledge base audit — verify product specifications, pricing, and availability data are current; update product comparison matrices for top 500 SKUs; (e) coordinate with Category Managers for technical product training content per W920 | Product Content Manager | Ecommerce Operations Manager | 4–6 hours/week |
| 5 | **AI Model Performance Monitoring & Continuous Improvement**: IT AI/ML Engineer monitors chatbot performance: (a) daily: review escalation rate (target: < 60%), customer satisfaction score (target: ≥ 4.0/5.0), and average session duration; (b) weekly: review intent classification accuracy — analyze misclassified conversations and retrain NLU model; (c) monthly: analyze "unresolved" conversations to identify new intent categories needed; expand response library; (d) quarterly: A/B test new response templates, product recommendation strategies, and conversation flows; (e) key metrics dashboard: resolution rate, escalation rate, average handle time (chatbot vs. human), customer satisfaction, cost per interaction (chatbot: ~PHP 5–10 vs. human agent: ~PHP 80–120) | IT AI/ML Engineer | Ecommerce Operations Manager | 8–12 hours/week |

### System Touchpoints
- AI chatbot platform integrated with: NLU engine, product catalog (PIM/W50), real-time inventory system, pricing engine, order management system, delivery tracking API (W592), loyalty system
- Omnichannel messaging integration: web chat widget, mobile app SDK, Facebook Messenger API, Viber API
- Human agent handoff module with conversation history and customer context transfer
- Customer satisfaction rating system (in-chat, 1–5 stars + optional comment)
- Knowledge base / content management system for product data, FAQs, and response templates
- Analytics dashboard: resolution rate, escalation rate, intent distribution, customer satisfaction, cost savings
- NLU model training pipeline with conversation log analysis

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Hallucination risk**: AI chatbot may generate incorrect product specifications, pricing, or availability information; guardrails must enforce that all product data responses are retrieved from authoritative systems (PIM, pricing engine, inventory) rather than generated from training data; product recommendations must be factually accurate to avoid customer complaints and liability
- **Tagalog/Visaya language support**: Filipino customers often mix English and Tagalog (Taglish) or regional languages (Cebuano, Ilonggo) in chat; the NLU model must be trained on Philippine language patterns; initial deployment should support English and Taglish; regional language support is phase 2
- **Inventory accuracy**: Chatbot tells customer "7 units in stock" but actual shelf is empty due to shrinkage or receiving lag; inventory data shown to chatbot should include buffer discount (show "available" only if system on-hand > 3 units) and include "subject to availability" disclaimer
- **Escalation during peak**: During promotional events (bi-monthly sales), chat volume may spike 300%; human agent queue may exceed capacity; chatbot must handle 50%+ during peaks to prevent abandonment; temporary agent surge staffing per W555

### Staffing Implication
- **Product Content Manager**: Chatbot knowledge base maintenance adds 4–6 hours/week; partially offset by reduced manual FAQ handling
- **IT AI/ML Engineer**: Chatbot model monitoring and improvement requires 8–12 hours/week; absorbed by existing Innovation/IT team (W200, W689)
- **Call Center Agents**: Chatbot resolves ~6,000–8,000 interactions/month without human agent; equivalent to ~4–5 full-time agents freed; reallocate to complex issue resolution and outbound proactive service per W756
- **Net headcount impact**: 0 (redistribution of existing headcount)

### Time Estimate
- Chatbot interaction (customer): 1–3 min per session
- Human escalation (agent): 5–15 min per session
- Knowledge base maintenance: 4–6 hours/week
- AI model monitoring: 8–12 hours/week
- **Total system operating effort**: ~20–25 hours/week (Product Content Manager + IT AI/ML Engineer)

## W1043. Customer Paint Coverage Area Calculator & Primer/Finish Quantity Estimator Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests paint quantity recommendation at paint mixing station, pro desk, or via ecommerce |
| **Frequency** | ~8,000–12,000 customer interactions/month across all stores (paint is 8% of SKU portfolio, ~2,800 SKUs) |
| **Volume** | 1 estimation per customer visit; average 3–5 surface calculations per project |
| **Owner** | Paint Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Paint Section), Paint Mixing Station Operator, Customer |

### Background

Paint & Finishes is a high-margin category (8% of active SKUs, ~2,800 items) that benefits significantly from consultative selling. Filipino homeowners and contractors frequently over- or under-purchase paint due to uncertainty about surface area coverage, primer requirements, and number of coats needed. Over-purchasing leads to customer dissatisfaction (perceived waste) and potential returns of tinted paint (which cannot be restocked). Under-purchasing leads to repeat store visits and color inconsistency between batches. The Philippine paint market has specific considerations: (a) tropical humidity affects drying time and coverage rates; (b) concrete block ("hollow block") and CHB (concrete hollow block) walls — the dominant wall material in Philippine construction — are highly porous and absorb 30–40% more paint than flat drywall; (c) new concrete requires alkali-resistant primer; (d) exterior surfaces need weather-resistant formulations; (e) the typical Filipino home has 40–80 sqm of interior wall area per room and 60–120 sqm of exterior wall per facade. This workflow provides an in-store (and ecommerce) paint quantity estimation tool that converts customer room dimensions into precise paint, primer, and supply quantities, reducing over-buying by an estimated 15–20% and increasing customer confidence in project scope. It is distinct from W168 (custom paint mixing operations) which governs the actual tinting process; this workflow addresses the upstream estimation and consultation phase.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Project Intake & Surface Area Calculation**: Sales Associate gathers project details: (a) surface type — interior wall, exterior wall, ceiling, trim/door, metal gate/railing, roof; (b) wall material — new CHB/concrete, old concrete (previously painted), drywall, plywood, wood, metal, stucco/roughcast; (c) surface condition — bare/unpainted, previously painted (good condition), previously painted (peeling/flaking), with stains/water marks; (d) room/area dimensions — length, width, height of each wall or surface; (e) deductions — window openings, door openings, built-in cabinets; (f) desired finish — flat, satin, semi-gloss, gloss; (g) system calculates net paintable surface area (gross area minus deductions) and applies surface-type absorption factor (CHB: 1.3–1.4×; smooth concrete: 1.0×; wood: 1.1×; metal: 0.9×) | Sales Associate | Paint Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 2 | **Primer & Undercoat Recommendation**: System determines primer requirements: (a) new CHB/concrete surfaces: alkaline-resistant primer (mandatory, 1 coat); (b) previously painted surfaces in good condition: no primer needed unless changing from oil-based to water-based; (c) peeling/flaking surfaces: scraping + patching compound + primer (1 coat); (d) stained/water-marked surfaces: stain-blocking primer (1 coat); (e) metal surfaces: anti-rust primer (1 coat); (f) exterior surfaces: weather-resistant primer (1 coat); (g) system calculates primer volume using primer coverage rate (typically 30–40 sqm per gallon for Philippine brands) and surfaces requiring primer | Sales Associate / System | Paint Department Supervisor | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Finish Coat Quantity Calculation**: System computes finish coat quantity: (a) number of coats recommended — interior walls: 2 coats; exterior walls: 2–3 coats (tropical rain exposure); ceiling: 2 coats; metal: 2 coats; (b) coverage rate per product — varies by paint line (economy: 25–30 sqm/gallon; premium: 35–45 sqm/gallon); system pulls coverage data from product master (W252) based on selected paint SKU; (c) total volume = (net surface area × absorption factor × number of coats) ÷ coverage rate per gallon; (d) system rounds up to nearest gallon/4-liter container and adds 10% contingency for touch-ups; (e) if customer has selected paint color, system checks availability in required volume per real-time inventory (W11/W533) | System / Sales Associate | Paint Department Supervisor | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Ancillary Supplies Recommendation**: System generates companion product list: (a) paint rollers — 7" or 9" width based on wall area; roller covers (nap length: 3/8" smooth, 1/2"–3/4" rough surfaces); (b) paint brushes — 2" trim brush, 4" wall brush; (c) paint tray and liners; (d) masking tape (painter's tape) — 1" and 2" widths, calculated linear meters based on edge/trim length; (e) sandpaper — grit 120 (surface prep), grit 220 (between coats); (f) putty/spackling knife and patching compound for surface repair; (g) drop cloth/plastic sheeting — sized to room dimensions; (h) solvent/cleaner — water for latex, mineral spirits for oil-based; (i) system bundles these as a "project supply kit" with total estimated cost | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 5 | **Estimate Generation & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates printable/pdf estimate with: project summary (room name, dimensions, surface types), calculated paintable area, primer recommendation (brand, product, volume, coats), finish coat recommendation (brand, product, color code, volume, coats), ancillary supply list with quantities and prices, total estimated project cost, estimated project time (drying time between coats: 2–4 hours water-based, 6–8 hours oil-based in Philippine humidity); (b) estimate saved to customer's loyalty account or as guest session; (c) customer can directly convert estimate to in-store transaction by scanning estimate QR code at POS (W542); (d) for trade account customers, estimate can be saved as project quote per W542 with 30-day validity; (e) paint mixing station operator receives color formula and volume — proceeds to W168 (custom paint mixing) if customer confirms | Sales Associate | Paint Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Paint coverage calculator engine (surface area, absorption factor, coverage rate per product)
- Product master (W252) — coverage rates, primer compatibility, paint line specifications
- Real-time inventory availability per store (W533)
- Paint mixing station integration (W168) — formula and volume handoff
- POS quotation module (W542) — estimate-to-sale conversion
- Loyalty account integration (W17) — saved estimates and purchase history
- Ecommerce product page integration — online paint calculator widget

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Surface condition misjudgment**: Customer self-reported surface condition may be inaccurate; over-the-phone or online estimates carry higher error risk; recommend in-store consultation for projects >20 sqm
- **Coverage rate variance**: Philippine paint brands (Boysen, Davies, Island Paints, Nippon Paint) have different coverage rates even within the same product line; product master must be updated per SKU per W252 governance
- **Color batch consistency**: If customer under-purchases and returns for additional paint of the same color, the second batch may have slight color variation; system should recommend rounding up and note this risk on the estimate
- **Returns of tinted paint**: Tinted paint cannot be restocked; returns policy (W12A) should clearly communicate non-returnability of custom-mixed paint; this workflow aims to reduce over-buying which in turn reduces return disputes

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Paint Section)**: Estimation adds 5–10 minutes per consultation; at 40–60 paint consultations per store per week, this represents ~5–10 hours/week; absorbed by existing 12 Sales Associates with paint section rotation
- **No permanent incremental headcount**; paint calculator tool reduces manual estimation errors and speeds up consultation by 40%

### Time Estimate
- Customer intake & surface area calculation: 5–10 min
- Primer recommendation: 2–3 min (automated)
- Finish coat calculation: 2–3 min (automated)
- Ancillary supplies: 1–2 min (automated)
- Estimate generation & handoff: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 13–23 min (reduced from 25–40 min without calculator tool)

## W1044. Customer Concrete Mix Ratio & Volume Calculator for Slab/Foundation/Column Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests concrete quantity estimate for a construction project (slab, footing, column, beam, driveway, post filler) |
| **Frequency** | ~4,000–6,000 customer interactions/month across all stores (cement and concrete materials are in the lumber & building materials category — 14% of SKUs) |
| **Volume** | 1 calculation per customer project |
| **Owner** | Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Building Materials Section), Customer |

### Background

Concrete is the most fundamental building material in Philippine construction. Virtually every residential and commercial building project in the Philippines involves concrete work — from simple post footings for a fence (0.05 cubic meters) to full house slabs (5–20 cubic meters) to multi-story foundation works (50+ cubic meters). The Philippine standard concrete mix uses bags of Portland cement (40 kg per bag), sand (fine aggregate), gravel (coarse aggregate), and water. Class A mix (1:1½:3 cement:sand:gravel) is standard for structural elements; Class B (1:2:4) for non-structural; Class C (1:3:6) for fill and non-critical work. Filipino contractors and DIY homeowners frequently miscalculate material quantities because: (a) concrete volume depends on three-dimensional formwork dimensions, which many customers struggle to compute; (b) waste factors for concrete are 5–10% due to spillage, over-excavation, and form irregularities; (c) the number of cement bags must be derived from the mix ratio and volume, not estimated visually. BuildRight Depot sells ~PHP 3–4 billion/year in cement, sand, gravel, and related concrete materials — this consultative service drives correct purchasing, reduces under-buying (which causes project delays and repeat visits), and differentiates BuildRight from competitors who do not offer estimation services. This workflow is distinct from W964 (bulk cement, sand & aggregates delivery) which covers the logistics of delivery; this workflow covers the upstream quantity estimation.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Type & Structural Element Identification**: Sales Associate identifies the concrete application: (a) slab-on-grade (floor slab, driveway, carport); (b) footing/foundation (isolated footing, continuous footing, mat foundation); (c) column (rectangular, circular); (d) beam (tie beam, grade beam, lintel); (e) wall (CHB wall footings, retaining wall); (f) post filler (hollow block post filler, 4"/6" round column filler); (g) stairs; (h) other custom form. System displays the applicable structural standards and minimum recommended concrete class (Class A for structural, Class B for general, Class C for fill) | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 2–3 min |
| 2 | **Dimension Input & Volume Calculation**: Customer provides dimensions and system computes volume: (a) rectangular slab: length × width × thickness (in meters; default thickness: 0.10m for residential floor, 0.15m for garage/driveway); (b) L-shaped or irregular slab: decomposed into rectangles; (c) footing: length × width × depth (typical depth 0.60–1.20m for single-story); (d) column: width × depth × height; (e) circular column: π × radius² × height; (f) beam: width × depth × length; (g) retaining wall: length × height × thickness (tapers if applicable); (h) system adds waste factor: 5% for simple shapes, 10% for irregular shapes or complex formwork; (i) system outputs total concrete volume in cubic meters (m³) | Sales Associate / Customer / System | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 3 | **Mix Design & Material Quantity Breakdown**: System computes material quantities based on selected mix class: (a) **Class A (1:1½:3)**: 9.5 bags cement per m³, 0.50 m³ sand per m³, 1.0 m³ gravel per m³; (b) **Class B (1:2:4)**: 7.0 bags cement per m³, 0.67 m³ sand per m³, 1.33 m³ gravel per m³; (c) **Class C (1:3:6)**: 5.0 bags cement per m³, 0.83 m³ sand per m³, 1.67 m³ gravel per m³; (d) system multiplies per-m³ quantities by total volume (including waste factor); (e) outputs: number of cement bags (40 kg), volume of sand (m³ or cubic meters equivalent in truck loads), volume of gravel (m³ or cubic meters equivalent in truck loads), estimated water volume (liters); (f) for projects >3 m³, system recommends ready-mixed concrete as an alternative per W964 (bulk delivery) and shows cost comparison: bagged DIY vs. ready-mix delivered | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Companion Materials Recommendation**: System generates companion product list: (a) reinforcing steel (rebar) — size and quantity per standard spacing (10mm @ 200mm O.C. for slab; 12mm or 16mm for columns and beams) per W986/W1060; (b) tie wire — 1.5 kg per 100 kg of rebar; (c) formwork materials — plywood (1/4" or 1/2" for concrete forming), 2×2 or 2×3 wood studs for form support; (d) plastic sheeting — for curing cover (kept wet for 7 days per Philippine engineering practice); (e) vibro-tamping rod or concrete vibrator rental per W139; (f) wheelbarrow and mixing tools; (g) waterproofing compound for below-grade concrete; (h) system bundles companion materials with total estimated cost | System | Sales Associate | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 5 | **Estimate Generation, Delivery Scheduling & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates printable/PDF estimate with: project description, structural element dimensions, computed concrete volume, selected mix class with ratio, material quantity breakdown (cement bags, sand m³, gravel m³, water liters), companion materials list with prices, total estimated project cost; (b) for orders >2 m³ of sand/gravel: system triggers bulk delivery scheduling per W964 with delivery fee estimate based on distance; (c) for orders ≤2 m³: customer can load materials at store yard per W950 (vehicle loading assistance); (d) estimate saved to customer's loyalty account; (e) customer can convert estimate to transaction at POS per W542; (f) for trade account B2B customers, estimate converts to project quote per W162 with delivery window scheduling | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Concrete volume calculator engine with dimensional input for multiple structural shapes
- Mix design database (Class A/B/C ratios, per-m³ material factors)
- Product master (W252) — cement bag size, sand/gravel pricing per m³
- Real-time inventory availability (W533) for cement, sand, gravel
- Bulk delivery scheduling module (W964) integration
- POS quotation module (W542) — estimate-to-sale conversion
- Loyalty account integration (W17) — saved estimates
- B2B quotation module (W162) — trade account project quotes

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Structural engineering disclaimer**: BuildRight staff are not structural engineers; the calculator provides material quantity estimates only, not structural design; system must display disclaimer on every estimate: "This estimate is for material quantity guidance only and does not constitute structural engineering advice. Consult a licensed civil engineer for structural design requirements."
- **Soil condition variability**: Actual excavation depth and footing size may differ from customer's stated dimensions due to soil conditions; recommend 10% contingency on volume for foundation works
- **Sand/gravel volume measurement**: Philippine sand and gravel are sold by the cubic meter (truck load) with inherent ±10% measurement variance; system should note this on estimates
- **Cement shelf life**: Cement bags have a 3-month shelf life in Philippine humidity; customers ordering large quantities (>50 bags) should be advised to schedule delivery closer to pour date

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Building Materials)**: Estimation adds 10–15 minutes per consultation; at 20–30 concrete consultations per store per week, this represents ~5–8 hours/week; absorbed by existing 12 Sales Associates with building materials section rotation
- **No permanent incremental headcount**; calculator tool reduces manual estimation time by ~60%

### Time Estimate
- Project type identification: 2–3 min
- Dimension input & volume calculation: 3–5 min
- Mix design & material breakdown: 1–2 min (automated)
- Companion materials: 2–3 min (automated)
- Estimate & delivery scheduling: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 11–18 min (reduced from 25–40 min without calculator tool)

## W1045. Store-Level Customer PVC Pipe Cutting, Jointing & Fabrication Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer purchases PVC pipe (or brings project requirements) and requests custom-length cutting or jointing/fabrication |
| **Frequency** | ~2,000–3,000 requests/month across all stores (plumbing is 12% of SKUs, ~4,200 items; PVC pipe is the highest-volume plumbing SKU) |
| **Volume** | 1–10 cuts per customer visit; average 3–5 cuts |
| **Owner** | Plumbing Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Plumbing Section), Customer |

### Background

PVC (polyvinyl chloride) pipe is the dominant plumbing material in Philippine construction, used for water supply lines (PVC Schedule 40/80), drainage (PVC DWV), and electrical conduit. BuildRight Depot sells PVC pipe in standard lengths (3m and 6m) across diameters from ½" to 6". Filipino DIY homeowners and small contractors frequently need custom-length PVC pipe for tight installations (under-sink drainage, toilet rough-in, shower lines) but lack the cutting tools (PVC cutter, hacksaw with fine-tooth blade, miter box) for clean, square cuts. Improperly cut PVC pipe has burrs that prevent solvent-weld joints from sealing, leading to leaks. This in-store cutting service provides: (a) clean, square cuts to customer-specified lengths; (b) solvent-weld joining of fittings to cut lengths (optional); (c) pipe threading for galvanized iron (GI) pipe (distinct from PVC). This is distinct from W944 (pipe threading, cutting & fabrication for metal pipe) which covers steel/GI pipe; PVC pipe requires different cutting tools and solvent cement joining. This service reduces customer frustration, increases average transaction value (customers buy full-length pipes and fittings instead of settling for pre-cut sections at higher per-meter cost), and differentiates BuildRight from competing hardware stores.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Requirement Intake**: Sales Associate gathers project requirements: (a) pipe material — PVC (Schedule 40, Schedule 80, DWV, conduit), CPVC (hot water), or PPR; (b) pipe diameter — ½", ¾", 1", 1¼", 1½", 2", 3", 4", 6"; (c) number of pieces and lengths needed (in centimeters or inches); (d) jointing requirements — solvent-weld fittings (elbow, tee, coupling, reducer, adapter) to be pre-joined; (e) intended application — water supply, drainage, electrical conduit, irrigation, other; (f) system validates that requested lengths are achievable from standard 3m/6m stock, minimizes waste (nesting algorithm for multiple cuts) | Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **Cutting Execution**: Sales Associate performs PVC cutting at dedicated cutting station in plumbing section: (a) select correct pipe from stock per diameter and schedule; (b) measure and mark cut points using tape measure and marker; (c) position pipe in cutting jig (or miter box for smaller diameters); (d) execute cut using dedicated PVC cutter (for diameters ≤2") or fine-tooth hacksaw with miter box (for diameters >2"); (e) deburr cut ends using chamfering tool or utility knife — remove internal and external burrs to ensure proper solvent-weld seating; (f) verify cut length within ±2mm tolerance using tape measure; (g) wipe cut ends clean of dust and shavings | Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 3–8 min (depending on number of cuts) |
| 3 | **Optional Jointing / Fabrication**: If customer requests pre-joined assemblies: (a) dry-fit all components to verify alignment before solvent cement application; (b) apply PVC primer (purple primer, mandatory for Schedule 40/80) to outside of pipe end and inside of fitting socket; (c) apply PVC solvent cement to primed surfaces; (d) insert pipe into fitting with quarter-turn twist; (e) hold joint for 15–30 seconds for initial set; (f) wipe excess cement; (g) mark joint set time: 15 min for handling, 2 hours for light pressure, 24 hours for full pressure; (h) customer takes pre-joined assembly with remaining uncut pipe lengths | Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 5–15 min (depending on number of joints) |
| 4 | **Transaction Processing & Waste Handling**: (a) system charges for: full-length pipe(s) consumed (prorated by meter), fittings used, primer/cement consumed (if jointing), cutting service fee (or waived for purchases >PHP 500); (b) cutting waste (offcuts <30 cm) collected in store PVC recycling bin per W502 (non-hazardous waste management); (c) offcuts ≥30 cm offered to customer for potential use; (d) system updates inventory: full-length pipe decremented, cutting waste accounted per disposition code; (e) customer receives cut pieces, any pre-joined assemblies, and remaining pipe | Sales Associate / POS Cashier | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- PVC cutting service module — cut list entry, nesting optimization, waste calculation
- Product master (W252) — pipe dimensions, cutting service SKU, fitting compatibility
- Inventory deduction — full-length pipe consumed, waste disposition (W502)
- POS service item processing (W544) — service fee SKU
- Real-time inventory availability (W533)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Cut accuracy**: PVC cutter blade wear leads to angled cuts; weekly blade replacement schedule required for high-volume stores
- **Solvent cement safety**: PVC primer and cement contain tetrahydrofuran (THF) and cyclohexanone — volatile, flammable chemicals; cutting station must be in well-ventilated area; PPE (gloves, safety glasses) required per W172
- **Customer mismeasurement**: Customers frequently provide incorrect measurements; recommend dry-fit verification before solvent cement application
- **Waste management**: PVC offcuts cannot be recycled through standard channels; partner with specialized PVC recyclers per W167

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Plumbing Section)**: Cutting adds 10–20 min per customer; at 10–15 PVC cutting requests per store per day, this represents ~2–5 hours/day; absorbed by existing department staff with rotating cutting duty
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Requirement intake: 3–5 min
- Cutting execution: 3–8 min
- Jointing (if applicable): 5–15 min
- Transaction & waste handling: 3–5 min
- **Total per customer**: 14–33 min (average ~20 min)

## W1046. Customer Door & Window Measurement, Sizing & Custom Order Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests door or window sizing assistance, custom-order door/window, or replacement for existing unit |
| **Frequency** | ~2,500–3,500 customer interactions/month across all stores |
| **Volume** | 1–4 door/window units per customer project |
| **Owner** | Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Building Materials Section), Special Order Coordinator, Customer |

### Background

Doors and windows are high-value, project-critical items in Philippine home construction and renovation. A single-panel flush door costs PHP 1,500–4,000; a panel door PHP 3,000–8,000; a sliding glass window PHP 2,500–15,000; and a main entrance door with frame PHP 8,000–25,000. Unlike commodity items (cement, nails), doors and windows are dimension-critical — a 10mm error in rough opening measurement results in an unusable unit. Philippine residential construction uses non-standardized rough openings (unlike US/Europe where modular sizes are common), making custom sizing the norm rather than the exception. Key door/window types in the Philippine market: (a) flush doors (standard sizes: 0.70m × 2.03m, 0.80m × 2.03m); (b) panel doors (decorative, same standard widths); (c) sliding glass windows (jalousie/awful windows being replaced by modern aluminum sliding); (d) swing casement windows; (e) main entrance doors (solid hardwood, customized); (f) fire-rated doors (for commercial buildings, per BFP requirement). BuildRight Depot carries standard-size doors and windows as stock items, but ~40% of door/window sales involve custom orders from partner manufacturers with 7–14 day lead times. This workflow covers the measurement consultation, sizing recommendation, and custom-order placement process.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Requirement Intake**: Sales Associate identifies the door/window need: (a) new construction (rough opening not yet built — recommend standard sizes); (b) replacement (existing unit to be replaced — requires precise measurement of existing frame and rough opening); (c) renovation/upgrade (existing opening to receive new unit — requires measurement of finished opening); (d) door type — interior flush, interior panel, main entrance (solid wood, metal-clad, fiberglass), fire-rated (1-hour, 2-hour), bi-fold, sliding; (e) window type — sliding aluminum, casement, fixed, awning, jalousie (replacement blades only); (f) material preference — wood (narra, tanguile, molave), aluminum, steel, fiberglass, PVC/uPVC; (g) finish — primed, pre-finished, raw (for on-site finishing) | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Measurement Guidance & Data Collection**: Sales Associate provides measurement guidance (if customer has not yet measured) or records customer-provided measurements: (a) for door replacement: (i) existing door slab width and height; (ii) frame interior width and height (jamb-to-jamb); (iii) rough opening width and height (framing to framing, behind the jambs); (iv) wall thickness (for jamb depth); (v) hinge side (left-hand or right-hand swing); (vi) lock bore hole location; (b) for window replacement: (i) glass/viewable area width and height; (ii) frame exterior width and height; (iii) rough opening width and height; (iv) wall thickness; (v) sill height from floor; (vi) number of panels/slides; (c) system records all measurements with unit (mm or inches) and provides a printable measurement worksheet; (d) if customer cannot provide measurements, system generates on-site measurement service request per W442 (site technical survey & measurement services) with service fee | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 3 | **Sizing Recommendation & Availability Check**: (a) system compares customer measurements against standard size catalog — if within 5mm tolerance of a standard size, recommend stock item for immediate purchase; (b) if no standard size matches, system flags for custom order; (c) system checks real-time inventory (W533) for matching stock items at customer's store and nearby stores within 50 km per W214 (inter-store transfer); (d) for custom orders: system generates custom specification with manufacturer — door/window type, dimensions (width × height × thickness/frame depth), material, finish, glass type (clear, tinted, frosted, tempered, laminated), hardware (lockset, hinges, handles), fire rating (if applicable); (e) system estimates custom order lead time: 7–10 days for doors, 10–14 days for windows, 14–21 days for fire-rated doors | System / Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 4 | **Custom Order Placement & Deposit Collection**: (a) for custom orders: Sales Associate creates special order in system per W545 (special order & customer order processing); (b) system generates custom order quote with: specification details, manufacturer, estimated lead time, total price, 50% deposit requirement; (c) customer reviews and approves quote; (d) system collects 50% deposit at POS per W546 (deposit & progress payment collection); (e) special order transmitted to partner manufacturer via vendor portal (W866); (f) system sets expected delivery date and sends confirmation to customer via SMS/email; (g) for stock items at nearby stores: system initiates inter-store transfer per W214 with 2–3 day delivery | Sales Associate / Special Order Coordinator | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 5 | **Delivery Notification & Customer Pickup/Delivery**: (a) when custom order arrives at store (7–21 days): receiving clerk processes goods receipt per W109; (b) system sends automated notification to customer via SMS/email: "Your custom door/window order #XXX has arrived at BuildRight [Store Name]. Please pick up within 5 days or call to schedule home delivery per W5D"; (c) customer picks up at customer service counter — verify order against receipt and customer ID; (d) remaining 50% balance collected at POS; (e) for bulky items: offer home delivery scheduling per W5D with delivery fee; (f) system closes special order and updates vendor performance metrics per W44 | Receiving Clerk / Customer Service Rep / Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–10 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Door/window sizing engine — measurement-to-specification conversion
- Standard size catalog lookup against product master (W252)
- Real-time inventory availability (W533) with inter-store transfer (W214)
- Special order module (W545) — custom specification, vendor order
- Deposit collection at POS (W546) — 50% upfront, 50% on delivery
- Vendor portal (W866) — custom order transmission to manufacturer
- Customer notification engine — SMS/email delivery alerts
- Home delivery scheduling (W5D) — bulky item delivery

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Measurement error liability**: Incorrect measurements result in unusable custom products that cannot be restocked; system must display measurement verification disclaimer and recommend on-site measurement service (W442) for high-value orders (>PHP 10,000)
- **Long custom order lead times**: 7–21 day lead times may lose customer to competitors with standard sizes; offer standard-size modifications (planing/shaving) for simple size adjustments as an in-store service
- **Damage during transport**: Large doors and windows are susceptible to damage during delivery; require vertical transport packaging and delivery partner compliance per W268

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Building Materials)**: Door/window consultation adds 15–25 min per customer; at 12–18 consultations per store per week, this represents ~4–6 hours/week
- **Special Order Coordinator**: Manages ~50–80 active custom door/window orders at any time across the store's order book; estimated 2–3 hours/day of order tracking and vendor follow-up
- **No permanent incremental headcount**; absorbed by existing building materials team

### Time Estimate
- Requirement intake: 5–8 min
- Measurement guidance: 5–10 min
- Sizing recommendation & availability: 3–5 min
- Order placement & deposit: 5–8 min
- Delivery notification & handoff: 5–10 min
- **Total per customer**: 23–41 min (average ~30 min)

## W1048. Customer Rainwater Harvesting System Design & Material Sizing Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests rainwater harvesting system design, or expresses interest in water conservation during plumbing/building materials consultation |
| **Frequency** | ~500–800 consultations/month across all stores (growing interest in Philippine water conservation, especially in water-scarce regions like Metro Manila, Cebu, and parts of Mindanao) |
| **Volume** | 1 system design per customer consultation |
| **Owner** | Plumbing Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Plumbing Section), Customer |

### Background

Rainwater harvesting is increasingly relevant in the Philippines due to: (a) water scarcity in urban areas (Metro Manila, Cebu, Davao) where municipal water supply is unreliable; (b) LGU mandates in some cities requiring rainwater collection systems for new construction (e.g., Quezon City Green Building Code, Davao City Rainwater Ordinance); (c) El Niño drought events that cause water rationing; (d) cost savings for households — a 1,000-liter rainwater tank can supply ~30% of a Filipino household's non-potable water needs (toilet flushing, laundry, garden watering, car washing). BuildRight Depot sells all the components needed for rainwater harvesting: PVC gutters and downspouts, PVC storage tanks (500L to 10,000L), first-flush diverters, leaf screens, mesh filters, PVC piping, submersible pumps, float valves, and overflow fittings. This consultative service helps customers size and select the right components for their roof area, rainfall intensity, and water demand — converting what would be a commodity parts sale into a full-system solution. This workflow is distinct from W984 (water tank & pump sizing) which focuses on pressurized water supply systems; this workflow specifically addresses rainwater collection system design with catchment-area-based sizing.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Catchment Area & Demand Assessment**: Sales Associate gathers project parameters: (a) roof type — galvanized iron (GI) sheet, clay tile, concrete flat roof, metal deck; (b) roof catchment area — length × width of roof section(s) that will drain to the collection system (in square meters); (c) roof slope and gutter location; (d) average annual rainfall for customer's location (system auto-populates from PAGASA data based on customer's city/municipality per W310 — address hierarchy); (e) water demand — intended uses (garden/lawn irrigation, toilet flushing, laundry, car washing, general cleaning); (f) available space for storage tank (ground level, elevated platform, underground); (g) existing gutter system — compatible or needs replacement; (h) budget range | Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Storage Tank Sizing Calculation**: System computes recommended tank capacity: (a) monthly harvestable rainwater (liters/month) = roof catchment area (m²) × average monthly rainfall (mm) × 0.85 (runoff coefficient for GI/metal roof; 0.75 for concrete; 0.80 for tile) × 0.90 (first-flush diverter and filter losses); (b) system displays monthly harvest by month using PAGASA rainfall distribution (wet months June–November produce 70–80% of annual harvest); (c) recommended tank size = 2–3 months of dry-season demand (December–May) to bridge the dry period; (d) system recommends tank model(s) from inventory: 500L (small household, garden only), 1,000L (medium household, garden + toilet flushing), 2,000L–5,000L (large household or small commercial), 10,000L (commercial/institutional); (e) system checks real-time inventory (W533) for recommended tank at customer's store | System / Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 3 | **System Component Specification**: System generates complete bill of materials: (a) gutter system — PVC or aluminum gutter (125mm or 150mm half-round or box profile), length = roof perimeter along collection side, brackets @ 600mm O.C., end caps, joiners; (b) downspout(s) — PVC pipe diameter (75mm or 100mm), number of downspouts (1 per 50 sqm of roof area, minimum 2), elbows and brackets; (c) first-flush diverter — 1 per downspout (diverts first 20 liters of rainwater containing roof contaminants); (d) leaf screen / mesh filter — installed at gutter-to-downspout transition; (e) inlet filter — at tank entry point; (f) storage tank — per step 2 recommendation; (g) overflow pipe — PVC pipe from tank overflow to storm drain, diameter ≥ downspout diameter; (h) outlet fitting — ball valve or float valve at tank base; (i) pump (optional) — submersible pump per W984 sizing if customer needs pressurized output; (j) pipework from tank to point-of-use — PVC pipe, fittings, isolation valves; (k) system calculates total material cost using current pricing per W252 | System | Sales Associate | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate Generation & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates printable/PDF estimate with: project summary (roof area, location, rainfall data), monthly harvest calculation with PAGASA data table, recommended tank size with rationale, complete bill of materials with quantities and prices, total estimated system cost, estimated installation time (DIY: 1–2 days; professional: 4–6 hours), maintenance requirements (gutter cleaning quarterly, tank cleaning annually, filter replacement as needed); (b) if tank requires delivery (tanks >500L): system triggers home delivery scheduling per W5D with delivery fee estimate; (c) offer professional installation referral per W138 (home installation services) and W904 (contractor referral); (d) estimate saved to customer's loyalty account; (e) customer can convert estimate to POS transaction per W542 | Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Rainwater harvest calculator engine — catchment area, PAGASA rainfall data, runoff coefficients
- PAGASA rainfall database integration — monthly averages by city/municipality (W310 address hierarchy)
- Product master (W252) — tank models, gutter profiles, PVC pipe specs, pricing
- Real-time inventory availability (W533)
- Home delivery scheduling (W5D) — bulky tank delivery
- POS quotation module (W542) — estimate-to-sale conversion
- Contractor referral module (W904) — professional installation referral
- Home installation service module (W138) — installation booking
- Loyalty account integration (W17) — saved estimates

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Water quality disclaimer**: Rainwater from GI sheet roofs may contain lead, zinc, and other contaminants; system must display disclaimer: "Rainwater harvested from this system is recommended for non-potable use only. Do not use for drinking, cooking, or bathing without additional water treatment per DOH standards."
- **Structural load of elevated tanks**: A 1,000L tank weighs 1,000 kg when full; if customer plans elevated installation, recommend structural assessment by licensed engineer
- **LGU permit requirements**: Some LGUs require building permits for tank installations >2,000L; advise customer to check with municipal building official per W1056 (construction permit advisory)
- **Mosquito breeding**: Open tanks or improperly sealed systems create mosquito breeding sites (dengue risk); recommend all openings have mesh screens and tank is fully enclosed

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Plumbing Section)**: Rainwater harvesting consultation adds 15–20 min per customer; at 3–4 consultations per store per week, this represents ~1–1.5 hours/week
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Catchment area & demand assessment: 5–8 min
- Tank sizing calculation: 2–3 min (automated)
- Component specification: 2–3 min (automated)
- Estimate generation & handoff: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 12–19 min (average ~15 min)

## W1050. Customer Staircase Tread, Riser & Railing Material Calculator Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests staircase material quantities for residential or small commercial construction project |
| **Frequency** | ~800–1,200 consultations/month across all stores |
| **Volume** | 1 staircase calculation per consultation |
| **Owner** | Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Building Materials Section), Customer |

### Background

Staircases are a universal element in Philippine multi-story residential construction (2–3 story homes are common in urban areas due to limited lot sizes). A typical Philippine residential staircase has 12–16 risers (floor-to-floor height ~3.0 meters) with 2–3 flights and 1–2 intermediate landings. Customers (both DIY homeowners and small contractors) frequently miscalculate staircase material quantities because: (a) tread and riser counts depend on precise floor-to-floor height and desired step dimensions (rise and run); (b) the Philippine National Building Code (PD 1096) mandates maximum riser height of 200mm and minimum tread depth of 250mm for residential stairs; (c) stringer (carriage) length must be calculated from total rise and run using the Pythagorean theorem; (d) railing balusters must comply with maximum 100mm spacing per PD 1096 (child safety). Common errors lead to under-buying (multiple store visits) or over-buying (waste and returns). This calculator service provides precise material quantities for: treads, risers, stringers, landing framing, railing posts, handrails, and balusters — converting a complex geometric calculation into a simple bill of materials that drives a complete sale.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Staircase Dimension Input**: Sales Associate gathers staircase parameters: (a) total floor-to-floor height (vertical rise) in meters; (b) total horizontal run available (floor space for staircase footprint) in meters; (c) staircase width (typical Philippine residential: 0.80m–1.00m); (d) number of flights (straight run, L-shaped with landing, U-shaped with landing); (e) desired step dimensions: target riser height (150–200mm per PD 1096), target tread depth (250–300mm per PD 1096); (f) material preference — treads: plywood (18mm), solid wood (tanguile, narra), tiles on concrete; risers: plywood (12mm), solid wood; stringers: 2×10 or 2×12 lumber; railing: wood (tanguile), steel, aluminum; (g) landing type — none, quarter-turn (L-shape), half-turn (U-shape) with landing dimensions | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Geometric Calculation & Code Compliance Check**: System computes staircase geometry: (a) number of risers = total rise ÷ target riser height (rounded up to nearest integer); (b) actual riser height = total rise ÷ number of risers; (c) system validates: riser height ≤ 200mm per PD 1096 (flags non-compliance with warning); (d) number of treads = number of risers − 1 (per flight); (e) total run = number of treads × tread depth; (f) system validates: total run ≤ available horizontal space (flags if insufficient space, recommends shorter tread or L/U configuration); (g) stringer length = √(total rise² + total run²) per flight; (h) for L/U configurations: calculates landing framing dimensions and separate stringer lengths for each flight; (i) system displays 2D side-view diagram of staircase with dimensions | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Material Quantity Calculation**: System generates bill of materials: (a) **Treads**: quantity = number of treads, width = staircase width, depth = tread depth, material = selected tread material (board footage calculated); (b) **Risers**: quantity = number of risers, width = staircase width, height = actual riser height, material = selected riser material; (c) **Stringers**: quantity = 2 (minimum) + 1 intermediate for stairs >1m wide; length per stringer calculated per step 2g; material = 2×10 or 2×12 lumber; (d) **Landing framing** (if applicable): joists, header beams, plywood decking — per landing dimensions; (e) **Railing**: newel posts (1 at bottom, 1 at top, 1 at each landing = 2–4 posts), handrail length = stringer length × number of flights, balusters = (handrail length ÷ maximum baluster spacing per PD 1096) − 1 per flight section, baluster height = riser height × number of risers per section + 0.90m (handrail height per code); (f) **Hardware**: nails, screws, construction adhesive, angle brackets for stringer-to-floor connection; (g) system calculates total board footage and converts to standard lumber lengths available in inventory | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate Generation & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates printable/PDF estimate with: staircase side-view diagram with dimensions, step-by-step code compliance summary, complete bill of materials with quantities, unit prices, and total cost, PD 1096 compliance notes, assembly instructions overview; (b) check inventory availability for all lumber lengths and materials per W533; (c) for non-stock items (special wood species, decorative balusters): create special order per W545; (d) offer home delivery for lumber per W5D; (e) estimate saved to loyalty account and convertible to POS transaction per W542 | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Staircase geometric calculator engine — rise, run, stringer length, landing dimensions
- PD 1096 compliance validation — riser height, tread depth, baluster spacing, handrail height
- Product master (W252) — lumber dimensions, pricing, availability
- Real-time inventory availability (W533) — lumber lengths
- POS quotation module (W542) — estimate-to-sale conversion
- Special order module (W545) — non-stock decorative items
- Home delivery scheduling (W5D) — lumber delivery

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Structural engineering disclaimer**: System provides material quantities only; staircase structural design (stringer sizing, load capacity, anchoring method) requires licensed engineer for commercial buildings; mandatory disclaimer on all estimates
- **Actual vs. planned dimensions**: Customer-provided floor-to-floor height may differ from actual by 50–100mm due to finish floor materials; recommend field measurement verification per W442
- **Non-standard staircase configurations**: Curved, spiral, or winder stairs require custom engineering beyond calculator capability; recommend professional contractor referral per W904

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Building Materials)**: Consultation adds 10–15 min; at 4–6 consultations per store per week, this represents ~1–1.5 hours/week
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Dimension input: 5–8 min
- Geometric calculation: 1–2 min (automated)
- Material quantity calculation: 1–2 min (automated)
- Estimate generation & handoff: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 10–17 min (average ~13 min)

## W1052. Customer Gutter, Downspout & Flashing Sizing Calculator Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests gutter system sizing for new construction, renovation, or replacement |
| **Frequency** | ~1,200–1,800 consultations/month across all stores (gutters are part of the lumber & building materials and plumbing categories) |
| **Volume** | 1 calculation per customer project |
| **Owner** | Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Building Materials/Plumbing Section), Customer |

### Background

Gutter and downspout systems are essential in Philippine residential and commercial construction due to high annual rainfall (1,500–4,000mm/year depending on region). Proper gutter sizing prevents: (a) roof runoff damaging building foundations and walls; (b) water ingress through windows and doors; (c) soil erosion around building perimeter; (d) flooding of ground-floor areas during intense downpours. Philippine construction commonly uses: (a) GI (galvanized iron) half-round or box gutters — traditional, durable; (b) PVC gutters — lightweight, corrosion-resistant, easier installation; (c) aluminum gutters — premium, lightweight, no rust; (d) pre-painted GI gutters — aesthetic appeal. Downspouts are typically PVC (75mm or 100mm diameter) or GI (round or rectangular). Flashing materials include GI sheet, aluminum sheet, and rubberized asphalt membrane for valley flashing, chimney flashing, and roof-wall intersections. Customers frequently miscalculate gutter lengths (forgetting to account for roof pitch and overhang) and downspout quantities (underestimating for large roof areas). This service converts a complex hydraulic calculation into a complete bill of materials.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Roof & Building Parameter Input**: Sales Associate gathers project parameters: (a) roof type — gable, hip, shed, flat (with parapet), combination; (b) roof dimensions — length and width of each roof plane (or total roof footprint area); (c) roof pitch/slope angle (in degrees or rise-to-run ratio); (d) number of stories (affects downspout length); (e) gutter type preference — half-round (125mm or 150mm), box/K-style (125mm or 150mm), PVC, GI, aluminum; (f) downspout type — round PVC (75mm/100mm), rectangular GI, round GI; (g) building location (for rainfall intensity lookup per PAGASA data per W310); (h) gutter run direction — along eaves (both sides for gable), along all sides (hip roof) | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Gutter & Downspout Sizing Calculation**: System computes hydraulic requirements: (a) roof drainage area per gutter run = roof plane width × horizontal projection (length × cos(pitch)); (b) design rainfall intensity (mm/hr) per PAGASA 10-year return period data for customer's location; (c) peak runoff (liters/min) = drainage area (m²) × rainfall intensity (mm/hr) ÷ 60; (d) gutter capacity per profile: half-round 125mm = 1.2 L/s at 1:200 slope, half-round 150mm = 2.0 L/s, box 125mm = 1.5 L/s, box 150mm = 2.5 L/s; (e) if peak runoff exceeds single gutter capacity: system recommends (i) larger profile, (ii) steeper slope, or (iii) additional downspouts to reduce gutter run length; (f) downspout quantity: minimum 1 per 10m of gutter run or 1 per 50m² of drainage area (whichever is greater); (g) downspout length = roof edge height to ground + 300mm extension (splash block or direct to drainage) | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Flashing & Accessories Calculation**: System generates complete material list: (a) **Gutter sections**: total linear meters per gutter profile (standard lengths: 3m or 6m); (b) **Gutter brackets/braces**: @ 600mm O.C. for PVC, @ 900mm O.C. for GI; (c) **End caps**: 2 per gutter run (left and right); (d) **Joiners/connectors**: 1 per section joint; (e) **Corner pieces** (inside/outside): per roof plan corners; (f) **Downspout sections**: total length per downspout × number of downspouts (standard lengths: 3m); (g) **Downspout elbows**: 2 per downspout (top offset from gutter, bottom offset away from wall); (h) **Downspout brackets/wall clips**: @ 1.5m O.C.; (i) **Splash blocks or flexible downspout extensions**: 1 per downspout; (j) **Valley flashing**: length × number of valleys (for gable/hip intersections); (k) **Apron flashing**: at roof-wall intersections; (l) **Step flashing**: at chimney/penetration interfaces; (m) **Sealant and pop rivets/screws** for assembly; (n) **Leaf guard/screen**: optional, same linear meters as gutter | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate Generation & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates printable/PDF estimate with: roof drainage diagram, hydraulic calculation summary, recommended gutter profile and downspout configuration, complete bill of materials with quantities and prices, total estimated project cost, installation instructions overview; (b) check inventory per W533; (c) for non-stock items (special gutter profiles, aluminum flashing): special order per W545; (d) offer delivery per W5D for long gutter sections; (e) offer contractor referral per W904; (f) estimate saved and convertible to sale per W542 | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Gutter sizing calculator engine — hydraulic calculation, PAGASA rainfall intensity data
- Product master (W252) — gutter profiles, downspout specifications, pricing
- Real-time inventory (W533)
- POS quotation (W542), special orders (W545), delivery (W5D)
- Contractor referral (W904)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Installation complexity**: Gutter installation requires working at roof height; recommend professional installation per W138 for multi-story buildings
- **Rainfall intensity data accuracy**: PAGASA data may not reflect local microclimate variations; add 20% capacity margin for safety

### Staffing Implication
- No permanent incremental headcount; ~1 hour/week of Sales Associate time per store

### Time Estimate
- Total per consultation: 10–17 min (average ~13 min)

## W1053. Customer Bathroom & Kitchen Exhaust Fan & Ventilation Duct Sizing Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests exhaust fan recommendation for bathroom, kitchen, or other ventilation application |
| **Frequency** | ~2,000–3,000 consultations/month across all stores (home appliances category: 5% of SKUs, ~1,750 items; exhaust fans are a high-turn sub-category) |
| **Volume** | 1 sizing calculation per room |
| **Owner** | Home Appliances Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Appliances Section), Customer |

### Background

Exhaust ventilation is critical in Philippine homes due to tropical humidity (60–90% relative humidity year-round). Without proper ventilation, bathrooms develop mold and mildew within weeks, and kitchens accumulate grease and cooking odors. Philippine building standards (PD 1096 National Building Code) require mechanical ventilation for windowless bathrooms and commercial kitchens. The Philippine exhaust fan market uses Air Changes per Hour (ACH) as the standard metric: bathrooms require 8–10 ACH, kitchens require 15–20 ACH, and laundry areas require 5–8 ACH. BuildRight Depot sells exhaust fans from PHP 500 (basic axial fan, 4" duct) to PHP 8,000 (premium centrifugal inline fan with humidity sensor, 6" duct). Customers frequently purchase under-sized fans because they select by duct diameter ("I need a 4-inch fan") rather than by airflow capacity (CMH — cubic meters per hour) matched to their room volume. This service converts room dimensions into CMH requirements and recommends the correct fan model, duct size, and accessories.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Room Parameter Input**: Sales Associate gathers room details: (a) application — bathroom, kitchen, laundry, workshop, storage room; (b) room dimensions — length, width, height (in meters); (c) room volume = length × width × height (m³); (d) existing duct/vent opening — yes/no, diameter if existing; (e) wall type — CHB (concrete hollow block, requires core drilling for new opening), wood frame, drywall; (f) ceiling type — suspended ceiling (space for inline fan above), solid concrete slab (wall-mount fan only); (g) power source — wall outlet available, or hardwired connection needed; (h) special features — humidity sensor, timer, backdraft damper, speed control | Sales Associate | Home Appliances Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **CMH Requirement & Fan Sizing**: System calculates required airflow: (a) minimum CMH = room volume × target ACH (bathroom: 8–10, kitchen: 15–20, laundry: 5–8, workshop: 6–10); (b) system recommends fan models from inventory with rated CMH ≥ minimum CMH; (c) system selects recommended duct size: 4" (100mm) for CMH ≤200, 5" (125mm) for CMH 200–400, 6" (150mm) for CMH 400–800; (d) for kitchen range hoods: additional consideration — hood width ≥ cooktop width, mounting height 600–750mm above cooktop, duct run to exterior (maximum 3m with 1 elbow, or upgrade to higher CMH for longer runs); (e) system shows top 3 fan model recommendations with: brand, model, rated CMH, duct diameter, noise level (sones), power consumption (watts), price | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Duct & Accessories Specification**: System generates complete material list: (a) exhaust fan unit (recommended model); (b) ducting — rigid aluminum duct (preferred) or flexible aluminum duct, diameter per step 2, length = distance from fan to exterior wall/roof vent + 0.5m contingency; (c) exterior wall vent/roof cap with backdraft damper (prevents outside air entry when fan is off); (d) duct tape or clamps for connections; (e) wall/ceiling mounting hardware; (f) exterior louver/grille (aesthetic cover); (g) for new wall penetration in CHB: core drilling service recommendation per W138 (installation services) — typical cost PHP 500–1,500 per hole; (h) optional upgrades: speed controller, humidity sensor, timer switch | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate Generation & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates estimate with: room ventilation calculation (volume, ACH, CMH), recommended fan with specifications, complete duct and accessory list, total cost, estimated installation time (DIY: 1–3 hours, professional: 1–2 hours); (b) offer installation service booking per W138; (c) estimate saved and convertible per W542 | Sales Associate | Home Appliances Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Ventilation sizing calculator engine — room volume, ACH, CMH
- Product master (W252) — fan models with CMH ratings, duct specifications
- Real-time inventory (W533)
- POS quotation (W542), installation services (W138)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Duct run length impact**: Each 1m of duct and each 90° elbow reduces effective CMH by 5–10%; calculator may under-recommend for long/complex duct runs; add 20% CMH margin for runs >3m or >2 elbows

### Staffing Implication
- No permanent incremental headcount; ~30 min/day of Sales Associate time per store

### Time Estimate
- Total per consultation: 8–14 min (average ~10 min)
