## W1054. Store-Level Customer Wire & Cable Cut-to-Length Spool Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests specific length of electrical wire or cable (shorter than full roll) |
| **Frequency** | ~6,000–8,000 cut-to-length requests/month across all stores (electrical category: 10% of SKUs, ~3,500 items; wire/cable is the highest-volume electrical SKU by linear meters sold) |
| **Volume** | 1–5 cuts per customer visit |
| **Owner** | Electrical Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Electrical Section), Customer |

### Background

Electrical wire and cable are sold in standard rolls (100m for THHN/THWN building wire, 50m for larger gauges, 305m/1000ft boxes for NM-B romex equivalent) at BuildRight Depot. Filipino electricians and DIY homeowners frequently need specific shorter lengths: (a) 3m of 12 AWG wire for a single outlet installation; (b) 10m of 10 AWG wire for an aircon circuit; (c) 5m of 14 AWG wire for a lighting circuit; (d) 2m of #8 AWG wire for a grounding electrode conductor. Purchasing a full 100m roll for a 5m need wastes ~PHP 1,500–3,000 (customer pays for 95m of unused wire). Conversely, some customers purchase pre-cut lengths from smaller hardware stores at inflated per-meter prices (often 2–3× the per-meter price of a full roll). BuildRight's cut-to-length service offers the optimal middle ground: customers purchase exactly the length they need at a per-meter price that is competitive with full-roll per-meter rates plus a small cutting service fee. This service: (a) reduces customer purchase barriers for small projects; (b) reduces wire waste; (c) increases foot traffic from small-project customers who would otherwise go to neighborhood hardware stores (sari-sari stores with limited wire selection). Wire types commonly requested: THHN/THWN solid and stranded (14 AWG, 12 AWG, 10 AWG, 8 AWG, 6 AWG), flat cord (2-wire, 3-wire), extension cord wire, speaker wire, coaxial cable, CAT6 LAN cable, and automotive wire. This is distinct from W463 (catch-weight & cut-to-length processing) which covers the general inventory management of variable-length items; this workflow is the customer-facing service process for wire cutting specifically.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Requirement Intake**: Sales Associate gathers wire/cable specifications: (a) wire type — THHN/THWN building wire, flat cord, extension cord wire, speaker wire, coaxial (RG-6/RG-59), CAT6 LAN cable, automotive wire, welding cable; (b) wire gauge/size — AWG size (14, 12, 10, 8, 6) or mm² (2.0mm², 3.5mm², 5.5mm², 8.0mm², 14mm², 22mm²); (c) conductor type — solid or stranded; (d) insulation color (for building wire: black, white, green/bare, red, blue, yellow per standard color coding); (e) required length in meters; (f) number of conductors needed (e.g., for a single-phase circuit: 1 black + 1 white + 1 green = 3 conductors, each × circuit length); (g) application — outlet wiring, lighting circuit, aircon circuit, subpanel feeder, grounding, data/communications | Sales Associate | Electrical Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **Inventory Check & Pricing**: (a) system checks real-time inventory (W533) for the requested wire type/gauge/color in full-roll stock; (b) if full roll available: system calculates cut-to-length price = (per-meter price from full roll) × length requested + cutting service fee (PHP 10–20 per cut, waived for purchases >PHP 300); (c) system displays per-meter price and total cost for customer confirmation; (d) if insufficient remaining length on open roll, system checks for additional rolls in stock or at nearby stores per W214; (e) system validates remaining length on open spool — if customer request would leave <5m on the spool, offer the remaining full length at a discount to avoid small unusable offcuts | System / Sales Associate | Electrical Department Supervisor | 1–2 min |
| 3 | **Cutting Execution**: Sales Associate performs wire cutting at dedicated electrical cutting station: (a) select correct wire roll from spool rack (verified by type, gauge, color, and lot/batch number per W3 inventory procedures); (b) measure required length using calibrated measuring tape or the cutting station's built-in meter counter; (c) mark cut point; (d) cut wire cleanly using wire cutter/cable snips (for wire ≤10 AWG) or cable cutter (for wire ≥8 AWG); (e) for cuts >20m: unroll from spool rack along the floor measuring path (most stores have a 10m measuring lane marked on the floor near the electrical section); (f) verify cut length within ±0.1m tolerance; (g) strip 10mm of insulation from both ends to verify conductor quality (no oxidation, correct stranding); (h) coil cut length neatly and secure with wire tie or tape; (i) label with wire type, gauge, length, and per-meter price on tag; (j) system decrements inventory from spool roll (partial unit deduction per catch-weight logic W463) | Sales Associate | Electrical Department Supervisor | 3–10 min (depending on length; longer lengths require floor unrolling) |
| 4 | **Transaction Processing**: (a) system generates line item for cut wire: SKU, type, gauge, color, length (m), per-meter price, total price, cutting service fee (if applicable); (b) customer pays at POS per W5B (in-store selling) or W542 (quotation conversion); (c) system updates spool remaining length in inventory; (d) if spool remaining length reaches zero, system auto-generates replenishment suggestion per W2A (auto-replenishment) | POS Cashier / System | Electrical Department Supervisor | 2–3 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Wire/cable product master (W252) — wire specifications, per-meter pricing
- Real-time inventory (W533) — spool remaining length tracking
- Catch-weight/partial unit inventory management (W463) — partial roll deduction
- POS service item processing (W544) — cutting service fee
- Auto-replenishment (W2A) — spool reorder trigger at minimum threshold

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Spool remaining length accuracy**: Manual measurement errors accumulate; weekly spool reconciliation (physical measurement of remaining length) required to maintain inventory accuracy per INV-001
- **Customer length disputes**: Customer claims cut length is shorter than requested; mitigate with length verification at cutting station before handoff and printed length on price tag
- **Wire tangle during long cuts**: Unrolling >20m of wire from spool can cause tangling and kinking; require two-person operation for cuts >30m (one unrolls, one manages slack)
- **Safety — cutting live wire risk**: Ensure all wire is de-energized and not connected to any power source; post safety notice at cutting station

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Electrical Section)**: Each cut-to-length request takes 5–15 min; at 30–40 requests per store per day, this represents ~4–8 hours/day; absorbed by existing electrical section staff (typically 2–3 Sales Associates assigned to electrical at any time)
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Requirement intake: 3–5 min
- Inventory check & pricing: 1–2 min
- Cutting execution: 3–10 min
- Transaction processing: 2–3 min
- **Total per customer**: 9–20 min (average ~12 min)

## W1055. Customer Water Filtration & Purification System Sizing for Residential & Commercial

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests water filtration/purification system recommendation for residential or commercial application |
| **Frequency** | ~1,500–2,500 consultations/month across all stores (plumbing category: 12% of SKUs; water filtration is a growing sub-category driven by Philippine water quality concerns) |
| **Volume** | 1 system sizing per consultation |
| **Owner** | Plumbing Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Plumbing Section), Customer |

### Background

Water quality is a significant concern in the Philippines. According to the Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS), ~15% of the Philippine population lacks access to safely managed drinking water. Even in urban areas served by water utilities (Manila Water, Maynilad, local water districts), tap water quality varies and many households use point-of-use filtration. The Philippine water filtration market includes: (a) sediment filters (remove particulates — essential for most Philippine water supplies); (b) carbon filters (remove chlorine, taste, odor, and some organics); (c) UV sterilizers (kill bacteria and viruses — important for areas with intermittent water supply where pipe contamination occurs); (d) reverse osmosis (RO) systems (remove dissolved solids, heavy metals, fluoride — for areas with high TDS or well water); (e) water softeners (for areas with hard water, especially in limestone regions like Cebu, Cavite, and parts of Palawan). BuildRight Depot sells complete filtration systems (under-sink, countertop, whole-house) and individual components (filter housings, cartridges, UV lamps, RO membranes, fittings). Customers frequently purchase the wrong system because they don't know their water quality parameters (TDS level, hardness, chlorine content) or flow rate requirements. This consultative service matches system specifications to customer needs.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Water Quality & Usage Assessment**: Sales Associate gathers water source and usage information: (a) water source — municipal/city water district, deep well, shallow well, rainwater, community water system; (b) known water quality issues — sediment/cloudiness, chlorine taste/smell, hardness (scale buildup on fixtures), staining (iron/manganese — brown/orange), TDS (total dissolved solids — if customer has TDS meter reading), bacterial contamination (if known); (c) household size — number of persons (determines daily water demand); (d) filtration points — point-of-use (under-sink for drinking/cooking only), point-of-entry (whole-house for all taps); (e) installation location — under kitchen sink, outside house, garage/utility room; (f) budget range; (g) if customer is uncertain about water quality, recommend water testing kit (BuildRight stocks DIY test kits for pH, TDS, hardness, iron) or local water testing laboratory referral | Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **System Type Recommendation**: System recommends filtration stages based on water quality assessment: (a) **Municipal water (typical quality)**: 3-stage under-sink system — (1) 5-micron sediment filter → (2) granular activated carbon (GAC) filter → (3) 1-micron carbon block filter; adequate for most Manila Water/Maynilad supplied areas; (b) **Municipal water with intermittent supply** (pressure fluctuations cause pipe contamination): 3-stage + UV sterilizer — add UV lamp (typically 11W or 24W depending on flow rate) after carbon filtration; (c) **Well water (high TDS, possible contamination)**: 5-stage RO system — (1) sediment → (2) carbon → (3) carbon block → (4) RO membrane (50–100 GPD) → (5) post-carbon polishing filter; plus UV for bacterial safety; (d) **Hard water** (scale buildup): water softener before filtration — ion exchange resin tank sized to household daily consumption and grain hardness; (e) **Whole-house system**: point-of-entry (POE) — larger filter housings (20" big blue) with sediment + carbon stages, sized to household peak flow rate (typical: 15–30 liters/min for 3–5 person household) | System / Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Component Specification & Sizing**: System generates bill of materials for recommended system: (a) filter housings — number of stages × housing size (10" standard for under-sink, 20" big blue for POE); (b) filter cartridges per stage — type, micron rating, replacement interval (sediment: 3–6 months, carbon: 6–12 months, RO membrane: 2–3 years); (c) UV sterilizer unit — wattage (11W for under-sink, 24W–40W for whole-house), replacement lamp interval: 12 months; (d) RO system components — booster pump (if inlet pressure <40 PSI), storage tank (3.2G or 10G), faucet; (e) water softener — resin tank size (1 cu.ft. for typical household), brine tank, control valve; (f) pipework and fittings — 1/4" tubing for under-sink RO, 1/2" or 3/4" pipe for POE; (g) installation accessories — mounting bracket, ball valves (inlet/outlet isolation), pressure gauge, TDS meter (for RO systems); (h) system calculates total cost and annual maintenance cost (replacement cartridges and UV lamp) | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate Generation & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates estimate with: water quality assessment summary, recommended system diagram, bill of materials, total cost, annual maintenance schedule with replacement costs, estimated filter life based on household consumption; (b) offer installation service per W138; (c) offer annual filter replacement subscription reminder (SMS notification when filter replacement is due based on purchase date + estimated life); (d) estimate saved per W542 | Sales Associate | Plumbing Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Water filtration system recommendation engine — water quality mapping to filtration stages
- Product master (W252) — filter specifications, cartridge compatibility, pricing
- Real-time inventory (W533)
- POS quotation (W542), installation services (W138)
- Customer notification engine — annual filter replacement reminders

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Water quality variability**: Without actual water test results, recommendations are based on typical source quality; actual conditions may differ; recommend DIY test kit before system purchase for >PHP 5,000 systems
- **Maintenance compliance**: Filters that are not replaced on schedule become breeding grounds for bacteria; system should send proactive replacement reminders

### Staffing Implication
- No permanent incremental headcount; ~1–2 hours/week of Sales Associate time per store

### Time Estimate
- Total per consultation: 11–18 min (average ~14 min)

## W1056. Store-Level Customer Construction Permit Advisory & Municipal Building Requirements Guidance

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer asks about construction permit requirements during building materials consultation |
| **Frequency** | ~3,000–5,000 advisory interactions/month across all stores |
| **Volume** | 1 advisory session per customer (often in conjunction with a materials estimation service) |
| **Owner** | Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Building Materials Section), Customer |

### Background

Philippine construction is governed by the National Building Code (PD 1096), the Fire Code (RA 9514), and local government unit (LGU) ordinances that impose additional requirements. Common permits and clearances required for residential and small commercial construction include: (a) Building Permit from the LGU Office of the Building Official (OBO); (b) Electrical Permit (separate from building permit in most LGUs); (c) Plumbing Permit; (d) Zoning Clearance from the LGU Zoning Administrator; (e) Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) from BFP per W476; (f) Environmental Compliance Certificate (ECC) or Certificate of Non-Coverage (CNC) from DENR-EMB for larger projects; (g) LGU Barangay Clearance; (h) DPWH clearance for projects near national roads; (i) Homeowners' Association (HOA) approval for subdivision lots; (j) Local water district connection permit; (k) Net-Metering application with the local electric cooperative/DUERC for solar installations. Filipino homeowners — particularly DIY renovators and first-time builders — are frequently unaware of permit requirements and begin construction without permits, risking: (i) stop-work order from the OBO; (ii) fines (typically 2× the permit fee); (iii) inability to obtain occupancy permit; (iv) insurance claim denial for unpermitted structures; (v) difficulty selling the property in the future. BuildRight Depot's advisory service does not provide legal or engineering advice but offers a structured information guide that helps customers understand the permit landscape for their project type. This builds customer trust, positions BuildRight as a knowledgeable partner, and often leads to larger material purchases as customers build with proper permits and higher-quality standards.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Classification**: Sales Associate identifies the customer's project type: (a) new residential construction (single-family, 1–3 stories); (b) residential renovation/remodel (interior, exterior, extension/addition); (c) small commercial construction (store, warehouse, workshop); (d) fence/wall construction; (e) swimming pool; (f) solar panel installation; (g) electrical upgrade (panel replacement, additional circuits); (h) plumbing modification (new bathroom, septic tank); (i) other. System displays the general permit requirements for the identified project type based on the customer's LGU jurisdiction (per W310 address hierarchy and LGU database) | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 2–3 min |
| 2 | **Permit Requirements Information Guide**: System generates a printable permit requirements guide for the customer's project type and LGU: (a) **New Residential Construction**: (i) Building Permit: signed and sealed plans by licensed architect and structural engineer, barangay clearance, tax declaration, vicinity map, fire safety plan (for ≥2 stories); (ii) Electrical Permit: electrical plan signed by licensed Professional Electrical Engineer (PEE); (iii) Plumbing Permit: plumbing plan signed by licensed Master Plumber; (iv) Zoning Clearance; (v) BFP FSIC (for ≥2 stories or commercial); (vi) typical permit processing time: 10–30 business days per LGU; (vii) typical permit cost: 0.5–1% of estimated construction cost; (b) **Renovation/Remodel**: (i) Building Permit may or may not be required depending on scope — structural changes, additional floor, or change of occupancy always require permit; cosmetic changes (painting, flooring, cabinets) typically do not; (ii) Electrical/Plumbing permits for any modification to existing systems; (c) **Fence/Wall**: (i) Building Permit typically required for fences >1.80m height per PD 1096; (ii) Barangay clearance; (d) **Solar Installation**: (i) Electrical Permit from LGU; (ii) Net-Metering application with local distribution utility (DU/EC); (iii) structural clearance if roof-mounted (additional dead load and wind load); (e) **Common LGU-Specific Additions**: (i) Cebu City: Additional Green Building compliance per local ordinance; (ii) Davao City: Rainwater collection system per Davao City ordinance; (iii) Quezon City: Green Building Code compliance for ≥10,000 sqm; (iv) system notes: "Requirements shown are general guidance only. Contact your LGU Office of the Building Official (OBO) for the specific and current requirements for your project" | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated generation) |
| 3 | **Professional Referral & Guidance**: (a) system provides referral list for professional services: (i) Licensed architects and civil engineers (from BuildRight's contractor referral database per W904); (ii) Licensed electricians and plumbers; (iii) BFP-accredited fire safety service providers (for fire safety plans); (b) system prints "Next Steps" checklist: (i) Contact LGU OBO for current requirements and fees; (ii) Engage licensed architect/engineer for plans and specifications; (iii) Obtain barangay clearance; (iv) Submit permit application; (v) Upon permit approval, return to BuildRight for materials quotation per W542 or W162; (c) system offers to save the requirements guide to customer's loyalty account for future reference | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 4 | **Materials Estimation Integration**: (a) if customer has their building plan and material specifications, Sales Associate can proceed to materials estimation services: W1044 (concrete calculator), W1043 (paint calculator), W1050 (staircase calculator), W983 (roofing calculator), W989 (plumbing layout), W991 (electrical circuit design); (b) if customer has a contractor, offer to send the requirements guide to their contractor via email/SMS for coordination; (c) if customer's project is a B2B trade/corporate account, refer to pro desk per W112 for full project quotation per W162 | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 2–5 min (optional continuation) |

### System Touchpoints
- Permit requirements database — project-type-to-permit mapping with LGU-specific variations
- LGU database per W310 (address & geographic hierarchy) — jurisdiction lookup
- Contractor referral module (W904) — professional service referrals
- Loyalty account (W17) — saved permit guides
- Materials estimation service modules — W1043, W1044, W1050, W983, W989, W991
- B2B quotation module (W162) — trade account project quotes
- Pro desk scheduling (W895) — professional service appointments

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Legal liability disclaimer**: BuildRight is not a licensed engineering, architectural, or legal advisory firm; all permit information must carry prominent disclaimer: "This information is provided as general guidance only and does not constitute legal, engineering, or architectural advice. Requirements vary by LGU and may change. Always verify with your local Office of the Building Official (OBO) and licensed professionals."
- **LGU requirement variability**: Philippine LGUs have widely varying permit requirements and processing times; the system cannot guarantee accuracy for every LGU; database must be reviewed and updated annually per W657 (regulatory change management)
- **Scope creep risk**: Customers may expect BuildRight staff to assist with permit applications, plan preparation, or LGU interactions; staff must clearly communicate that BuildRight provides information guidance only, not permit facilitation services

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Building Materials)**: Advisory session adds 5–10 min; most sessions are embedded within existing materials consultation; incremental time burden: ~1–2 hours/week per store
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Project classification: 2–3 min
- Permit requirements guide: 1–2 min (automated)
- Professional referral & guidance: 3–5 min
- Materials integration (optional): 2–5 min
- **Total per advisory session**: 8–15 min (average ~10 min)

## W1057. Customer Insulation Material Calculator (Wall, Ceiling, Roof Thermal & Acoustic)

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests insulation quantity estimate for residential or small commercial building project |
| **Frequency** | ~600–1,000 consultations/month across all stores (insulation is a growing category driven by Philippine energy efficiency awareness and Green Building Code adoption) |
| **Volume** | 1 calculation per project |
| **Owner** | Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Building Materials Section), Customer |

### Background

Thermal and acoustic insulation is an emerging category in Philippine construction, historically underutilized due to the perception that Philippine tropical climate does not require insulation. However, the growing adoption of air conditioning (penetration rate: ~60% of Philippine households, rising to ~80% in urban areas) and increasing electricity costs (PHP 10–12/kWh residential rate) have created demand for insulation that reduces cooling energy consumption by 20–40%. Additionally, acoustic insulation is increasingly requested for: (a) condominiums and townhouses (shared walls); (b) home theaters and entertainment rooms; (c) bedrooms adjacent to noisy streets; (d) office meeting rooms. BuildRight Depot carries: (a) fiberglass blanket/batt insulation (R-11 to R-30, widths 400mm and 600mm); (b) rigid foam board insulation (polystyrene EPS/XPS, polyurethane PIR, 25mm–100mm thickness); (c) reflective foil insulation (radiant barrier for roof/attic applications); (d) rock wool insulation (fire-rated and acoustic, 50mm–100mm thickness); (e) spray foam insulation kits (for gap/void filling). This calculator helps customers determine the correct insulation material, thickness/R-value, and quantity for their specific application.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Application & Climate Assessment**: Sales Associate gathers project parameters: (a) insulation application — exterior wall, interior partition wall, ceiling (below attic), attic floor, roof (under-roof/above-ceiling), floor (above crawl space), acoustic partition; (b) building type — single-family detached, townhouse/rowhouse (shared wall), condominium, commercial; (c) air-conditioned spaces — yes/no (determines thermal insulation value); (d) climate zone — based on customer's location per W310 (Philippine climate zones: Type I — two pronounced seasons, Type II — no dry season, Type III — dry season short, Type IV — rainfall evenly distributed); (e) objective — thermal (reduce cooling cost), acoustic (noise reduction), both thermal and acoustic, fire-rated (compartmentalization); (f) wall construction — CHB (hollow block) with furring, wood frame, steel frame, concrete solid; (g) available cavity depth — determines maximum insulation thickness | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **R-Value & Material Recommendation**: System recommends insulation material and thickness: (a) **Thermal — exterior wall**: recommended R-value R-13 to R-19 for Philippine climate (lower than temperate countries due to smaller indoor-outdoor temperature differential); fiberglass batt R-13 (89mm) or R-19 (152mm) for framed walls; rigid foam board 50mm–75mm for CHB furred walls; (b) **Thermal — ceiling/roof (most impactful application in Philippines)**: recommended R-30 (241mm fiberglass) or equivalent in rigid board + radiant barrier for attic/roof applications; radiant barrier alone reduces radiant heat gain by 25–40% in Philippine metal roof installations; (c) **Acoustic — interior partition**: rock wool 50mm (STC 45–50) or fiberglass batt 89mm (STC 38–43) with resilient channel; (d) **Fire-rated partition**: rock wool 50mm–100mm (fire rating 1–2 hours) per BFP requirement per W476; (e) system recommends material based on: application, available cavity depth, objective (thermal/acoustic/fire), and budget | System / Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Area & Quantity Calculation**: System calculates insulation quantities: (a) total wall/ceiling/roof area = length × height (for walls) or length × width (for ceilings/roofs), minus deductions (windows, doors, openings); (b) for batt/blanket insulation: number of rolls = total area ÷ coverage per roll (product-specific, e.g., 11.6 m² per roll for 400mm × 6m batt), rounded up; (c) for rigid board insulation: number of boards = total area ÷ area per board (standard: 1.2m × 2.4m = 2.88 m² per board), rounded up; (d) for radiant barrier (roof): linear meters = roof ridge length × 1.15 (waste factor for overlapping joints), width per roll (typically 1.2m or 1.5m); (e) companion materials: (i) vapor barrier (polyethylene sheeting, 0.15mm, for warm-humid climate — install on exterior side of insulation), (ii) insulation supports/wire rods (for ceiling applications, @ 600mm O.C.), (iii) reflective tape for radiant barrier joints, (iv) sealant/caulk for gap sealing, (v) protective equipment: gloves, long-sleeve shirt, dust mask (for fiberglass per W172 PPE requirements) | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate Generation & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates estimate with: application summary, recommended R-value and material, area calculation, complete bill of materials, total cost, energy savings estimate (for thermal applications: "Estimated cooling cost reduction: 20–30% for ceiling insulation, 10–15% for wall insulation"), installation overview; (b) check inventory per W533; (c) offer installation referral per W138/W904; (d) estimate saved per W542 | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Insulation calculator engine — R-value recommendation, area calculation, material selection
- Product master (W252) — insulation specifications, R-values per thickness, coverage per unit
- Real-time inventory (W533)
- POS quotation (W542), installation services (W138), contractor referral (W904)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Vapor barrier positioning**: In Philippine warm-humid climate, vapor barriers must be on the warm (exterior) side of the insulation to prevent condensation within the wall cavity; incorrect placement causes mold and rot; installation instructions must clearly specify this
- **Fire safety for rigid foam**: Polystyrene (EPS/XPS) insulation is combustible and must be covered with a thermal barrier (gypsum board minimum 12mm) when used in habitable spaces per PD 1096; system must display fire safety warning

### Staffing Implication
- No permanent incremental headcount; ~30 min/day of Sales Associate time per store

### Time Estimate
- Total per consultation: 9–15 min (average ~12 min)

## W1059. Customer Kitchen Countertop Measurement & Custom Fabrication Order Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests custom kitchen countertop or bathroom vanity top measurement and fabrication |
| **Frequency** | ~1,500–2,500 orders/month across all stores (home décor & furniture: 5% of SKUs; countertops are high-value items: PHP 3,000–30,000 per project) |
| **Volume** | 1 countertop per order (may include multiple sections for L-shaped or U-shaped kitchens) |
| **Owner** | Home Décor & Furniture Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Home Décor Section), Special Order Coordinator, Fabrication Partner, Customer |

### Background

Kitchen countertops and bathroom vanity tops are among the highest-value individual items in home improvement, with Filipino homeowners investing PHP 3,000–30,000 per project depending on material and size. BuildRight Depot offers countertop materials including: (a) prefabricated granite slabs (standard sizes: 600mm × 2.0m, 600mm × 2.4m, 600mm × 3.0m) — PHP 2,000–5,000 per piece; (b) prefabricated quartz/engineered stone — PHP 4,000–10,000 per piece; (c) laminate countertop boards (post-formed, standard 600mm × 2.4m) — PHP 1,500–4,000 per piece; (d) solid surface (acrylic) — PHP 5,000–15,000 per piece; (e) tile-on-concrete (DIY — customer buys tiles per W963 and cement board). Philippine residential kitchen layouts are predominantly: (a) straight/linear (1.2m–2.4m); (b) L-shaped (2 legs, each 1.2m–2.4m); (c) U-shaped (3 sides); (d) galley (2 parallel runs). Standard counter depth is 600mm (24 inches). Unlike flat boards that can be cut on-site, granite and quartz countertops require professional fabrication (cutting, edge profiling, sink cutout, polishing) using specialized wet-saw and CNC equipment. BuildRight coordinates fabrication through partnered stone fabricators (not in-store capability). This workflow covers measurement, specification, custom order placement, and delivery/installation coordination. It is distinct from W1046 (door & window custom orders) which covers different product categories; this workflow addresses countertop-specific measurement and fabrication requirements.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Kitchen/Bathroom Layout Assessment**: Sales Associate gathers project details: (a) room type — kitchen countertop, bathroom vanity top, laundry countertop, bar/counter; (b) layout shape — straight, L-shaped, U-shaped, galley, custom; (c) existing or planned cabinet dimensions — cabinet length along wall for each section; (d) counter depth — standard 600mm or custom; (e) edge profile preference — flat/eased, beveled, bullnose, half-bullnose, ogee; (f) sink type — undermount (requires sink cutout in slab), drop-in (self-rimming, no slab cutout), farmhouse/apron front (large front cutout); (g) faucet holes — number and location (1-hole, 3-hole, 4-inch spread, 8-inch spread); (h) backsplash — matching material splash (100mm or 150mm height), tile backsplash (separate per W963), or none; (i) material preference and budget | Sales Associate | Home Décor & Furniture Dept Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 2 | **Measurement Verification & Template Requirement**: (a) if customer provides measurements: system validates dimensions for reasonableness (typical Philippine kitchen counter lengths: 1.2m–3.6m per section; standard depth: 600mm; typical vanity: 0.6m–1.2m × 0.5m depth); (b) if customer does not have measurements: system offers two options: (i) customer takes measurements at home using provided measurement worksheet (printable from system — wall-to-wall length, depth, corner angles, sink opening dimensions, cutouts for stove/range); (ii) on-site measurement service per W442 (site technical survey & measurement services) with service fee (PHP 500–1,000, waived for orders >PHP 10,000); (c) for natural stone (granite, marble): system recommends on-site templating by fabricator before cutting — natural stone slabs vary in pattern and color, and site conditions may require field adjustments; (d) system creates custom specification record with all dimensions and preferences | Sales Associate / Special Order Coordinator | Home Décor & Furniture Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 3 | **Material Selection, Pricing & Order Placement**: (a) system displays material options within customer's budget: granite (PHP 3,000–8,000 per linear meter installed), quartz (PHP 5,000–15,000 per linear meter installed), laminate (PHP 1,500–4,000 per linear meter, DIY install), solid surface (PHP 6,000–20,000 per linear meter installed); (b) system calculates total cost: (i) material cost = length × per-linear-meter rate (including waste factor: 10% for straight layouts, 15–20% for L/U-shaped to account for seaming and waste at corners); (ii) fabrication cost = edge profiling (per linear meter) + sink cutout (per cutout) + faucet holes (per hole) + seaming (per joint, if multiple pieces needed); (iii) installation cost = per-linear-meter installation rate (if professional install requested per W138); (iv) delivery cost = bulky item delivery fee per W5D; (c) system generates custom order quote with 50% deposit requirement per W546; (d) customer approves quote and pays deposit at POS; (e) system transmits order to fabrication partner per W866 (vendor portal — custom order); (f) estimated lead time: laminate (3–5 days), granite/quartz fabrication (7–14 days), solid surface (10–21 days) | Sales Associate / System | Home Décor & Furniture Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 4 | **Fabrication, Delivery & Installation Coordination**: (a) fabrication partner manufactures countertop per specification; (b) if natural stone: fabricator performs on-site templating before cutting (arranges directly with customer); (c) upon fabrication completion, fabricator notifies BuildRight with ready date and weight/dimensions; (d) system sends delivery scheduling notification to customer; (e) customer selects delivery date; (f) for granite/quartz (heavy, fragile): system requires professional delivery per partnered logistics provider per W268 (last-mile delivery tracking); (g) if professional installation requested: system coordinates installation appointment per W138 (home installation services) — installer delivers and installs in one visit; (h) remaining 50% balance collected upon delivery/installation completion; (i) system closes custom order and logs vendor fabrication lead time for vendor scorecard per W44 | Special Order Coordinator / Fabrication Partner / Delivery Coordinator | Home Décor & Furniture Dept Supervisor | 10–15 min (coordination per order) |

### System Touchpoints
- Countertop specification module — layout input, material selection, pricing
- Custom order module (W545) — fabrication specification, vendor order
- Deposit collection (W546) — 50% upfront, 50% on completion
- Vendor portal (W866) — custom order transmission to fabricator
- Site measurement service (W442) — on-site measurement coordination
- Home installation service (W138) — installation booking
- Home delivery scheduling (W5D) — bulky item delivery
- Last-mile delivery tracking (W268) — professional delivery coordination
- Vendor scorecard (W44) — fabrication lead time and quality tracking

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Measurement error liability**: Incorrect measurements result in countertops that don't fit — granite/quartz cuts cannot be easily modified; on-site templating by fabricator (step 4b) mitigates this for natural stone; for laminate (cut on-site), risk is lower
- **Color variation in natural stone**: Granite slab samples in-store may not match the actual slab used for fabrication; recommend customer visits fabricator's warehouse to select specific slab before cutting
- **Fragility during transport**: Granite and quartz countertops are brittle and crack if transported incorrectly (must be transported vertically, never flat); delivery partner must comply with handling standards
- **Long lead times**: 7–21 days for fabrication may lose customer to competitors who stock prefabricated standard sizes; offer prefabricated granite options (600mm × 2.0m with pre-finished edges) for immediate purchase to serve customers who cannot wait

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Home Décor)**: Consultation adds 15–25 min per customer; at 8–12 consultations per store per week, this represents ~2–5 hours/week
- **Special Order Coordinator**: Manages ~20–40 active countertop orders at any time; estimated 1–2 hours/day of coordination; shared with other custom order categories (doors/windows per W1046)
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Layout assessment: 5–10 min
- Measurement verification: 5–8 min
- Material selection & order placement: 5–8 min
- Fabrication/delivery coordination: 10–15 min (per order, spread over days)
- **Sales Associate time per order**: 15–26 min (average ~20 min)

## W1060. Customer Rebar Stirrup, Tying Wire & Binding Material Quantity Estimator Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests rebar accessory quantities (stirrups, tying wire, spacers) for a reinforced concrete project |
| **Frequency** | ~2,500–3,500 consultations/month across all stores (rebar and reinforcing accessories are core items in the lumber & building materials category — 14% of SKUs) |
| **Volume** | 1 estimation per project |
| **Owner** | Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Building Materials Section), Customer |

### Background

Reinforced concrete construction is the dominant building method in the Philippines. Rebar (deformed steel bar) is the skeletal reinforcement inside concrete elements — columns, beams, slabs, and footings. But rebar alone is not sufficient; it must be properly configured with: (a) stirrups (rectangular ties that wrap around the longitudinal rebar in columns and beams, providing shear reinforcement and confinement — typically 10mm bar bent into rectangles at 100–200mm spacing per structural engineer's specification); (b) tying wire (annealed black wire, typically 16-gauge, used to tie intersections of longitudinal bars and stirrups — consumes 1.0–1.5 kg per 100 kg of rebar); (c) concrete spacers/cover blocks (maintain specified concrete cover between rebar and formwork surface — typically 40mm for interior exposure, 50mm for exterior exposure per Philippine structural code); (d) mechanical couplers (for splicing rebar where lap splicing is impractical — higher-value item at PHP 50–200 per coupler). Filipino contractors and foremen routinely underestimate tying wire and stirrup quantities, leading to work stoppages and mid-project store runs. This estimator service provides precise quantities for all rebar accessories based on the structural element dimensions and rebar configuration, bundled with the rebar cutting/bending service per W986.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Structural Element & Rebar Configuration Input**: Sales Associate gathers project parameters: (a) structural element type — column, beam, slab, footing, retaining wall; (b) element dimensions — (i) column: width × depth × height; (ii) beam: width × depth × length; (iii) slab: length × width × thickness; (iv) footing: length × width × depth; (c) longitudinal rebar — diameter (10mm, 12mm, 16mm, 20mm, 25mm) and number of bars per element (typical: 4–8 bars per column, 4–6 bars per beam); (d) stirrup/tie bar diameter (typically 10mm for columns, 8–10mm for beams); (e) stirrup spacing per engineer's specification (typical: 100mm at ends/ joints, 200mm at midspan — or uniform 150mm for simple residential); (f) concrete cover (typical: 40mm interior, 50mm exterior); (g) if customer has structural plan: system accepts direct input of bar schedule (diameter, number, length, bending schedule) — provides the most accurate estimation | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Stirrup Quantity & Cutting Schedule Calculation**: System computes stirrup requirements: (a) stirrup perimeter per piece: for rectangular column/beam stirrup = 2 × (width − 2 × cover) + 2 × (depth − 2 × cover) + hook length (typically 75mm × 2 hooks); (b) stirrup length per piece = perimeter (including hooks); (c) number of stirrups = element length ÷ stirrup spacing + 1 (first stirrup at 50mm from end); (d) total stirrup bar length = number of stirrups × length per piece; (e) system converts to number of 6m standard bars: total stirrup bar length ÷ 6m, rounded up; (f) system generates cutting schedule for in-store rebar cutting/bending per W986: piece number, stirrup dimensions (inside width × inside depth), bend angle (90° × 4 corners), hook length, quantity; (g) for circular columns: stirrup perimeter = π × (diameter − 2 × cover) + overlap (typically 300mm for lap splice) | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Tying Wire, Spacer & Accessory Calculation**: System computes accessory quantities: (a) **Tying wire**: (i) total rebar weight (longitudinal bars + stirrups) = number of bars × length × weight per meter (per diameter); (ii) tying wire quantity = total rebar weight × 0.015 (1.5 kg wire per 100 kg rebar); (iii) sold in 1 kg coils — round up to nearest coil; (b) **Concrete spacers**: (i) for columns: 4 spacers per stirrup × number of stirrups (to maintain cover on each face); (ii) for beams: 2–4 spacers per stirrup; (iii) for slabs: 1 spacer per m² (distributed on chairs/supports); (iv) sold in bags of 50; (c) **Rebar chairs/supports** (for slab reinforcement): 1 per m² of slab area at the bottom mat; (d) **Mechanical couplers** (if specified by engineer): per bar splice schedule, each coupler replaces 1 lap splice; (e) **Rebar caps** (safety — cover exposed rebar ends per OSHA/DOLE safety per W140): 1 per exposed bar end | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate Generation, Cutting/Bending & Customer Handoff**: (a) system generates comprehensive estimate with: structural element summary, longitudinal rebar schedule (diameter, number, length, weight, cost), stirrup cutting schedule (per piece dimensions, number of pieces, 6m bar consumption, cost), tying wire quantity (kg, cost), spacers and accessories (quantity, cost), total project cost; (b) if customer requests in-store rebar cutting/bending for stirrups: system sends cutting schedule to W986 (rebar cutting & bending service) for execution; (c) for large orders (>500 kg rebar): offer site delivery per W964 (bulk delivery); (d) for trade/corporate accounts: convert to project quote per W162; (e) estimate saved per W542 | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Rebar accessory estimator engine — stirrup geometry, tying wire calculation, spacer quantities
- Rebar cutting/bending service module (W986) — cutting schedule generation
- Product master (W252) — rebar specifications, weight per meter, pricing
- Real-time inventory (W533) — rebar and accessory availability
- Bulk delivery scheduling (W964) — large order delivery
- POS quotation (W542), B2B project quotation (W162)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Structural engineering disclaimer**: Rebar configuration (number of bars, diameter, stirrup spacing) is a structural design decision that must be made by a licensed civil engineer; system must display disclaimer: "Rebar quantities shown are based on customer-provided specifications. BuildRight does not provide structural engineering services. Consult a licensed civil engineer for proper rebar design per NSCP (National Structural Code of the Philippines)."
- **Stirrup bending accuracy**: In-store rebar bending per W986 must match the cutting schedule precisely; tolerance: ±3mm on stirrup inside dimensions; bent stirrups that don't fit around longitudinal bars are unusable

### Staffing Implication
- No permanent incremental headcount; ~2 hours/week of Sales Associate time per store

### Time Estimate
- Input: 5–8 min
- Calculation: 1–2 min (automated)
- Accessories: 1–2 min (automated)
- Estimate & handoff: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 10–17 min (average ~13 min)

## W1061. Customer Tile Grout, Adhesive & Thin-Set Mortar Quantity Calculator Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer purchases tiles or requests tile installation material quantities |
| **Frequency** | ~4,000–6,000 consultations/month across all stores (tiles & flooring: 12% of SKUs, ~4,200 items — this is the natural companion service to W963 tile quantity calculator) |
| **Volume** | 1 calculation per tiling project |
| **Owner** | Tiles & Flooring Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Tiles Section), Customer |

### Background

W963 (Customer Tile & Flooring Quantity Calculator) covers the tile quantity itself but does not address the installation materials — grout, adhesive/thin-set mortar, and related supplies. These installation materials represent 15–25% of the total project cost and are frequently under-purchased because: (a) grout quantity depends on tile size, joint width, and joint depth — not just floor area; (b) thin-set/adhesive quantity depends on trowel notch size (which varies by tile size and type), substrate condition, and tile back texture; (c) different tile materials (ceramic, porcelain, natural stone, mosaic) require different adhesive types (standard thin-set, modified thin-set, epoxy, mastic); (d) Filipino DIY tilers frequently purchase only tiles and a single bag of adhesive, then discover mid-project that they need grout, spacers, waterproofing membrane (for wet areas), and crack isolation membrane — necessitating multiple store visits. This workflow is the direct companion to W963; where W963 calculates tile quantities, this workflow calculates all tile installation material quantities, ensuring the customer purchases everything needed in a single store visit.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Parameter Input (Integration with W963)**: Sales Associate gathers tiling project parameters (or pulls from W963 estimate if already completed): (a) tile type — ceramic, porcelain, natural stone (granite, marble, travertine), mosaic, vinyl tile; (b) tile dimensions — length × width × thickness (mm); (c) total tiled area (m²) from W963 or manual input; (d) application — floor, wall, countertop, backsplash, shower/tub surround (wet area), outdoor; (e) substrate — concrete slab, cement screed, existing tile (re-tiling), plywood, gypsum board (wall tile only); (f) joint width — 2mm (min. for rectified tiles), 3mm (standard for ceramic/porcelain), 5–10mm (for rustic/natural stone); (g) grout type preference — cementitious (standard), epoxy (wet areas/chemical resistance), urethane (stain resistant); (h) adhesive type — pre-mixed mastic (wall tile, dry areas only), standard thin-set mortar (dry-mix, cement-based), modified thin-set (polymer-modified, for porcelain and wet areas), epoxy adhesive (for chemical-resistant/industrial) | Sales Associate | Tiles & Flooring Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **Adhesive/Thin-Set Quantity Calculation**: System computes adhesive quantity: (a) trowel notch size recommended per tile type: (i) tiles ≤100mm × 100mm (mosaic): 6mm V-notch; (ii) tiles 100–300mm: 8mm square-notch; (iii) tiles 300–600mm: 10mm square-notch; (iv) tiles >600mm or natural stone: 12mm square-notch; (b) adhesive coverage rate per trowel notch: 6mm = ~5 m² per 20kg bag; 8mm = ~4 m² per 20kg bag; 10mm = ~3 m² per 20kg bag; 12mm = ~2.5 m² per 20kg bag; (c) adjust for substrate condition: rough/unflat substrate: ×1.3 (additional material to compensate for unevenness); smooth/flat substrate: ×1.0; (d) total adhesive bags = total area ÷ coverage rate × substrate factor, rounded up; (e) for wet areas (shower surround, bathroom floor): add waterproofing membrane quantity = area ÷ coverage per roll (typically 10 m² per 20kg pail of liquid membrane, or 15 m² per roll of sheet membrane) | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Grout Quantity Calculation**: System computes grout quantity: (a) grout volume formula per linear meter of joint: joint depth (mm) × joint width (mm) × 1m ÷ 1,000,000 = m³ per linear meter; (b) joint depth = tile thickness (full depth for full-bed installation; or 2/3 of tile thickness for thin-bed); (c) total joint length (linear meters): (i) for rectangular tiles: total area ÷ tile length + total area ÷ tile width = approximate total joint length; (ii) system adds perimeter joint length (perimeter of tiled area — expansion joint); (d) total grout volume = total joint length × grout volume per linear meter; (e) grout coverage: cementitious grout ≈ 1.6 kg/m³; epoxy grout ≈ 1.8 kg/m³; (f) total grout weight (kg) = total grout volume × density; (g) bags of grout = total weight ÷ bag size (1kg, 2kg, or 5kg), rounded up; (h) for epoxy grout: system calculates Part A (resin) and Part B (hardener) units | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Complete Installation Material List & Estimate**: System generates full bill of materials: (a) **Adhesive/thin-set**: type, number of bags, price; (b) **Grout**: type, color options, number of bags/units, price; (c) **Tile spacers**: 1 bag per 5 m² (bag of 200 pieces); size matches joint width (2mm, 3mm, 5mm); (d) **Waterproofing membrane** (if wet area): type, quantity, price; (e) **Primer** (if needed for modified thin-set on non-porous substrate): 1 liter per 4 m²; (f) **Notched trowel**: 1 per project (size per step 2a); (g) **Grout float**: 1 per project; (h) **Sponge and bucket**: 1 per project (for grout cleanup); (i) **Tile cutter rental**: per W139 (tool rental) or purchase; (j) **Rubber mallet**: 1 per project (for tapping tiles level); (k) **Level** (600mm or 1200mm): 1 per project; (l) **Crack isolation membrane** (optional): for substrates with existing cracks; (m) system calculates total project cost including all materials; (n) system generates estimate per W542 with optional installation referral per W138/W904 | System / Sales Associate | Tiles & Flooring Dept Supervisor | 2–3 min (automated) |

### System Touchpoints
- Tile installation material calculator engine — adhesive, grout, accessories
- Integration with W963 (tile quantity calculator) — pulls tile dimensions and area
- Product master (W252) — adhesive specifications, grout coverage data, pricing
- Real-time inventory (W533)
- POS quotation (W542), tool rental (W139), installation referral (W138/W904)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Substrate condition unknown**: Customer-reported substrate condition may be inaccurate; rough substrates consume 30% more adhesive than estimated; recommend adding 20% adhesive contingency for first-time DIY customers
- **Grout color matching**: Grout color appearance changes after drying; recommend customer purchase a small test quantity first and apply to a few tiles to verify color match before committing to full quantity
- **Epoxy grout difficulty**: Epoxy grout has a short working time (30–45 min in Philippine heat) and is difficult to clean; recommend professional installation per W138 for epoxy grout projects

### Staffing Implication
- No permanent incremental headcount; this service is naturally embedded in tile section consultations (~5 min incremental time per customer)

### Time Estimate
- Parameter input: 3–5 min
- Adhesive calculation: 1–2 min (automated)
- Grout calculation: 1–2 min (automated)
- Complete material list: 2–3 min (automated)
- **Total per consultation**: 7–12 min (average ~9 min) — typically runs in parallel with W963 tile quantity calculation

## W1062. Store-Level Customer Scaffolding Rental, Safety Harness Package & Delivery Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests scaffolding rental for construction, painting, or maintenance project at height |
| **Frequency** | ~800–1,200 rental requests/month across all stores (driven by Philippine construction activity and homeowner renovation projects) |
| **Volume** | 1 rental order per customer project; average 1–3 frame sets per order |
| **Owner** | Lumber & Building Materials Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Building Materials Section), Tool Rental Coordinator, Customer |

### Background

Working at height is a daily reality in Philippine construction — from painting a 3-meter ceiling to building a 2-story house exterior to installing gutters on a roof. Professional scaffolding provides a safe, stable working platform compared to the common Filipino practice of using bamboo scaffolding (which lacks standard load ratings) or improvised platforms (ladders with planks). BuildRight Depot offers scaffolding rental as a value-added service that: (a) drives foot traffic and incremental merchandise sales (customers rent scaffolding + buy paint, tools, materials in the same visit); (b) generates recurring rental revenue (PHP 150–500 per frame set per day, or PHP 800–2,500 per week); (c) promotes workplace safety (DOLE DO 13 — Construction Safety Standards — requires proper scaffolding for work above 3 meters). Rental inventory typically includes: (a) steel frame scaffolding sets (standard frame: 1.7m × 1.2m, cross braces, adjustable base jacks, coupling pins); (b) aluminum scaffolding towers (lightweight, mobile with casters — for indoor painting and ceiling work); (c) ladder jacks and walk planks (for simpler 1-person jobs); (d) safety harnesses and lanyards (rented as a package with scaffolding for elevated work per W172 PPE requirements); (e) hard hats (rented or sold). This is distinct from W139 (tool & equipment rental) which covers general tool rental; this workflow addresses scaffolding-specific rental processes including safety documentation, deposit management, and height-safety compliance.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Height & Scope Assessment**: Sales Associate gathers project requirements: (a) working height — highest point where worker will stand (in meters); (b) project type — interior painting, exterior painting, gutter installation, ceiling installation, wall construction, roof work, general maintenance; (c) working platform needed — number of workers on scaffold simultaneously (typical: 1–2); (d) load requirement — light duty (painting, inspection — 120 kg/m²), medium duty (general construction — 240 kg/m²); (e) site surface — concrete/flat (stable base), soil/unpaved (requires base plates and mudsills), uneven/stepped (requires adjustable jacks); (f) indoor or outdoor (indoor: aluminum mobile tower preferred; outdoor: steel frame with base jacks); (g) rental duration — days or weeks; (h) delivery needed or customer pickup (scaffold frames are bulky — steel frame set ~25 kg per frame; 3-set tower ~100 kg; requires pickup truck or delivery per W5D) | Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Scaffolding Configuration & Safety Package**: System recommends scaffolding configuration: (a) **Number of frame tiers** = working height ÷ frame height (1.7m per tier, minimum 1 tier below working platform); e.g., 4m working height = 3 tiers (1.7 + 1.7 + 1.7 = 5.1m platform height minus safety margin); (b) **Frame sets**: 2 frames per tier × number of tiers; (c) **Cross braces**: 2 per tier × number of tiers; (d) **Base jacks**: 2 (adjustable, for leveling); (e) **Coupling pins**: 2 per tier connection; (f) **Walk planks**: 1–2 per platform level (steel or wood, rated for load); (g) **Guardrails**: top rail (1.0m above platform) + mid-rail (0.5m above platform) per DOLE DO 13 safety standard; (h) **Toe boards**: 150mm minimum height at platform edge per DOLE DO 13; (i) **Safety harness package** (mandatory for work >3m per DOLE): full-body harness + shock-absorbing lanyard + anchor point; (j) **Hard hat**: mandatory per DOLE DO 13 for all construction work; (k) system checks rental inventory availability per store per W533 | System / Sales Associate | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Rental Agreement, Deposit & Safety Waiver**: (a) system generates rental agreement with: rental item list (each frame, brace, jack, plank — serialized with asset tags), daily/weekly rental rate per item, rental duration, total rental cost, replacement cost per item (for damage/loss), deposit amount (typically 50% of replacement cost or PHP 5,000–20,000 depending on configuration); (b) customer signs safety acknowledgment per DOLE DO 13: (i) scaffold must be erected per manufacturer instructions and DOLE standards; (ii) maximum load rating must not be exceeded; (iii) safety harness must be worn and properly anchored at all times when working >3m; (iv) scaffold must be inspected before each use; (v) BuildRight Depot is not liable for injury resulting from improper scaffold erection, overloading, or failure to use safety equipment; (c) system collects deposit at POS per W546 (deposit & progress payment collection) — held as customer deposit per W94; (d) system records rental agreement with customer ID, rental start date, expected return date | Sales Associate / POS Cashier | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 4 | **Delivery (If Requested) & Customer Handoff**: (a) if delivery requested: system schedules delivery per W5D (home delivery scheduling) with bulky item delivery fee; (b) delivery team loads scaffold components and safety equipment; (c) upon delivery, customer or customer's representative signs delivery receipt acknowledging receipt of all items per serialized list; (d) if customer pickup: Sales Associate stages rental items at store loading area per W950 (vehicle loading assistance); (e) customer receives: rental agreement copy, safety instruction sheet, scaffold assembly diagram (manufacturer's instructions), and emergency contact number | Sales Associate / Delivery Coordinator | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 5 | **Return, Inspection & Deposit Refund**: (a) customer returns scaffold components on or before rental end date; (b) Sales Associate inspects each serialized component: (i) frames: no bends, cracks, or weld damage; (ii) cross braces: no bends, locking pins functional; (iii) base jacks: threads functional, no corrosion; (iv) walk planks: no cracks, rot, or excessive wear; (v) safety harness: no cuts, fraying, or chemical damage; webbing intact; (vi) hard hat: no cracks, dents, or UV degradation; (c) system logs return condition per asset tag; (d) if all items returned in good condition: system releases full deposit refund per W101 (customer refund & credit processing); (e) if items damaged or missing: system deducts replacement cost from deposit per rental agreement terms; (f) system calculates final rental charge: (actual rental days × daily rate) or (rental weeks × weekly rate, whichever is lower); (g) system settles: deposit minus (rental charge + any damage deductions); (h) system updates rental asset inventory per W399 and rental equipment maintenance schedule per W650 (warehouse equipment preventive maintenance adapted for rental assets) | Sales Associate / Tool Rental Coordinator | Lumber & Building Materials Dept Supervisor | 10–15 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Scaffolding rental module — configuration engine, inventory tracking, rental agreement
- Product/rental asset master (W252/W399) — serialized rental inventory, replacement costs
- Real-time inventory (W533) — rental availability
- Safety acknowledgment module — DOLE DO 13 compliance documentation
- Customer deposit management (W94) — rental deposit collection and refund
- POS processing (W5B) — rental agreement and deposit transaction
- Home delivery scheduling (W5D) — bulky item delivery
- Vehicle loading assistance (W950) — customer pickup
- Customer refund processing (W101) — deposit refund
- Preventive maintenance scheduling (W650) — rental asset maintenance

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Safety liability**: Scaffolding accidents can cause serious injury or death; rental agreement must include robust liability waiver and safety acknowledgment; all safety instructions must be provided in writing and verbally explained at handoff; per W285 (public liability claims management)
- **Deposit disputes**: Customers dispute damage deductions from deposits; mitigate with pre-rental condition documentation (photos of each serialized component at handoff) and post-return condition photos
- **Non-return / theft**: Customer fails to return rental equipment; deposit may not cover full replacement cost; implement ID verification (government-issued ID photocopy) at rental agreement signing
- **Maintenance between rentals**: Scaffold components that are not inspected and maintained between rentals can fail; implement post-return inspection per step 5 and scheduled maintenance per W650

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Building Materials)**: Rental consultation adds 15–25 min per customer; at 4–6 requests per store per day, this represents ~1–2.5 hours/day
- **Tool Rental Coordinator**: Manages rental inventory, agreements, inspections, and returns; at 4–6 active rentals per store at any time, estimated 1–2 hours/day; shared with tool rental per W139
- **No permanent incremental headcount**; absorbed by existing building materials team

### Time Estimate
- Project assessment: 5–8 min
- Configuration: 2–3 min (automated)
- Rental agreement & deposit: 5–8 min
- Delivery/handoff: 5–10 min
- Return & inspection: 10–15 min
- **Total Sales Associate time per rental**: 27–44 min (average ~35 min, split across rental start and end)

## W1063. Store-Level Customer Welding Gas Cylinder Exchange & Refill Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer presents empty or near-empty welding gas cylinder (acetylene, argon, CO₂, oxygen, or mixed gas) for exchange or refill at store |
| **Frequency** | ~3,000–5,000 cylinder transactions/month across all stores (welding & metal fabrication services are a high-value B2B segment) |
| **Volume** | 1–4 cylinders per customer visit |
| **Owner** | Tools & Hardware Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Tools/Hardware Section), Receiving Clerk, Customer |

### Background

Welding gas cylinder management is a specialized retail operation critical for BuildRight's professional contractor and metal fabricator customer base. The Philippines has a significant welding and metal fabrication industry — from small barangay-level shops to large construction contractors — and welding gas is a recurring consumable. Cylinders are typically supplier-owned (deposit-based) or customer-owned. The key gases sold through BuildRight are: (a) Acetylene (DA — Dissolved Acetylene) for oxy-acetylene cutting and welding; (b) Argon (Ar) for TIG/MIG welding of stainless steel and aluminum; (c) CO₂ and Argon/CO₂ mixes for MIG welding of mild steel; (d) Oxygen (O₂) for oxy-acetylene cutting; (e) Nitrogen (N₂) for pressure testing and pipe purging. Cylinders come in standard Philippine sizes: Size B (1 m³), Size C (2 m³), Size D (5 m³), and Size E (10 m³). The exchange model (return empty, receive full) is the dominant transaction pattern in Philippine retail because it avoids the customer needing to wait for on-site refilling. Safety is paramount — compressed gases are classified as hazardous materials per W236 (hazmat storage) and W698 (SDS management), and cylinders must be inspected for damage, valve integrity, and hydrostatic test date validity before acceptance for exchange.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cylinder Inspection & Acceptance**: Sales Associate inspects the returned empty cylinder: (a) check cylinder body for dents, cracks, arc burns, or corrosion; (b) verify valve is intact and functional (no leaks detected by smell or sound); (c) check hydrostatic test date stamp — Philippine DOE/BFSR requires re-testing every 5 years; cylinders past test date must be rejected and customer directed to supplier for re-certification; (d) verify cylinder type matches gas type (color-coded per Philippine standard: acetylene = maroon, argon = dark green, CO₂ = gray, oxygen = black, nitrogen = black with white shoulder); (e) check for customer-owned vs. supplier-owned cylinder (identified by supplier stamp/label); (f) record cylinder serial number and condition in ERP per W92 (inventory adjustment for cylinder tracking) | Sales Associate | Tools & Hardware Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **Cylinder Exchange Selection & Inventory Check**: System identifies available full cylinders: (a) system queries real-time cylinder inventory (W533) by gas type, size, and supplier; (b) matching: customer receives same gas type and same size as returned cylinder; (c) for supplier-owned cylinders: system verifies supplier name on returned cylinder matches available exchange pool from same supplier; (d) for customer-owned cylinders: system processes as a refill transaction with customer's own cylinder sent to refilling partner; (e) system displays gas type, cylinder size, fill pressure, and exchange/refill price; (f) if out of stock on specific size, system offers alternative nearest-size option or rain check per W772 | Sales Associate / System | Tools & Hardware Dept Supervisor | 2–3 min |
| 3 | **Companion Product Recommendation**: System recommends welding consumables based on gas type: (a) for acetylene/oxygen customers: welding torch tips, filler rods (RA 6013, 7018 electrodes), flux, cutting torch attachments, striker/lighter; (b) for argon customers: TIG filler rods (ER308L, ER70S-6), tungsten electrodes, gas lenses, collet bodies, cup nozzles; (c) for CO₂/mix customers: MIG wire (ER70S-6), contact tips, nozzle gel, drive rolls; (d) PPE: welding helmet/goggles (auto-darkening lens), leather gloves, leather apron, spats; (e) safety: fire extinguisher per W1051, welding blanket, flash-back arrestor check; (f) system bundles recommendation with exchange transaction | System | Sales Associate | 1–2 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Transaction Processing & Cylinder Handoff**: (a) system processes exchange transaction at POS with cylinder deposit tracking (if supplier-owned): deposit amount held on customer's account, credited on return, new deposit charged on exchange; (b) for trade account B2B customers: transaction charged to account with monthly billing per W8; (c) Sales Associate issues full cylinder to customer with safety briefing: "Keep cylinder upright, secure during transport, do not modify valve, store in well-ventilated area, keep away from ignition sources"; (d) system prints gas safety data sheet summary per W698 (SDS management); (e) for customer-owned refills: issue claim stub with estimated refill date (typically 1–2 business days via refill partner); (f) cylinder serial number of issued full cylinder recorded against customer transaction for traceability | Sales Associate | Tools & Hardware Dept Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 5 | **Cylinder Inventory Reconciliation & Replenishment**: (a) system updates cylinder count: +1 empty, −1 full for exchange transactions; (b) when empty cylinder count reaches reorder threshold per store (typically 5+ empty cylinders of same gas/size), system triggers automatic refill requisition to gas supplier via W2 (purchase order cycle); (c) for supplier-owned pool cylinders, system generates weekly supplier reconciliation report matching cylinders received vs. cylinders dispatched per location; (d) monthly cylinder inventory audit per W6 (cycle counting) — cylinders tracked individually by serial number; (e) hazmat storage compliance check per W236: ensure cylinder storage area has adequate ventilation, is separated from flammable materials, and has appropriate fire suppression per W1051 | Receiving Clerk / System | Tools & Hardware Dept Supervisor | Daily reconciliation: 15 min; Monthly audit: 2–3 hrs |

### System Touchpoints
- Cylinder inventory tracking module (serialized cylinder tracking by gas type, size, supplier)
- Real-time inventory availability per store (W533)
- POS transaction module with deposit management (W5)
- Hazmat storage compliance module (W236)
- SDS management system (W698)
- Purchase order / supplier requisition system (W2)
- Cycle counting module (W6)
- Trade account / B2B billing module (W8)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Cylinder safety liability**: Damaged or expired cylinders pose explosion risk; staff must be trained to reject non-compliant cylinders per W237 (hazmat safety training); quarterly safety refresher required per W655
- **Supplier-owned cylinder reconciliation**: Cylinders from different suppliers (Linde/BOC, Air Liquide, Veritas, local refillers) must not be intermixed; supplier-owned cylinders returned to wrong supplier result in deposit disputes and penalty charges
- **Out-of-stock risk**: Welding gas is a just-in-time consumable for fabricators; stockouts drive customers to competitors; safety stock level must account for supplier delivery lead time (2–3 days for refills)
- **Regulatory compliance**: Philippine DOE Bureau of Fire Standards and Regulations (BFSR) requires all compressed gas cylinders to have valid hydrostatic test certification; sale or exchange of expired cylinders is a regulatory violation

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Tools/Hardware Section)**: Cylinder inspection and exchange adds 3–5 minutes per transaction; at 15–25 exchanges per store per week, this represents ~1–2 hours/week; absorbed by existing Sales Associates
- **Receiving Clerk**: Cylinder delivery receipt and storage compliance adds ~30 min per delivery (1–2 deliveries/week per store)
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Cylinder inspection & acceptance: 3–5 min
- Exchange selection & inventory check: 2–3 min
- Companion product recommendation: 1–2 min (automated)
- Transaction & handoff: 3–5 min
- **Total per exchange transaction**: 9–15 min
- Daily reconciliation: 15 min
- Monthly cylinder audit: 2–3 hrs
