## W1094. Customer Construction Equipment Rental Partner Coordination & Booking

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests construction equipment rental (excavator, backhoe, concrete mixer, scaffolding, generator, welding machine, jackhammer, plate compactor, etc.) during a project material purchase, or accesses the equipment rental section via the BuildRight app or store kiosk |
| **Frequency** | ~1,500–2,500 booking requests/month across all stores (equipment rental is a growing value-added service for BuildRight's B2B contractor base) |
| **Volume** | 1 equipment rental booking per request |
| **Owner** | Trade Counter / Pro Desk Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Trade Counter), Equipment Rental Partner, Customer |

### Background

BuildRight already operates a tool rental service per W139, covering handheld and benchtop power tools for DIY customers. However, the construction equipment rental market is a distinct and much larger segment serving BuildRight's B2B contractor customers (5,000 trade accounts) and more ambitious B2C renovation customers. Construction equipment needed for typical BuildRight customer projects includes: (a) **earthmoving**: mini-excavator (1–3 ton), backhoe loader, plate compactor, rammer/tamper; (b) **concrete work**: transit mixer truck (for ready-mix concrete delivery), portable concrete mixer (bag-type, 1-bag or 2-bag capacity), concrete vibrator, power trowel; (c) **lifting & access**: scaffolding set (mobile tower), boom lift/scissor lift (for multi-story projects), material hoist; (d) **power generation**: portable generator (3KVA–10KVA for on-site power, critical in areas with unreliable electricity); (e) **demolition**: jackhammer/breaker (electric or pneumatic), concrete saw; (f) **welding**: portable welding machine (arc/MIG/TIG); (g) **material handling**: forklift (1.5–3 ton capacity), pallet jack. BuildRight does not own this heavy equipment; instead, it partners with equipment rental companies in each region and earns a booking coordination fee. This model is common in Philippine hardware retail — the customer buys materials from BuildRight and rents equipment through BuildRight's partner network, creating a one-stop-shop experience. This is distinct from W139 (tool rental) which covers BuildRight-owned tools; this workflow covers partner-owned construction equipment. It is also distinct from W1062 (scaffolding rental) which covers a specific equipment type; this workflow covers the broader equipment rental coordination process.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Equipment Requirement Identification**: Sales Associate identifies equipment needs based on the customer's project: (a) project type: foundation excavation (mini-excavator + dump truck for soil hauling), concrete pouring (portable mixer + vibrator + trowel), multi-story construction (scaffolding + material hoist), demolition (jackhammer + concrete saw), roofing (scaffolding + generator for power tools); (b) equipment specifications: capacity/size (excavator: 1-ton mini for tight spaces, 3-ton for open sites), power source (electric — requires on-site power, or diesel/petrol — self-contained), duration needed (daily, weekly, monthly rates); (c) site conditions: accessibility (narrow alley in urban barangay limits equipment width to <1.0m), ground conditions (soft soil may require tracked vs. wheeled equipment), and noise restrictions (residential area may limit operating hours per LGU ordinance); (d) operator requirement: does the customer need an equipment operator (required for excavators and heavy equipment) or will they self-operate (for mixers, generators, jackhammers)? | Sales Associate | Trade Counter Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Partner Matching & Availability Check**: (a) system queries equipment rental partners in the customer's service area per W600 (service contractor accreditation — extended to equipment rental companies); (b) system displays available equipment: equipment type, capacity, brand/model, rental rate (daily/weekly/monthly), operator availability (with or without), delivery/pickup availability, partner name and rating; (c) for equipment requiring certified operators (excavators, backhoes, forklifts): system verifies partner provides TESDA-certified operators per Philippine DOLE regulations; (d) system auto-selects best-value option (lowest total cost = rental rate + delivery + operator if needed, weighted by partner rating and availability); (e) for high-demand equipment during peak construction season (January–May dry season): system may show limited availability and offer waitlist or alternative equipment options | System | Trade Counter Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Booking Confirmation & Contract Generation**: (a) system generates equipment rental booking: equipment type, model, rental period (start date/time, end date/time), rental rate, operator (if applicable), delivery address, site contact person, total estimated cost (rental + delivery + operator + fuel surcharge if applicable); (b) system generates rental agreement with terms: (i) damage liability (customer responsible for damage beyond normal wear); (ii) late return charges (1.5× daily rate per day late); (iii) fuel policy (diesel/petrol equipment returned with same fuel level); (iv) insurance requirement (customer must provide evidence of project insurance or purchase rental insurance from partner); (v) operator conduct (for partner-supplied operators: customer may not direct operator to perform unsafe operations); (vi) cancellation policy (free cancellation 24+ hours before delivery; 50% charge for same-day cancellation); (c) customer signs rental agreement (digital or wet signature); (d) system sends confirmation to customer and partner; (e) for trade account customers: rental charges billed to account per W8; for B2C customers: pre-authorization hold on credit card or cash deposit at POS | System / Sales Associate | Trade Counter Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 4 | **Delivery, Monitoring & Return Coordination**: (a) partner delivers equipment to customer site on scheduled date; (b) customer and partner conduct joint equipment inspection at delivery: document existing damage (photos + written record), verify fuel level, test operation; (c) system logs delivery confirmation; (d) during rental period: system monitors rental duration and sends return reminders 24 hours before scheduled return; (e) for rental extensions: customer notifies BuildRight (via app, phone, or store) — system checks partner availability for extension and adjusts billing; (f) at return: customer and partner conduct joint return inspection: verify equipment condition matches delivery inspection, fuel level, and hours meter reading; (g) system logs return confirmation and final charges; (h) any damage disputes: documented with photos, assessed by partner, and charged to customer per rental agreement terms | Partner / System | Trade Counter Supervisor | Delivery/return inspection: 15–30 min each; Monitoring: automated |
| 5 | **Settlement & Partner Performance Management**: (a) system generates final rental invoice: rental charges (actual duration × rate), delivery/pickup charges, operator charges, fuel charges, damage charges (if any), taxes, total; (b) for trade accounts: added to monthly billing; for B2C: credit card pre-auth converted to actual charge or deposit refunded less charges; (c) BuildRight earns coordination fee: 5–10% of total rental charge; (d) system updates partner performance record: on-time delivery rate, equipment condition rating, customer satisfaction score, damage dispute rate; (e) quarterly: Trade Counter Supervisor reviews partner performance; poorly rated partners are placed on probation or replaced | System / Trade Counter Supervisor | Finance Manager | Per-booking settlement: automated; Quarterly review: 2–3 hrs |

### System Touchpoints
- Equipment rental partner management module (W600 extension)
- Real-time equipment availability & pricing API (partner integration)
- Rental agreement generator
- Customer notification engine (SMS/email/app)
- POS invoicing & payment module (W542 / W556)
- Trade account billing module (W8)
- Credit card pre-authorization module
- Partner performance dashboard
- Equipment inspection documentation module (photo upload, damage logging)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Equipment damage liability**: Construction equipment is expensive (a mini-excavator costs PHP 2–5M); damage during rental creates disputes between customer and partner; clear inspection documentation at delivery and return is essential
- **Operator safety**: Equipment operators working on customer sites face safety risks; DOLE requires operators to have TESDA certification and the partner to provide proper PPE; any operator injury on a BuildRight-referred project creates reputational risk
- **Equipment availability during peak season**: Dry season (January–May) is peak construction season in the Philippines; popular equipment (excavators, concrete mixers) may be fully booked weeks in advance; the system must manage customer expectations and offer alternatives
- **Partner reliability**: Small equipment rental operators in provincial areas may have inconsistent service quality; maintaining a pool of 2–3 vetted partners per service area is critical

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Trade Counter)**: Equipment rental coordination adds 10–15 minutes per booking; at ~8–12 bookings per store per week, this represents ~2–3 hours/week — absorbed by existing Trade Counter staff
- **No permanent incremental headcount** — coordination fee revenue covers the labor allocation

### Time Estimate
- Equipment requirement identification: 5–8 min
- Partner matching: 3–5 min
- Booking & contract: 5–8 min
- Delivery/return monitoring: automated + 15–30 min inspections
- Settlement: automated
- **Total per booking**: 13–21 min active staff time

## W1095. Store-Level Customer Electrical Residential Wiring Diagram & Material List Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests a complete residential electrical wiring layout and material list for a new home construction or major renovation project, extending from the panel board design in W1064 |
| **Frequency** | ~2,500–4,000 consultations/month across all stores (electrical is 10% of SKUs, ~3,500 items; new residential construction and renovation are core customer projects) |
| **Volume** | 1 wiring diagram and material list per consultation |
| **Owner** | Electrical Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Electrical Section), Customer |

### Background

While W1064 covers panel board and circuit breaker sizing, and W982 covers electrical load calculation and wire sizing, there is no existing workflow that produces a complete residential wiring diagram showing the routing of all circuits from the panel board to every outlet, switch, light fixture, and appliance connection point. The typical Filipino residential electrical project involves: (a) service entrance from the utility pole (MERALCO, Davao Light, or electric cooperative) to the meter base to the main panel; (b) branch circuits from the panel to every point of use throughout the house; (c) each circuit consisting of: wire (THHN in EMT conduit, or NM-B cable where permitted), junction boxes, switches, outlets, light fixtures, and connections. The Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017 mandates specific requirements: minimum wire sizes per circuit, maximum number of outlets per circuit, GFCI protection for wet areas, proper grounding, and separate circuits for major appliances. A complete wiring diagram with a matching material list helps the customer: (a) understand the full scope of electrical materials needed (and their cost); (b) provide their electrician or electrical engineer with a clear materials specification; (c) purchase the correct quantities of wire, conduit, boxes, switches, and outlets in a single trip; (d) avoid the common problem of under-purchasing wire ( Filipino electricians often request additional rolls mid-project, causing delays). This workflow integrates with W1064 (panel design) and W982 (load calculation) to produce a comprehensive electrical material package.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Floor Plan Input & Room Specification**: (a) Sales Associate enters the customer's floor plan into the system: number of floors, room layout (living room, dining room, kitchen, bedrooms, bathrooms, laundry area, garage/carport, outdoor area); (b) for each room, Associate specifies: room name, dimensions, and electrical point requirements: (i) ceiling light points (quantity, type: flush mount, pendant, LED panel); (ii) wall light points (quantity, if any); (iii) switch locations (quantity, type: 1-gang, 2-gang, 3-gang, position: inside or outside room); (iv) convenience outlets (quantity, type: grounded duplex, USB combo, weatherproof for outdoor); (v) special outlets (air conditioner — wall-mounted at 1.8m, electric stove — floor-level, water heater — wall-mounted, washing machine — floor-level); (vi) exhaust fan points (bathroom, kitchen); (vii) doorbell point (main entrance); (c) for outdoor: perimeter light points, gate light, garage light, outdoor outlets (GFCI-protected) | Sales Associate | Electrical Department Supervisor | 8–12 min |
| 2 | **Automatic Circuit Allocation & Wiring Diagram Generation**: System performs PEC-compliant circuit allocation: (a) lighting circuits: allocate points to 15A circuits with max 10 light points per circuit per PEC; separate lighting circuits per floor; (b) convenience outlet circuits: allocate to 20A circuits with max 6 outlets per circuit per PEC; separate kitchen and bathroom outlet circuits; (c) dedicated appliance circuits per W1064 (aircon, water heater, electric stove, pump); (d) system generates single-line wiring diagram: shows panel board at top, circuits branching down to room-level junction boxes, then to individual points; (e) wire routing: system estimates wire lengths based on room layout: (i) home run length from panel to each room's first junction box (estimated from floor plan dimensions); (ii) branch lengths within each room between points; (iii) standard factor: total wire per circuit = measured length × 1.3 (30% additional for routing around obstacles, drops, and connections); (f) system selects wire size per circuit per W982: 14 AWG (2.0 sqmm) for 15A lighting circuits, 12 AWG (3.5 sqmm) for 20A outlet circuits, 10 AWG (5.5 sqmm) for 30A appliance circuits, 8 AWG (8.0 sqmm) for 40A circuits, 6 AWG (14 sqmm) for 50–60A circuits | System | Electrical Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Complete Electrical Material List**: System generates comprehensive BOM: (a) **Wire/Cable**: per circuit — wire size, number of conductors (2-wire with ground for 1-phase circuits, or 3-wire with ground for multi-wire branch circuits), length per circuit in meters (rounded up to standard roll lengths: 100m rolls for 14/12 AWG, 50m rolls for 10/8/6 AWG); (b) **Conduit**: EMT (electrical metallic tubing) or PVC conduit per circuit — diameter (½" for 2 wires, ¾" for 3–4 wires, 1" for 5+ wires per PEC fill ratio), length per circuit; conduit fittings: connectors, couplings, elbows, straps; (c) **Boxes**: junction boxes (4" octagonal for ceiling points, 4" square for switch/outlet combinations, handy boxes for exposed wiring), switch boxes (gang count matching switch type), outlet boxes, ceiling rose/canopy for light fixtures; (d) **Switches**: per room specification — 1-gang, 2-gang, 3-gang toggle or rocker switches, 1-way and 2-way (for hallways and stairs), dimmer switches (optional, for living room/bedroom); (e) **Outlets**: grounded duplex convenience outlets (per room count), USB combo outlets (optional upgrade), GFCI outlets (bathroom, kitchen, outdoor, garage), weatherproof covers for outdoor outlets; (f) **Circuit breakers**: per W1064 panel schedule; (g) **Service entrance**: meter base (MERALCO/Davao Light approved), service entrance wire (size per utility requirement), grounding system (ground rod, ground wire, ground clamp); (h) **Accessories**: wire nuts/solderless connectors, electrical tape (per circuit count), cable ties, nail-in clips for conduit, drywall anchors for boxes, circuit directory labels for panel; (i) **Installation tools**: wire stripper, conduit cutter, fish tape, voltage tester, screwdrivers (flat and Phillips), drill with masonry bit for concrete walls | System | Sales Associate | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate, Safety Advisory & Professional Referral**: (a) system generates itemized estimate with: single-line wiring diagram, room-by-room circuit allocation table, complete BOM with quantities and prices, total estimated cost; (b) system calculates estimated cost breakdown: wire and cable (~40% of electrical material cost), conduit and fittings (~15%), switches and outlets (~15%), boxes (~10%), circuit breakers and panel (~15%), accessories (~5%); (c) for trade account customers: applies contract pricing per W163 and converts to project quote per W162; (d) safety advisory: "All electrical installations in the Philippines must comply with the Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) 2017 and must be performed by a licensed Professional Electrical Engineer (PEE) or Registered Master Electrician (RME) under the supervision of a PEE. This wiring diagram and material list is for quantity estimation only and does not constitute a professional electrical design. A licensed PEE must review and approve the electrical plan before construction. BuildRight Depot requires customers to engage a qualified electrical professional for installation."; (e) system offers referral to licensed electrical engineers and electricians per W904; (f) estimate and diagram saved to customer loyalty account for future reference | Sales Associate | Electrical Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Floor plan input module (simple grid-based or upload PDF/image)
- PEC 2017 circuit allocation engine
- Single-line wiring diagram generator
- Wire length estimation engine (room layout-based)
- Product attribute master (W298) — wire specifications, conduit fill ratios, box specifications
- Real-time inventory availability per store (W533)
- POS quotation module (W542)
- Loyalty account integration (W17)
- Contractor referral service module (W904)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **PEC compliance liability**: BuildRight's wiring diagram must not be represented as a professional electrical design; the disclaimer must be prominent and the customer must understand that a licensed PEE must produce or approve the actual electrical plan for building permit purposes
- **Wire length estimation accuracy**: Wire length estimates from a simple floor plan input will differ from actual site conditions (wall chase routing, detours around structural elements, vertical drops); the 1.3× factor provides a buffer but some customers may still come up short
- **Conduit fill ratio violations**: Overfilling conduit (too many wires in too-small conduit) violates PEC and creates fire risk; the system must calculate and enforce PEC conduit fill ratios
- **Grounding compliance**: Philippine electrical installations require proper grounding (earth electrode at the service entrance); some older Filipino homes lack grounding entirely; the material list must include grounding materials and the advisory must emphasize grounding importance

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Electrical Section)**: Wiring diagram consultation adds 15–25 minutes per customer; at ~12–20 consultations per store per week, this represents ~3–8 hours/week — absorbed by existing Electrical Department staff
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Floor plan input: 8–12 min
- Circuit allocation & diagram: 3–5 min (automated)
- Material list: 2–3 min (automated)
- Estimate & advisory: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 16–25 min

## W1096. Customer Solar Water Heater System Sizing & Complete Package Recommendation

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer inquires about solar water heating options, or Sales Associate identifies solar water heater applicability during a water heater consultation or solar panel consultation per W990 |
| **Frequency** | ~600–1,200 consultations/month across all stores (growing segment driven by Philippine electricity costs and DOE renewable energy promotion) |
| **Volume** | 1 system design per consultation |
| **Owner** | Electrical Department Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Electrical/Appliance Section), Customer |

### Background

Solar water heating (SWH) is a mature technology well-suited to the Philippines' tropical climate with abundant sunshine (average 5–6 peak sun hours per day year-round). The Philippine Department of Energy (DOE) actively promotes solar water heating through the Renewable Energy Act (RA 9513) and the Philippine Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act (RA 11285). For BuildRight customers, solar water heaters offer: (a) electricity savings of PHP 2,000–5,000/month compared to electric water heaters (Philippine electricity rates are among the highest in Southeast Asia at PHP 9–12/kWh); (b) hot water availability even during power outages (passive thermosiphon systems require no electricity); (c) environmental benefits (reducing carbon footprint per W192). Two main SWH technologies are available: (a) **Evacuated tube collectors (ETC)**: more efficient in cloudy conditions, lighter weight, higher operating temperatures, but more fragile; (b) **Flat plate collectors (FPC)**: more durable, lower cost, good for Philippine sunny conditions. Systems can be: (i) **passive (thermosiphon)**: water circulates naturally by convection — no pump, no electricity needed, tank must be mounted above collector; (ii) **active (pumped)**: uses a circulation pump and controller — more flexible installation (tank can be at ground level) but requires electricity for the pump. This workflow is distinct from W990 (solar panel system) which covers photovoltaic (PV) solar for electricity generation; this workflow addresses solar thermal for water heating.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Hot Water Demand Assessment**: Sales Associate gathers hot water usage information: (a) household size (number of persons); (b) bathrooms with hot water: count and type (shower only, shower + bathtub); (c) kitchen hot water: yes/no (sink hot water tap); (d) laundry hot water: yes/no (washing machine hot water connection); (e) hot water usage pattern: morning peak (bathing), evening peak (bathing + kitchen), or both; (f) current water heating method: electric storage, electric tankless, LPG, or none; (g) desired water temperature (comfortable shower: 38–42°C); (h) cold water inlet temperature: Philippine municipal water ~25–28°C, deep well ~26–29°C; (i) roof type and orientation: flat concrete roof or pitched roof (G.I. sheet or tile), orientation (south-facing optimal in Philippines), available roof area for collector; (j) roof structural capacity: solar water heater + water tank = 150–300 kg — Filipino concrete flat roofs can typically support this, but lightweight G.I. sheet roofs may require structural reinforcement | Sales Associate | Electrical Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **System Sizing & Technology Selection**: System performs sizing calculation: (a) daily hot water demand: standard Philippine household usage = 40–50 liters per person per day at 50°C delivery temperature; total = household size × 50 liters; (b) collector area: Philippine solar radiation ≈ 5 kWh/m²/day; collector area = daily hot water demand (liters) × temperature rise (°C) ÷ (solar radiation × collector efficiency × conversion factor); typical result: 1 sqm collector per 50–70 liters of daily hot water demand; (c) tank size = daily hot water demand × 1.2 (20% buffer for cloudy day storage); (d) system recommendations based on household size: (i) 2–3 persons: 150L tank + 1.5–2 sqm collector (20-tube ETC or 1.5 sqm FPC); (ii) 4–5 persons: 250L tank + 3–4 sqm collector (30-tube ETC or 2 × 2 sqm FPC); (iii) 6–8 persons: 300L tank + 4–5 sqm collector (2 × 20-tube ETC or 2 × 2.5 sqm FPC); (e) technology selection: ETC recommended for households in cloudy areas (mountainous regions, typhoon-prone areas), FPC recommended for most Philippine lowland locations (more durable, lower maintenance); (f) passive vs. active: passive (thermosiphon) recommended for single-story homes with flat concrete roof (tank + collector on roof); active (pumped) recommended for multi-story homes or roofs that cannot support tank weight (tank at ground level, collector on roof) | System | Electrical Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Complete System Package & Companion Materials**: System generates full BOM: (a) solar collector: ETC (specify tube count, diameter, length) or FPC (specify dimensions, absorber coating, glazing type); (b) hot water storage tank: capacity, stainless steel or enamel-lined, insulation thickness (≥50mm polyurethane foam), integrated or separate from collector; (c) mounting frame: stainless steel or aluminum, adjustable tilt angle (optimal tilt for Philippines: 10–15° for year-round performance, adjustable for seasonal optimization); (d) circulation pump (active system only): rated for hot water, 40–60W, with controller; (e) piping: insulated hot water pipe (PPR or copper, minimum 19mm diameter, with 19mm foam insulation per W1057); (f) cold water supply connection: PPR pipe from existing cold water line to tank inlet; (g) hot water delivery connection: PPR or copper pipe from tank outlet to bathrooms and kitchen; (h) temperature & pressure relief valve (safety device per PEC/plumbing code); (i) anti-scale filter (for areas with hard water — some Philippine water supplies have high mineral content); (j) backup electric heating element: most solar water heater tanks include a 1.5–2kW electric backup element for cloudy/rainy days when solar is insufficient; (k) accessories: pipe insulation, pipe fittings, valves (gate valve, check valve), mounting hardware (bolts, anchors for concrete roof, flashing for pitched roof), sealant, and thermostatic mixing valve (prevents scalding at taps) | System | Sales Associate | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 4 | **ROI Calculation, Estimate & Installation Advisory**: (a) system calculates financial return: (i) current electric water heater energy cost: liters/day × temperature rise × specific heat of water ÷ electric heater efficiency × PHP/kWh rate = monthly cost; (ii) solar water heater energy cost: PHP 0 (sunlight is free) + backup electric heating on cloudy days (~20% of total energy) = monthly cost; (iii) monthly savings = (i) − (ii); (iv) payback period = system cost ÷ monthly savings; typical result: PHP 25,000–45,000 system cost ÷ PHP 2,000–4,000/month savings = 6–18 month payback; (b) system generates estimate with: system specification, complete BOM, total cost, ROI analysis, estimated installation time (1–2 days for passive system, 2–3 days for active system); (c) installation advisory: "Solar water heater installation involves both plumbing and structural work. Tank and collector mounting on the roof requires proper waterproofing to prevent leaks. BuildRight Depot recommends professional installation by a qualified plumber and, for active systems, a licensed electrician for the pump/controller wiring."; (d) system offers referral to accredited installation partners per W904; (e) for customers interested in larger renewable energy systems: Associate mentions W990 (solar PV system) for electricity generation | Sales Associate | Electrical Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Solar water heater sizing calculator
- ROI calculation engine
- Product attribute master (W298) — collector specifications, tank specifications
- Real-time inventory availability per store (W533)
- POS quotation module (W542)
- Loyalty account integration (W17)
- Contractor referral service module (W904)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Roof structural concerns**: A 250L tank + collector weighs ~300 kg; Filipino concrete flat roofs (typically 150mm CHB slab) can support this, but older homes or lightweight G.I. sheet roofs cannot; system must flag structural assessment requirement
- **Water quality impact**: Hard water (high calcium/magnesium content, common in some Philippine groundwater sources) causes scale buildup in evacuated tubes and tank heat exchangers, reducing efficiency over time; anti-scale filter must be recommended for affected areas
- **Typhoon vulnerability**: Solar collectors mounted on roofs are vulnerable to typhoon winds (Philippines experiences ~20 typhoons per year); mounting frame must be designed for wind speeds per NSCP (National Structural Code of the Philippines) and customers must be advised to check mounting bolts annually
- **Consumer awareness**: Solar water heating is less well-known than solar PV in the Philippines; Sales Associates need training to explain the technology and benefits clearly

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Electrical/Appliance Section)**: SWH consultation adds 15–20 minutes per customer; at ~3–6 consultations per store per week, this represents ~1–2 hours/week — absorbed by existing staff
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Hot water demand assessment: 5–8 min
- System sizing: 3–5 min (automated)
- Material list: 2–3 min (automated)
- ROI & estimate: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 13–21 min

## W1097. Store-Level Customer Outdoor Deck, Patio & Pergola Material Estimation Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests material estimation for an outdoor deck, patio, or pergola project, or Sales Associate identifies the project type during a lumber or garden section consultation |
| **Frequency** | ~2,000–3,500 consultations/month across all stores (outdoor living is a growing segment in the Philippine market, particularly in upscale subdivisions and resort areas) |
| **Volume** | 1 structure estimation per consultation |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Lumber & Building Materials) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Lumber Section), Customer |

### Background

Outdoor decks, patios, and pergolas are increasingly popular in Philippine residential construction, driven by: (a) the Filipino "lanai" and outdoor living culture (entertaining, family gatherings, "inihaw" grilling); (b) the growth of residential subdivisions in Metro Manila, Cebu, and Davao with larger lots that include outdoor spaces; (c) the resort and hospitality sector (hotel and resort construction is a strong segment for BuildRight's B2B customers); (d) social media influence (Pinterest, Instagram, and local home improvement pages featuring outdoor living spaces). The materials for these structures are primarily from BuildRight's lumber and building materials category (14% of SKUs, ~4,900 items): (a) **decking**: pressure-treated lumber (tanguile, yakal, or imported treated pine), composite decking (wood-plastic composite — growing in popularity despite higher cost due to low maintenance), or concrete decking tiles; (b) **structural framing**: treated lumber joists and beams, or steel framing (galvanized C-purlins for modern deck construction); (c) **pergola posts and beams**: hardwood (yakal, guijo — native Philippine hardwoods) or steel posts with wood cladding; (d) **pergola roofing**: polycarbonate sheets (for shade with natural light), G.I. corrugated sheets, or shade sail/canvas; (e) **fasteners**: deck screws (stainless steel for coastal areas, galvanized for inland), post anchors, joist hangers, beam brackets; (f) **finishing**: wood stain, sealant, or exterior paint per W1093; (g) **lighting**: outdoor LED per W1084 (security/CCTV adapted for outdoor accent lighting). This workflow provides a comprehensive material estimation for the structure, integrating with W976 (lumber grade selection) and W169 (lumber cutting services) for the lumber-specific aspects.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Structure Design & Dimension Input**: Sales Associate gathers project specifications: (a) structure type: deck only, pergola only, deck + pergola, patio (concrete slab); (b) deck dimensions: length × width × height above ground (ground-level: 0–0.3m, raised: 0.3–1.0m, elevated: 1.0m+); (c) deck shape: rectangular, L-shaped, or multi-level; (d) deck surface material preference: natural wood (specify: tanguile, yakal, or treated pine), composite decking (WPC), or concrete tile; (e) pergola dimensions: length × width × post height (standard: 2.4m post height for 2.1m clearance); (f) pergola roof type: open-rafter (decorative only, no rain protection), polycarbonate roof (rain protection + natural light), G.I. sheet roof (full rain protection), or retractable canvas/shade sail; (g) site conditions: ground type (concrete pad, compacted soil, or grass), drainage consideration (slope away from house), attachment to existing structure (ledger board against house wall or freestanding); (h) load requirements: residential light-duty (furniture + people, ~200 kg/sqm) or heavy-duty (hot tub, outdoor kitchen, ~400 kg/sqm) | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Structural Design & Material Calculation**: System designs the structure and calculates materials: **For Deck**: (a) footing: concrete footing at each post location — footing diameter × depth based on deck height and soil type (Philippine standard: 0.3m diameter × 0.6m depth for ground-level, 0.4m × 0.8m for raised); footing count = post grid spacing (typically 1.5–2.0m centers); (b) posts: 4×4 (100mm × 100mm) or 6×6 (150mm × 150mm) treated lumber or steel — quantity = footing count, length = deck height + footing projection + beam clearance; (c) beams: double 2×8 or 2×10 (50mm × 200mm or 50mm × 250mm) per span table — spans ≤ 3.0m for 2×8, ≤ 4.0m for 2×10; (d) joists: 2×6 or 2×8 at 400mm or 600mm spacing — quantity = deck width ÷ joist spacing + 1, length = deck depth; (e) decking boards: quantity = deck area ÷ board coverage per piece × 1.10 (10% wastage for cutting); (f) fasteners: deck screws (stainless steel 304 for coastal, 316 for saltwater proximity), joist hangers, post anchors, beam brackets, carriage bolts for post-to-beam connections. **For Pergola**: (g) posts: 4×4 or 6×6 — 4 posts minimum (2 per side), length = post height + footing embedment; (h) beams: double 2×8 spanning across posts; (i) rafters: 2×4 or 2×6 spanning between beams at 400–600mm spacing — quantity = pergola length ÷ rafter spacing; (j) roofing: polycarbonate sheets (6mm or 10mm twin-wall, length matching rafter span × width needed) or G.I. sheets per W983 (roofing calculator); (k) post bases: galvanized steel post anchors set in concrete footings; (l) hardware: lag bolts, through bolts, angle brackets, rafter ties | System | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Companion Products & Finishing Materials**: System adds: (a) **Surface preparation**: gravel base under deck (for ground-level, to prevent weed growth and improve drainage) — volume in cubic meters; weed barrier fabric; (b) **Concrete for footings**: cement bags + sand + gravel per footing count × footing volume; concrete mix ratio per W1044; (c) **Wood treatment**: if using natural lumber (not pre-treated): wood preservative (solignum or equivalent), application brush, 2–3 coats recommended for ground-contact posts; (d) **Deck finish**: wood stain or exterior sealer for decking surface (quantity based on deck area × 2 coats); application by brush or sprayer; (e) **Waterproofing**: ledger board flashing (aluminum or galvanized) where deck meets house wall — prevents water infiltration; (f) **Outdoor lighting**: deck post solar lights, step lights (LED), pergola string lights ("fairy lights" — very popular in Philippine outdoor spaces), and under-deck LED strip lighting; per W1084 adapted for decorative outdoor lighting; (g) **Railing** (for decks > 0.6m above ground per Philippine building code): posts, top rail, bottom rail, balusters (wood, steel, or cable railing), and hardware; (h) **Stairs** (for raised decks): stringers, treads, risers, handrail per stair calculator; (i) **Tools**: circular saw per W169 (lumber cutting service available in-store), drill, level, measuring tape, post level, concrete mixer rental per W1094 | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–4 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Estimate, Lumber Advisory & Service Coordination**: (a) system generates itemized estimate with: structural diagram (simplified isometric sketch), complete BOM organized by structural component, quantities and prices, total estimated cost; (b) estimated cost ranges: ground-level wood deck (tanguile): PHP 2,500–4,000/sqm; raised wood deck: PHP 3,500–5,500/sqm; composite deck: PHP 5,000–8,000/sqm; pergola (wood, open-rafter): PHP 3,000–5,000/sqm; pergola (polycarbonate roof): PHP 4,500–7,000/sqm; (c) lumber advisory: (i) wood grade: per W976 (lumber grade selection) — Associate explains the difference between construction grade (knots allowed, for structural framing) and select grade (minimal knots, for visible decking and pergola beams); (ii) cutting service: per W169 — BuildRight can cut lumber to specified lengths, reducing customer's on-site cutting; (iii) treatment: untreated lumber must be treated before installation, especially posts in contact with ground; (iv) moisture content: lumber should be kiln-dried or air-dried to ≤ 18% moisture content to prevent warping; (d) system offers installation referral per W904 for customers who need professional deck/pergola construction; (e) estimate saved to customer loyalty account | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Deck/pergola structural calculator (span tables, material quantity formulas)
- Product attribute master (W298) — lumber dimensions, grades, composite decking specs
- Real-time inventory availability per store (W533)
- Lumber cutting service integration (W169)
- POS quotation module (W542)
- Loyalty account integration (W17)
- Contractor referral service module (W904)
- Concrete mix calculator integration (W1044)
- Roofing calculator integration (W983)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Wood quality variability**: Philippine lumber (tanguile, yakal) quality varies significantly by batch and supplier; visible defects (knots, splits, warping) may only be apparent after purchase; quality inspection at delivery per W109 is essential
- **Termite risk**: Philippine tropical climate is highly conducive to termites; all ground-contact wood must be pressure-treated or treated with solignum; failure to treat leads to structural failure within 2–5 years
- **Typhoon wind resistance**: Pergolas with polycarbonate or G.I. roofs must be designed for typhoon wind loads per NSCP; under-designed pergolas become dangerous flying debris during typhoons
- **Cost sensitivity**: Many customers underestimate deck/pergola costs; the estimate must be clear and transparent, with material cost breakdown, to avoid sticker shock at POS

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Lumber Section)**: Deck/pergola estimation adds 15–20 minutes per consultation; at ~10–18 consultations per store per week, this represents ~3–6 hours/week — absorbed by existing Lumber Department staff
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Structure design & input: 5–8 min
- Structural calculation: 3–5 min (automated)
- Companion products: 3–4 min (automated)
- Estimate & advisory: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 14–22 min

## W1098. Customer Emergency Home Repair Quick-Fix Bundle Curation & Package Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer arrives at store with an urgent home repair need (leaking pipe, broken window, electrical issue, roof leak, clogged drain, etc.), or customer calls/uses the app requesting an emergency repair material bundle |
| **Frequency** | ~8,000–12,000 emergency repair interactions/month across all stores (home repair emergencies are a consistent high-frequency retail traffic driver) |
| **Volume** | 1 bundle per emergency |
| **Owner** | Customer Service Representative |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate, Customer Service Representative, Customer |

### Background

Emergency home repairs are one of the most common reasons Filipino homeowners visit a hardware store. The Philippine climate and housing stock create recurring repair needs: (a) **roof leaks** during rainy season (June–November) — G.I. sheet roofing develops rust holes, flashing deteriorates, ridge cap gaps open; (b) **plumbing leaks** — pipe corrosion (especially in older GI pipe systems), faucet washer failure, toilet valve failure; (c) **electrical issues** — tripped breakers during brownouts, faulty outlets, damaged wiring after flooding; (d) **window/door damage** — broken glass from typhoon debris, swollen wooden doors from humidity, broken hinges; (e) **clogged drains** — common in Philippine homes due to insufficient drain pipe diameter and tree root intrusion; (f) **wall cracks and leaks** — concrete hollow block walls develop cracks from settling and seismic activity (Philippines is earthquake-prone). These customers share common characteristics: (a) they are stressed and time-pressured ("I need to fix this NOW before the next rain"); (b) they may not know exactly what materials they need ("My roof is leaking — what do I buy?"); (c) they need everything in one trip (making multiple trips during an emergency is highly undesirable); (d) they often need basic tools they may not own (putty knife, pipe wrench, wire nuts). Pre-curated "Quick-Fix Bundles" for the top 10–15 emergency repair scenarios address these needs: each bundle contains all materials and tools needed for the repair, packaged together with a simple instruction card. This is distinct from W910 (product bundle assembly & pre-packaged solution kit management) which covers planned merchandise bundles; this workflow focuses on emergency repair scenarios with real-time bundle assembly. It integrates with W1093 (paint color consultation) for cosmetic repair matching.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Emergency Diagnosis & Bundle Selection**: (a) Customer Service Representative or Sales Associate quickly diagnoses the emergency: "What's the problem? Where is it? How urgent?"; (b) Associate maps the problem to a Quick-Fix Bundle: (i) **Roof Leak Bundle**: G.I. sheet patch (matching existing profile), roofing screws with rubber washers, butyl tape (for flashing repair), wire brush (for rust removal), rust converter, roofing sealant, and a set of basic hand tools if needed; (ii) **Pipe Leak Bundle**: pipe repair clamp or self-fusing silicone tape, pipe cutter (for GI pipe), replacement pipe section (GI or PPR), fittings, Teflon tape, pipe wrench, and a bucket (for residual water); (iii) **Faucet Leak Bundle**: replacement washer set (universal rubber washers), faucet cartridge (if known brand), adjustable wrench, Teflon tape, plumber's putty; (iv) **Clogged Drain Bundle**: drain snake (hand-crank, 6m), chemical drain cleaner (caustic soda or enzymatic), plunger, rubber gloves, bucket; (v) **Electrical Tripped Breaker**: circuit tester, replacement breaker (if customer knows panel type — Schneider, ABB, etc.), wire nuts, electrical tape; (vi) **Broken Window Bundle**: glass cutter (if cutting own glass), replacement glass pane (standard sizes pre-cut per W943 glass cutting service), glazing points, window putty/glazing compound, putty knife; (vii) **Wall Crack / Leak Bundle**: hydraulic cement (for active leaks), crack injection polyurethane foam, wire brush, trowel, bonding agent, and wall patch compound; (viii) **Flood Cleanup Bundle**: wet/dry shop vacuum rental per W139, squeegee, heavy-duty mop, chlorine bleach for disinfection, rubber boots, nitrile gloves, N95 mask; (ix) **Door/Hinge Repair Bundle**: replacement hinges (brass or stainless), wood screws, wood filler (for stripped screw holes), screwdriver set, door stopper; (x) **Toilet Repair Bundle**: toilet fill valve replacement kit, flush valve/flapper, toilet wax ring, supply hose, adjustable wrench, sponge (for bowl water removal) | Sales Associate / Customer Service Rep | Customer Service Representative | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **Bundle Assembly & Customization**: (a) system retrieves the Quick-Fix Bundle template from product master: pre-defined SKU list per emergency type with standard quantities; (b) Associate customizes based on customer's specific situation: (i) for roof leak: "What's your roof profile? (corrugated, rib-type, tile?) What color?" — system substitutes matching G.I. sheet; (ii) for pipe leak: "What pipe material? (GI, PPR, PVC, copper?) What diameter?" — system substitutes matching pipe and fittings; (iii) for electrical: "What breaker brand? How many amps?" — system substitutes matching breaker; (c) system checks real-time inventory for all bundle items at the store per W533; if any item is out of stock, system suggests nearest alternative or offers to order for DC delivery per W19; (d) Associate adds items not in the standard bundle that the customer may need based on conversation (e.g., safety glasses for roof work, a longer pipe section than standard, additional roofing screws) | Sales Associate / System | Customer Service Representative | 3–5 min |
| 3 | **Quick-Fix Instruction Card & Advisory**: (a) system prints a Quick-Fix Instruction Card specific to the emergency type: single-page, illustrated, step-by-step guide in English and Filipino/Tagalog; (b) example — Roof Leak Quick-Fix Card: "Step 1: Safety first — do not climb on the roof during rain. Wait for dry weather. Step 2: Locate the leak source from inside the attic or ceiling. Step 3: Wire-brush the rust/corrosion area. Step 4: Apply rust converter and wait 30 minutes. Step 5: Cut butyl tape to cover the hole plus 5cm overlap on all sides. Step 6: Press firmly and smooth from center outward. Step 7: If replacing a G.I. sheet section, remove screws, position new sheet with 1.5 corrugation overlap, secure with roofing screws. Step 8: Apply sealant to screw heads and overlap edges. WARNING: For roofs higher than 3 meters, BuildRight recommends hiring a professional roofer. Safety harness required."; (c) safety warnings printed in bold on every card: appropriate PPE, fall hazard warnings for roof/height work, electrical shock warnings for electrical repairs ("Turn off the main breaker before touching any wiring"), and chemical hazard warnings for drain cleaner and solvents; (d) system prints "When to Call a Professional" guidance: conditions where the repair exceeds DIY capability (e.g., "If the pipe leak is at a joint inside the wall, call a licensed plumber. Do not break open walls unless you can identify the exact leak location.") | System / Sales Associate | Customer Service Representative | 2–3 min |
| 4 | **Fast-Track Checkout & Loyalty Tracking**: (a) bundle is processed at POS as a single transaction with all items pre-grouped for fast scanning (pre-printed bundle barcode or quick-scan list on cashier terminal); (b) emergency repair bundles qualify for BuildRight's "Rush Repair" priority checkout lane (no queuing during emergencies); (c) for loyalty members: system automatically saves the repair details and materials purchased to the customer's account — useful for future maintenance tracking (e.g., "You repaired your roof with butyl tape on [date]. Roof patches typically last 1–2 years. Consider a professional roof inspection."); (d) system tracks emergency repair bundle sales data: bundle type, frequency by store, seasonal spikes (roof leak bundles spike during rainy season, flood cleanup bundles spike after typhoons), and average bundle value | Sales Associate / Cashier | Customer Service Representative | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Quick-Fix Bundle template library (product master with pre-defined SKU lists per emergency type)
- Real-time inventory availability per store (W533)
- Bundle customization engine (substitution logic based on customer specifications)
- Quick-Fix Instruction Card printer (template-based, bilingual English/Filipino)
- POS fast-scan module (bundle barcode or quick-scan list)
- Loyalty account integration (W17) — repair history tracking
- Seasonal demand analytics dashboard (bundle sales by type and season)
- Product substitution rules engine (W279)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Customer safety liability**: Emergency repairs often involve hazardous situations (roof work, electrical work, chemical handling); the instruction card must include prominent safety warnings, and Associates must verbally reinforce "If you're not comfortable doing this repair yourself, BuildRight can refer a professional."
- **Incomplete diagnosis**: The customer may describe the symptom incorrectly (e.g., "my roof is leaking" could be a plumbing leak from an overhead pipe, not the roof); the bundle may not address the actual problem; the instruction card must include a "diagnostic check" step before proceeding with the repair
- **Tool knowledge gap**: Many DIY customers don't know how to use the tools in the bundle; the instruction card must include basic tool usage guidance
- **Seasonal stockouts**: Roof leak bundles during rainy season and flood cleanup bundles after typhoons experience demand spikes; pre-positioning per W960 (seasonal forward stock pre-positioning) is critical

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate / Customer Service Representative**: Emergency bundle assembly adds 5–10 minutes per customer; at ~40–60 emergency customers per store per week, this represents ~4–8 hours/week — absorbed by existing floor staff; the fast-track process is designed to reduce checkout time to offset the consultation time
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Emergency diagnosis & bundle selection: 3–5 min
- Bundle assembly & customization: 3–5 min
- Instruction card & advisory: 2–3 min
- Fast-track checkout: 3–5 min
- **Total per emergency**: 11–18 min

## W1101. Store-Level Customer Door & Window Security Grille Custom Fabrication Coordination

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests custom-made security grilles for doors or windows during a building material purchase, or Sales Associate identifies the need during a fencing/security consultation per W1084 |
| **Frequency** | ~3,000–5,000 coordination requests/month across all stores (security grilles are a standard feature in Philippine homes — nearly every ground-floor window and door has steel security grilles) |
| **Volume** | 1 fabrication project per coordination (typically covering 4–15 windows + 1–2 doors) |
| **Owner** | Trade Counter / Pro Desk Supervisor |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Trade Counter / Lumber & Building Materials), Fabrication Service Partner (accredited welder/fabricator), Customer |

### Background

Steel security grilles (locally called "berde" or "rehas" in Filipino) are an essential feature of Philippine residential construction. Due to property crime concerns in both urban and rural areas, virtually every Filipino home installs steel grilles on all ground-floor windows, main doors, and back doors. The standard Philippine security grille is fabricated from: (a) flat bar steel (typically ¼" × 1" or 6mm × 25mm) for the main frame; (b) square tube (16mm × 16mm or 20mm × 20mm) or round bar (12mm or 16mm diameter) for the vertical bars; (c) welding (arc or MIG) at all joints; (d) anti-rust primer and enamel paint finish (black or custom color per W1093). The grilles are custom-made to fit each window or door opening exactly, because Philippine window sizes are not standardized — they vary by house design, builder, and era of construction. The fabrication process requires: (a) on-site measurement of each window/door opening; (b) custom cutting, welding, and finishing at the fabricator's workshop; (c) delivery and installation at the customer's home; (d) anchoring to the concrete or hollow block wall using expansion bolts or embedded steel brackets. This workflow coordinates the custom fabrication process from measurement through installation, connecting BuildRight's material supply (steel, paint, hardware) with accredited fabrication partners.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Measurement Requirements & Design Specifications**: (a) Sales Associate gathers grille specifications: (i) number of windows requiring grilles and approximate dimensions (width × height per window); (ii) number of doors requiring security doors and approximate dimensions; (iii) bar style preference: vertical bars only (most common and cost-effective), vertical + horizontal (cross-hatch for higher security), or decorative scrollwork (premium); (iv) bar spacing: standard (100–120mm between bars — prevents head entry) or tight (80mm — maximum security for high-risk areas); (v) frame material: flat bar (¼" × 1") or angle bar (1" × 1" × ¼"); (vi) bar material: square tube (16mm, 20mm) — modern look, or round bar (12mm, 16mm) — traditional; (vii) finish: primer + black enamel (standard), primer + color-matched enamel (per W1093), powder coating (premium), or stainless steel (highest grade, coastal areas); (viii) hinged or fixed: hinged grilles for windows that need opening (for cleaning or emergency egress) vs. fixed grilles; (ix) locking mechanism for hinged grilles: barrel bolt, padlock hasp, or keyed lock | Sales Associate | Trade Counter Supervisor | 8–12 min |
| 2 | **Fabrication Partner Matching & Quotation**: (a) system queries accredited fabrication partners (welding shops) in the customer's area per W600 (service contractor accreditation); (b) system generates material cost estimate: (i) steel material: flat bar × total perimeter length (all windows/doors) + square tube/round bar × total bar count × standard bar length; (ii) welding consumables: welding rods/electrodes (E6013 or E7018), cutting gas (if oxy-acetylene); (iii) paint: anti-rust primer (red oxide, 1 coat) + enamel paint (2 coats) — quantity per surface area of finished grilles; (iv) hardware: expansion bolts (4 per window grille, 6 per door grille), hinges (2 per hinged grille), barrel bolts/locks, and miscellaneous (wire brush, sandpaper for surface prep); (c) system estimates fabrication labor: cutting, welding, grinding, and finishing — based on linear meters of welding and number of pieces; (d) system estimates installation labor: delivery, fitting, anchoring, and cleanup; (e) total project cost estimate = material cost + fabrication labor + installation labor; (f) typical cost ranges: window grille (1.0m × 1.2m, standard vertical bars, primer + black enamel): PHP 2,500–4,000 per window; door security gate (0.9m × 2.1m, hinged with lock): PHP 6,000–12,000 per door | System | Trade Counter Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 3 | **On-Site Measurement & Fabrication Order**: (a) for accuracy: Associate recommends that the fabrication partner perform on-site measurement before fabrication (Philippine window openings often deviate from planned dimensions by 10–30mm); (b) system schedules on-site measurement visit: partner visits customer's home within 2–3 days to measure every opening precisely; (c) partner sends measurement sheet to BuildRight system: exact width, height, and any irregularities (arched top, angled sill, pipe/conduit obstruction); (d) system generates final fabrication order with precise dimensions and updates material quantities accordingly; (e) material delivery: BuildRight delivers steel, paint, and hardware to the fabrication partner's workshop (not to the customer's home — the partner fabricates at their workshop) per W668 | Trade Counter Supervisor / Fabrication Partner | Trade Counter Supervisor | Measurement visit: 1–2 hrs; Order update: 15 min |
| 4 | **Fabrication, Quality Check & Installation**: (a) fabrication partner fabricates grilles per the measurement sheet: (i) cuts flat bar and square tube/round bar to size; (ii) assembles frame by welding; (iii) welds vertical bars at specified spacing; (iv) grinds all welds smooth (no sharp edges); (v) installs hinges and lock hardware (for hinged grilles); (vi) applies anti-rust primer (1 coat) and enamel paint (2 coats) with drying time between coats; (b) fabrication timeline: 3–7 days depending on scope (4–6 windows: 3 days; 10–15 windows + 2 doors: 5–7 days); (c) Trade Counter Supervisor performs quality check (or partner self-certifies per W600 accreditation): (i) dimensions match measurement sheet (±5mm tolerance); (ii) weld quality: no visible gaps, porosity, or undercut; (iii) bar spacing uniform and within specification; (iv) paint coverage: complete, no bare steel visible, smooth finish; (v) hinges operate smoothly, locks engage properly; (d) partner delivers and installs grilles at customer's home: anchors to wall with expansion bolts, seals around frame with silicone sealant, and verifies operation | Fabrication Partner / Trade Counter Supervisor | Trade Counter Supervisor | Fabrication: 3–7 days; Installation: 1 day |
| 5 | **Customer Acceptance, Settlement & Warranty**: (a) customer inspects installed grilles: verifies fit, finish, operation, and security; (b) customer signs acceptance; (c) system generates final invoice: material cost (BuildRight) + fabrication labor (partner) + installation labor (partner) = total project cost; (d) payment: (i) for trade account customers: added to monthly billing per W8; (ii) for B2C customers: 50% deposit at order placement, 50% upon installation acceptance; (e) BuildRight pays partner: fabrication + installation labor minus BuildRight coordination fee (8–12%); (f) warranty: fabrication partner provides 1-year workmanship warranty (weld integrity, paint adhesion); BuildRight provides material quality warranty per manufacturer terms; (g) system sends customer satisfaction survey and updates partner performance record per W600 | System / Trade Counter Supervisor | Finance Manager | Settlement: automated; Satisfaction: 5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Service contractor accreditation module (W600 — extended to fabrication partners)
- Material estimation module (steel, paint, hardware quantity calculator)
- Partner availability & scheduling module
- Measurement sheet input module
- Quality check checklist module
- POS invoicing module (W542) — split billing (materials + labor)
- Trade account billing module (W8)
- Customer notification engine (SMS/email)
- Partner performance dashboard

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Measurement accuracy**: If the on-site measurement is wrong, the fabricated grille won't fit; the 2–3 day measurement visit step is critical and cannot be skipped (despite customer impatience)
- **Weld quality**: Poor weld quality (cold welds, porosity) creates security risk — the grille fails under force; quality check per step 4c is essential
- **Corrosion in coastal areas**: Philippine coastal environments (many BuildRight stores are in coastal cities) cause rapid steel corrosion; anti-rust primer quality and paint thickness are critical for longevity; stainless steel option must be actively recommended for coastal installations
- **Emergency egress safety**: Security grilles that cannot be opened from inside create fire safety hazards; hinged grilles with inside-only locks must be recommended for bedrooms and sleeping areas per BFP fire safety regulations

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Trade Counter)**: Coordination adds 10–15 minutes per project; at ~15–25 projects per store per week, this represents ~3–6 hours/week — absorbed by existing Trade Counter staff
- **Trade Counter Supervisor**: Quality check adds ~30 minutes per project; at ~15–25 projects per week, this represents ~8–12 hours/week — significant but absorbed by existing role; may delegate to Senior Sales Associate in high-volume stores
- **No permanent incremental headcount** — coordination fee revenue covers the labor allocation

### Time Estimate
- Specification gathering: 8–12 min
- Quotation: 3–5 min
- Measurement coordination: 15 min
- Quality check: 30 min per project
- Settlement: automated
- **Total per coordination**: 25–35 min active staff time

## W1102. Customer Retaining Wall & Foundation Formwork Material Estimation Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests material estimation for a retaining wall or foundation formwork project, or Sales Associate identifies the need during a construction material consultation for a sloped lot or multi-level project |
| **Frequency** | ~2,000–3,000 consultations/month across all stores (retaining walls are common in Philippine hillside and terraced construction; foundation formwork is needed for most new construction projects) |
| **Volume** | 1 retaining wall or formwork estimation per consultation |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Lumber & Building Materials) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Lumber/Building Materials Section), Customer |

### Background

Retaining walls and foundation formwork are critical structural elements in Philippine construction. The Philippines' mountainous and hilly terrain (especially in areas like Baguio, Cebu, Davao's hillside subdivisions, and Rizal province) creates widespread need for retaining walls: (a) **garden/landscape retaining walls**: low walls (0.3–1.0m height) for terraced gardens and landscaping, typically built with hollow blocks (CHB) or stone; (b) **structural retaining walls**: medium walls (1.0–3.0m height) for hillside lot leveling, built with reinforced concrete (RC) cantilever or gravity walls; (c) **major retaining walls**: high walls (>3.0m) for commercial and subdivision development, requiring structural engineering design. Foundation formwork is needed for all new construction projects that involve reinforced concrete: footings, columns, beams, and slabs. The formwork (also called "shuttering") is the temporary mold into which concrete is poured — typically made from lumber (plywood sheets and timber studs/wales) or steel formwork panels. This workflow addresses the material estimation for: (a) CHB/concrete block retaining walls; (b) reinforced concrete retaining walls; (c) foundation formwork (footings, columns, beams). This integrates with W976 (lumber grade selection) for formwork lumber, W1044 (concrete mix calculator) for concrete quantities, and W986 (rebar cutting and bending) for reinforcement steel.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Specification & Structural Input**: Sales Associate gathers project details: (a) **For retaining walls**: (i) wall height (meters) and total wall length (meters); (ii) retained soil height (may differ from wall height if wall is partially embedded); (iii) soil type: clay (high lateral pressure), sandy (moderate), gravel (low); (iv) surcharge load: is there a structure, driveway, or slope above the wall? (affects wall design); (v) wall type preference: CHB (hollow block — for walls ≤ 1.5m), reinforced concrete cantilever (for walls 1.0–3.0m), or gravity wall (stone/mass concrete — for walls ≤ 2.0m); (vi) drainage provision: weep holes (required for all retaining walls — prevents hydrostatic pressure buildup behind the wall); (b) **For foundation formwork**: (i) foundation type: isolated footing, continuous footing, mat foundation, or pile cap; (ii) number and dimensions of footings (length × width × depth); (iii) column dimensions and heights (from footing to beam level); (iv) beam dimensions (width × depth) and total beam length; (v) slab area and thickness (if slab formwork needed); (vi) formwork material preference: lumber (plywood + timber) — most common in the Philippines, or steel panels — for large projects; (c) **Site conditions**: (i) accessibility for material delivery; (ii) water table level (affects concrete mix and waterproofing needs); (iii) seismic zone (Philippines is Zone 4 — highest seismic risk per NSCP, affects reinforcement requirements) | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 8–12 min |
| 2 | **Retaining Wall Material Calculation**: System calculates retaining wall materials based on wall type: **For CHB wall (≤ 1.5m height)**: (a) CHB quantity = wall area (length × height) ÷ CHB face area (0.2m × 0.4m = 0.08 sqm per 4" CHB or 0.2m × 0.2m = 0.04 sqm per 6" CHB) × 1.05 (5% wastage); (b) cement mortar: 1 bag cement per 70 pieces of 4" CHB or 1 bag per 50 pieces of 6" CHB; sand: 0.08 cubic meters per bag of cement; (c) reinforcement: for CHB walls > 0.6m, vertical rebar (10mm or 12mm) at 0.40m centers grouted into CHB cells; horizontal rebar (10mm) at every 2 courses; (d) foundation: concrete strip footing below wall — width = wall height × 0.5, depth = 0.30m minimum; concrete volume per W1044; (e) drainage: weep holes (50mm PVC pipe) at 1.5m centers along wall base; gravel drain (¾" crushed stone) behind the wall with filter fabric; **For RC cantilever wall (1.0–3.0m)**: (f) concrete volume = (base slab + stem wall + toe + heel) based on standard cantilever wall proportions; system calculates per wall height; (g) reinforcement steel: main vertical bars (12mm or 16mm), horizontal distribution bars (10mm or 12mm), base slab reinforcement (12mm or 16mm both ways); rebar weight calculated per kg per W986; (h) formwork: plywood (12mm thick, 4'×8' sheets) for wall faces; timber studs (2"×3" at 400mm centers); timber wales (2"×4" at 600mm vertical spacing); form ties (snap ties or threaded rod with wing nuts); (i) concrete volume per W1044 — mix ratio 1:2:4 (Class A) for structural retaining walls; (j) drainage: perforated PVC drain pipe (110mm diameter) along wall base with gravel surround; weep holes at 1.5m centers | System | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 3 | **Foundation Formwork Material Calculation**: System calculates formwork materials: (a) **Footing formwork**: (i) plywood area = 2 × (footing length + footing width) × footing depth per footing × number of footings; (ii) studs: 2"×3" at 400mm centers along plywood; (iii) braces: 2"×4" diagonal braces to prevent form bulging under concrete pressure; (iv) form ties: snap ties per lineal meter of formwork; (b) **Column formwork**: (i) plywood area = column perimeter × column height × number of columns; (ii) yokes/clamps: at 400mm vertical spacing (made from 2"×4" lumber or steel column clamps); (iii) kicker: bottom form to prevent grout leakage; (c) **Beam formwork**: (i) plywood area = 2 × beam depth × beam length + beam width × beam length (for soffit); (ii) soffit supports: 2"×4" joists at 400mm centers; (iii) shores/posts: 4"×4" lumber at 1.0m centers to support beam soffit; (iv) side forms: 2"×3" studs at 400mm centers with 2"×4" wales; (d) **Slab formwork**: (i) plywood area = slab area (sqm); (ii) joists: 2"×4" at 400mm centers; (iii) stringers: 2"×6" at 1.0m centers perpendicular to joists; (iv) shores: 4"×4" at 1.0m × 1.0m grid; (e) **Common formwork materials**: (i) form release agent (oil or emulsion — prevents concrete from sticking to plywood); (ii) nails (assorted: 2" for plywood-to-stud, 3" for stud-to-wale, 4" for braces); (iii) tie wire (16-gauge black annealed wire for reinforcement tying); (iv) spacers: concrete cover spacers (25mm or 50mm) to maintain rebar cover; (f) lumber reuse factor: plywood = 4–5 uses (for typical construction quality), timber = 6–8 uses; system estimates new lumber purchase vs. potential reuse for customers with multiple pours | System | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min (automated) |
| 4 | **Companion Materials & Complete BOM**: System adds companion materials: (a) **Concrete materials** per W1044: cement, sand, gravel — quantities based on total concrete volume from steps 2/3; (b) **Reinforcement steel** per W986: rebar cutting and bending schedule; tie wire quantity; rebar chairs/spacers; (c) **Waterproofing**: for retaining walls — apply waterproofing membrane (cementitious or bituminous) to the back face (soil side) before backfilling; quantity based on wall area; (d) **Backfill and drainage**: gravel (¾" crushed stone) for drainage layer behind wall; filter fabric (non-woven geotextile) to prevent soil clogging the drainage; perforated PVC drain pipe (110mm); (e) **Compaction**: gravel base compaction — manual tamper for small projects, plate compactor rental per W1094 for larger projects; (f) **Tools**: carpentry tools for formwork (hammer, saw, level, plumb bob, measuring tape, string line), concrete tools (wheelbarrow, shovel, trowel, vibrator rental per W1094), and rebar tools (bolt cutter or hacksaw, bending tool, tie wire twister) | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 2–3 min (automated) |
| 5 | **Estimate, Safety Advisory & Professional Referral**: (a) system generates itemized estimate with: structural sketch (simplified section view of retaining wall or formwork layout), complete BOM organized by category (structural, concrete, reinforcement, formwork, drainage, tools), quantities and prices, total estimated cost; (b) safety and engineering advisory: "Retaining walls exceeding 1.0m height and all structural foundations must be designed by a licensed Civil Engineer. The National Structural Code of the Philippines (NSCP) 2015 governs structural design in Seismic Zone 4. This material estimation is for quantity purposes only and does not constitute a structural design. BuildRight Depot strongly recommends engaging a licensed Civil Engineer to design and supervise the construction of retaining walls and foundations."; (c) for retaining walls > 3.0m: system requires a disclaimer that the estimation is for preliminary budgeting only and must not be used for construction without a professional engineer's design; (d) system offers referral to licensed civil engineers and contractors per W904; (e) estimate saved to customer loyalty account | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Retaining wall material calculator (CHB and RC wall types)
- Formwork material calculator (footing, column, beam, slab types)
- Concrete mix calculator integration (W1044)
- Rebar calculator integration (W986)
- Product attribute master (W298) — lumber dimensions, CHB specifications, rebar weights
- Real-time inventory availability per store (W533)
- POS quotation module (W542)
- Loyalty account integration (W17)
- Contractor referral service module (W904)

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Structural safety liability**: Retaining wall failures can cause property damage, injury, and death; the disclaimer must be prominent and the Associate must verbally emphasize the need for professional engineering design for walls > 1.0m
- **Seismic design complexity**: Philippine Seismic Zone 4 requires specific reinforcement and design considerations that cannot be addressed by a simple material calculator; the system must not produce designs that appear to substitute for professional engineering
- **Concrete quality sensitivity**: Retaining wall concrete must achieve specified strength (typically 3,000–4,000 PSI / 20–28 MPa for structural walls); improper concrete mix ratio or inadequate curing leads to structural weakness; concrete mix instructions per W1044 must be precise
- **Formwork failure risk**: Formwork collapse during concrete pouring is a leading cause of construction accidents in the Philippines; the formwork material estimation must include adequate bracing and the instruction card must emphasize formwork inspection before pouring

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Lumber/Building Materials Section)**: Estimation consultation adds 15–25 minutes per customer; at ~10–15 consultations per store per week, this represents ~3–6 hours/week — absorbed by existing Lumber Department staff
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Project specification: 8–12 min
- Retaining wall calculation: 3–5 min (automated)
- Formwork calculation: 3–5 min (automated)
- Companion materials: 2–3 min (automated)
- Estimate & advisory: 3–5 min
- **Total per consultation**: 19–30 min
