## W1104. Customer Tool Rental Return Damage Assessment & Billing

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer returns a rented tool or equipment at the store customer service counter |
| **Frequency** | ~3,000–4,000 rental returns/month across all stores (complement to W139 tool rental operations) |
| **Volume** | 1–3 tools per return transaction |
| **Owner** | Customer Service Representative |
| **Participants** | Customer Service Representative, Department Supervisor (Tools), Customer |

### Background

BuildRight Depot operates a tool and equipment rental service (W139) allowing customers to rent power tools (drills, grinders, circular saws, jackhammers), specialty equipment (tile cutters, concrete mixers, scaffolding, pressure washers), and commercial-grade items not typically owned by DIY customers. The rental program is a differentiator for the trade/professional customer segment (30% of revenue) and drives foot traffic from contractors who also purchase consumables and materials during rental visits. Tool rental returns require a structured damage assessment process to: (a) determine if the tool is returned in the same condition as issued (normal wear vs. damage); (b) assess additional charges for damage beyond normal wear; (c) process the security deposit refund or partial charge; (d) determine if the tool needs repair, cleaning, or recalibration before re-rental; (e) update the tool's maintenance history in the rental asset tracking system. This workflow specifically covers the return and damage assessment process; the initial rental issuance and overall rental operations are covered under W139.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Rental Record Retrieval & Pre-Return Verification**: (a) Customer Service Representative (CSR) scans the customer's rental agreement barcode or looks up by loyalty card/phone number; (b) system displays: tool ID, tool description, rental start date/time, agreed return date/time, rental rate, security deposit amount, pre-rental condition notes, and photos of tool at issuance; (c) CSR verifies customer identity (government ID matching rental agreement); (d) system auto-calculates elapsed rental time and any overdue charges: overdue rate = 1.5× standard daily rate per day late | Customer Service Representative | Customer Service Representative | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **Physical Tool Inspection & Condition Comparison**: CSR inspects returned tool against pre-rental condition: (a) visual inspection for new scratches, dents, cracks, or missing parts; (b) functional test: power on, run for 30 seconds, check for unusual noise or vibration; (c) accessory check: verify all accessories listed at issuance are returned (blades, bits, chargers, batteries, cables, manuals, carrying case); (d) cleanliness check: tool should be returned free of excessive concrete dust, paint, or mud (reasonable use debris is acceptable); (e) for electrical tools: inspect cord for cuts, check plug integrity; (f) for gas-powered equipment: check fuel level (should be returned with minimum fuel), oil condition; (g) for scaffolding: verify all pins, braces, and platforms are present and undamaged; (h) CSR photographs any damage or missing items using store tablet | Customer Service Representative | Department Supervisor (Tools) | 5–10 min |
| 3 | **Damage Classification & Assessment**: CSR classifies tool condition: (a) **Normal Wear** — minor cosmetic scratches, expected consumable wear (blade dulling, brush wear), dust/debris from normal use → no additional charge; (b) **Minor Damage** — small dent, scuffed housing, missing low-value accessory (screw, washer) → flat PHP 150–500 cleaning/minor repair surcharge; (c) **Moderate Damage** — cracked housing, damaged cord, bent blade, broken accessory → repair cost estimate generated by system based on tool type and damage code, typically PHP 500–2,000; (d) **Major Damage** — motor burnout, cracked frame, missing major component (battery, blade guard) → full repair or replacement cost, capped at the tool's current replacement value; (e) **Total Loss** — tool returned non-functional, submerged in water, dropped from height, or stolen → security deposit forfeited + additional charge up to replacement value per rental agreement terms. For categories (c)–(e), Department Supervisor is called for visual confirmation and approval | Customer Service Representative | Department Supervisor (Tools) | 5–8 min |
| 4 | **Security Deposit Settlement & Additional Billing**: (a) system calculates final bill: base rental charge + overdue charges (if any) + damage surcharge (if any) - security deposit held; (b) if net amount is positive (customer owes more): customer pays balance via POS (W5B); (c) if net amount is negative (deposit exceeds charges): refund processed to original payment method per W101 (customer refund processing), or issued as store credit per W781; (d) system generates itemized rental return receipt with condition assessment details; (e) customer signs digital acknowledgment of return condition; (f) if customer disputes damage assessment, escalate to Store Manager per dispute resolution hierarchy | Customer Service Representative / POS | Department Supervisor (Tools) | 5–7 min |
| 5 | **Post-Return Tool Reconditioning & Availability Update**: (a) tool placed in designated "inspection/reconditioning" area in backroom; (b) if **Normal Wear**: CSR cleans tool (compressed air, wipe down), functional test confirmation, return to rental shelf; system updates tool status to "Available"; (c) if **Minor/Moderate Damage**: tool sent to in-store repair station (W440 — power tool service & repair center) with damage assessment form; system updates status to "In Repair" with estimated availability date; (d) if **Major Damage / Total Loss**: tool dispositioned per W91 (damaged goods disposition) if uneconomical to repair, or sent to vendor for factory refurbishment; insurance claim filed per W859 (vehicle & fleet insurance) if rental tool is covered under rental equipment policy; (e) system tracks repair turnaround time and updates rental availability calendar | Stock Associate / CSR | Department Supervisor (Tools) | 10–20 min (for normal wear); varies for repair |

### System Touchpoints
- Tool rental management module — agreement lookup, inventory status, availability calendar
- Pre-rental condition photo repository (linked to tool asset ID)
- POS module (W5B) — rental return billing and deposit settlement
- Customer refund processing (W101) — deposit refund
- Store credit issuance (W781) — credit in lieu of cash refund
- Power tool repair center module (W440) — repair work order creation
- Damaged goods disposition (W91) — write-off for total loss
- Fixed asset tracking — rental tool depreciation and lifecycle (W39)
- Customer loyalty integration — rental history tracked for tier benefits

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Subjective damage assessment**: "Normal wear" vs. "minor damage" can be subjective; photography at issuance and return is critical evidence but adds processing time
- **Customer disputes**: Contractors who use tools heavily may contest damage charges; clear rental agreement terms and photographic evidence are essential
- **Rental tool downtime**: Damaged tools in repair reduce available rental fleet, potentially losing rental revenue; a 5–10% fleet buffer is recommended
- **Hygiene concerns**: Returned tools that have been used in construction sites (concrete dust, paint, adhesives) require thorough cleaning before re-rental
- **Liability for tool malfunction**: If a tool is returned damaged but not flagged, and subsequently rented to another customer who is injured, BuildRight faces liability exposure

### Staffing Implication
- **Customer Service Representative**: Tool return processing adds 15–30 minutes per return; at ~15–20 returns/store/week, this represents ~4–6 hours/week — absorbed by existing CSR (1 per store)
- **Department Supervisor (Tools)**: Damage escalation review adds ~1–2 hours/week during peak rental periods
- **No permanent incremental headcount** — damage surcharge revenue (estimated PHP 100,000–200,000/month chain-wide) more than covers processing labor

### Time Estimate
- Record retrieval: 3–5 min
- Physical inspection: 5–10 min
- Damage classification: 5–8 min
- Billing settlement: 5–7 min
- Tool reconditioning: 10–20 min (normal wear)
- **Total per return**: 28–50 min

## W1109. Customer Project Material Surplus Buy-Back & Recycling Program

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer brings unused/surplus building materials to store for buy-back, or customer requests a project completion surplus pickup |
| **Frequency** | ~3,000–5,000 surplus buy-back transactions/month across all stores |
| **Volume** | 1–10 items per transaction |
| **Owner** | Customer Service Representative |
| **Participants** | Customer Service Representative, Department Supervisor, Customer |

### Background

Filipino contractors and DIY homeowners frequently end up with surplus building materials after project completion: unused cement bags (leftover from a pour), extra tiles (bought 10% extra for wastage but didn't use all), unopened paint cans, extra lumber pieces, surplus electrical wire, and leftover plumbing fittings. In the Philippines, the common practice is to either: (a) store the surplus indefinitely (cluttering homes and job sites), (b) sell to neighbors at a discount, or (c) discard as construction waste. BuildRight Depot's surplus buy-back program creates a structured channel for customers to return unused materials for a partial refund or store credit, which BuildRight can then resell as open-box/discounted items (per W549) or return to vendors (per W88). This program: (i) drives customer loyalty by reducing the perceived risk of over-buying; (ii) generates foot traffic as customers return to the store for the buy-back and often purchase additional items; (iii) provides a source of discounted inventory for budget-conscious customers; (iv) supports sustainability goals by reducing construction waste. This workflow is distinct from W12 (returns & exchanges) which handles defective or unwanted items within the standard return window; this workflow specifically handles post-project surplus materials that may be beyond the standard return period but are in resalable condition.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Surplus Material Intake & Eligibility Check**: (a) Customer brings surplus materials to the customer service counter; (b) CSR verifies eligibility: (i) items must be BuildRight-branded or identifiable as BuildRight inventory (receipt, loyalty account purchase history, or SKU barcode scan); (ii) items must be in resalable condition: unopened packaging (cement bags intact, tile boxes sealed, paint cans unopened) or minimally used and clean (lumber without damage, full-length); (iii) items must not be hazardous materials requiring special handling (paint/chemicals must be unopened); (iv) items must be in the current active catalog (not discontinued); (c) system looks up original purchase price from customer's transaction history; (d) items not meeting eligibility criteria are declined with explanation and disposal guidance offered per W502 (non-hazardous waste management) | Customer Service Representative | Customer Service Representative | 5–8 min |
| 2 | **Condition Grading & Buy-Back Valuation**: (a) CSR grades each item's condition: **Grade A** — unopened, original packaging intact, current catalog item → buy-back at 70% of original purchase price; **Grade B** — opened but complete and undamaged, or minor cosmetic imperfection → buy-back at 50% of original purchase price; **Grade C** — partial quantity (e.g., half a bag of cement, cut lumber), clean and usable → buy-back at 30% of original purchase price; (b) system auto-calculates buy-back values based on grade and original purchase price; (c) customer chooses compensation: (i) store credit (additional 10% bonus on buy-back value, incentivizing reinvestment at BuildRight), (ii) cash refund via GCash or bank transfer (3–5 day processing), (iii) loyalty points (converted at standard rate); (d) Department Supervisor reviews and approves any single transaction exceeding PHP 10,000 in buy-back value | Customer Service Representative | Department Supervisor (if > PHP 10K) | 5–10 min |
| 3 | **Surplus Item Processing & Resale Preparation**: (a) surplus items are processed for resale: Grade A items restocked to original shelf location via standard inventory putaway; Grade B items labeled as "Open Box — Surplus Buy-Back" with discounted price per W549 (damaged/open-box item processing) and placed in designated clearance area; Grade C items labeled as "Partial/Remnant — Surplus" with calculated price and placed in the remnant/cutoff section (common for lumber, wire, pipes); (b) system creates inventory receipt at buy-back cost (not original cost) to ensure accurate margin tracking; (c) resale price set by system: Grade A at 90% SRP, Grade B at 70% SRP, Grade C at 50% SRP (or per-unit pricing for remnants); (d) buy-back inventory flagged in system for shrinkage reporting exclusion (to avoid inflating shrinkage numbers with intentional markdowns) | Stock Associate / System | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |
| 4 | **Accounting & Reporting**: (a) buy-back transaction recorded: debit Inventory (at buy-back cost), debit Buy-Back Expense (difference between buy-back cost and original cost if still on hand), credit Cash/Store Credit/GC Payable; (b) monthly buy-back program report: total items bought back by category, total buy-back cost, total resale revenue, net program margin, customer participation rate; (c) program ROI calculated: (resale revenue − buy-back cost − processing labor) / buy-back cost; (d) report shared with Category Manager for pricing optimization and program viability assessment | System / Finance | Category Manager | automated monthly |

### System Touchpoints
- Customer purchase history lookup (loyalty account / transaction search)
- Inventory receipt module — buy-back inventory creation at buy-back cost
- Open-box / clearance pricing module (W549) — resale pricing
- Store credit issuance (W781) — compensation processing
- GCash / bank transfer module (W99) — cash refund
- Loyalty points module (W17) — points conversion
- GL posting — buy-back expense and inventory accounting
- Shrinkage reporting module (W845) — buy-back exclusion flag
- Category performance reporting (W101) — program analytics

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Fraud risk**: Customers may attempt to buy back items purchased at other retailers or items they did not actually purchase; receipt/loyalty account verification mitigates this
- **Storage and display**: Grade B/C items require dedicated clearance floor space that may compete with full-price merchandise display
- **Cement bag integrity**: Opened cement bags are effectively worthless (cement hardens quickly); Grade C cement is not accepted
- **Tile shade matching**: Surplus tiles from different production batches may have slight shade variations; resale must note "surplus — shade may vary from current stock"
- **Margin erosion**: If too many customers over-buy expecting easy buy-back, it shifts inventory risk back to BuildRight; buy-back pricing at 30–70% of original creates a natural deterrent

### Staffing Implication
- **Customer Service Representative**: Buy-back processing adds 15–25 minutes per transaction; at ~15–25 per store per week, this represents ~4–6 hours/week — absorbed by existing CSR
- **Stock Associate**: Resale preparation adds ~2–3 hours/week across all grades
- **No permanent incremental headcount** — program is expected to be margin-positive from resale revenue

### Time Estimate
- Intake & eligibility: 5–8 min
- Grading & valuation: 5–10 min
- Resale preparation: 10–15 min
- **Total per transaction**: 20–33 min

## W1113. Customer E-Gift Card Purchase & Digital Delivery

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer purchases an e-gift card via BuildRight website, mobile app, or in-store |
| **Frequency** | ~15,000–20,000 e-gift card purchases/month (growing segment, especially during holidays and gift-giving occasions) |
| **Volume** | 1–5 e-gift cards per purchase transaction |
| **Owner** | Ecommerce Operations Manager |
| **Participants** | Customer (purchaser), Customer (recipient), Ecommerce Platform, POS System, Finance (GL) |

### Background

Gift cards are an important revenue and customer acquisition channel for retail. BuildRight currently manages physical gift cards (W28 — gift card & store credit lifecycle) but the e-gift card segment — digital gift cards purchased online and delivered via email or SMS — is growing rapidly, driven by: (a) OFW (Overseas Filipino Worker) gift-giving — OFWs sending digital gift cards to family in the Philippines for home improvement projects; (b) corporate bulk purchases — companies buying e-gift cards as employee rewards or Christmas gifts; (c) last-minute gifting — customers who need a gift immediately and cannot visit a store; (d) birthday/holiday gifts — especially during ber months (Sep–Dec) when gift-giving peaks in the Philippines. E-gift cards differ from physical gift cards in several operational aspects: (i) no physical inventory to manage or secure; (ii) instant delivery via email/SMS; (iii) redemption via QR code on mobile screen (no physical card to present); (iv) higher fraud risk (digital theft, unauthorized purchases); (v) different accounting treatment (immediate liability recognition vs. deferred for physical cards awaiting shipment). This workflow covers the end-to-end e-gift card lifecycle from purchase to redemption, complementing W28 (physical gift card) and W896 (corporate/bulk gift card purchases).

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **E-Gift Card Purchase & Personalization**: (a) customer selects e-gift card on BuildRight website/app or at POS: (i) chooses denomination: PHP 500, PHP 1,000, PHP 2,000, PHP 5,000, or custom amount (min PHP 200, max PHP 50,000); (ii) selects design/theme: Birthday, Wedding, Housewarming, Congratulations, Holiday, Generic; (iii) enters recipient name, email address, and mobile number; (iv) writes personal message (max 200 characters); (v) selects delivery date: immediate or scheduled future date (up to 90 days ahead); (vi) pays via CC, GCash, Maya, or bank transfer; (b) system validates: purchaser's payment is successful, recipient email/mobile is valid format, total purchase amount is within anti-money laundering limits (single purchase ≤ PHP 50,000 per BSP guidelines) | Customer / System | Ecommerce Operations Manager | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **E-Gift Card Generation & Digital Delivery**: (a) system generates unique e-gift card: 16-digit card number, 4-digit PIN, QR code, and barcode — all cryptographically generated with checksum validation; (b) system creates personalized e-gift card image with selected design, recipient name, personal message, sender name, and amount; (c) system records liability: debit Cash/Receivable, credit Gift Card Liability (deferred revenue) at full face value; (d) delivery: (i) email with e-gift card image as attachment and embedded redemption instructions; (ii) SMS to recipient's mobile with shortened link to e-gift card; (iii) both include: card number, PIN, QR code, expiration date (24 months from purchase per BuildRight policy), terms and conditions, and customer service contact; (e) purchaser receives confirmation email with delivery status; (f) for scheduled delivery, system queues the email/SMS for the selected date | System | automated | < 1 min |
| 3 | **E-Gift Card Redemption at POS or Online**: (a) recipient uses e-gift card at any BuildRight store or online: (i) **In-Store**: customer presents e-gift card QR code on mobile screen at POS; cashier scans QR code; system validates: card number exists, PIN matches, card has remaining balance, card is not expired; balance displayed on cashier screen; customer enters PIN on pin pad for security; transaction amount deducted from card balance; (ii) **Online**: customer enters card number and PIN at checkout; system validates and applies available balance; remaining balance (if any) displayed after transaction; (b) system updates: (i) gift card liability reduced by transaction amount; (ii) revenue recognized at redemption (not at purchase, per revenue recognition per W487 PFRS 15); (iii) remaining balance tracked on card record; (c) partial redemption is allowed; remaining balance stays on the card for future use; (d) if transaction amount exceeds gift card balance, customer pays the difference via another tender type (split payment per multi-tender POS support) | Cashier / System / Customer | Store Manager / Ecommerce Operations Manager | 2–3 min additional at POS |
| 4 | **E-Gift Card Balance Inquiry & Re-Send**: (a) customer can check balance online (buildright.com.ph/giftcard-balance), via mobile app, or at any store POS; (b) if recipient did not receive the e-gift card email/SMS: purchaser can request re-send from order confirmation page or by contacting customer service (W258); system re-sends to the same or updated email/mobile; (c) e-gift card cannot be re-sent to a different recipient after original delivery (to prevent fraud) | System / Customer Service | automated | 1–2 min |
| 5 | **Monthly E-Gift Card Reconciliation & Liability Reporting**: (a) Finance performs monthly reconciliation: (i) total e-gift card liability (unredeemed balance); (ii) redemption rate by cohort (month of purchase vs. month of redemption); (iii) breakage estimate (expected unredeemed portion recognized as revenue per historical patterns); (iv) fraud incidents and chargebacks; (b) system auto-recognizes breakage revenue for cards older than 24 months (expired, unredeemed) per W939 (store credit expiration management); (c) report submitted to VP Finance for liability management and program health assessment | System / Finance | VP Finance | 2–3 hours/month |

### System Touchpoints
- E-commerce platform — e-gift card purchase flow, personalization
- Payment gateway (GCash, Maya, CC, bank transfer) — payment processing
- Gift card management module — unique card generation, balance tracking, redemption processing
- POS system (W5B) — QR code scanning, balance inquiry, split tender
- Email/SMS gateway — digital delivery
- GL module — gift card liability accounting, breakage revenue recognition
- Anti-fraud module — purchase velocity limits, suspicious transaction detection
- Customer service ticketing (W258) — re-send requests, balance inquiries

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Digital gift card fraud**: Stolen credit cards used to purchase e-gift cards, which are then resold or used for merchandise; velocity limits (max 3 purchases per day per purchaser) and 24-hour hold on first-time purchasers mitigate this
- **Email delivery failures**: Philippine email spam filters or incorrect email addresses can prevent delivery; SMS backup and re-send functionality address this
- **Mobile QR code scanning issues**: Cracked phone screens, low brightness, or expired mobile data can prevent successful QR code scanning at POS; manual card number + PIN entry is the fallback
- **Liability management**: Large unredeemed gift card balances represent a financial liability; breakage recognition must comply with PFRS 15 (W487)
- **AML compliance**: Per BSP regulations, gift card purchases may be subject to AML reporting (W961) if used for money laundering; PHP 50,000 single-purchase limit mitigates this

### Staffing Implication
- **Ecommerce Operations Manager**: Program oversight adds ~2–3 hours/week
- **Finance**: Monthly reconciliation adds 2–3 hours/month
- **Customer Service**: Re-send and balance inquiry requests add ~1–2 hours/week across the call center
- **No permanent incremental headcount** — system is highly automated

### Time Estimate
- Purchase: 3–5 min (customer self-service)
- Generation & delivery: < 1 min (automated)
- Redemption: 2–3 min additional at POS
- Monthly reconciliation: 2–3 hours/month (Finance)
- **Total per transaction**: 6–9 min (customer-facing); < 1 min system processing

## W1114. Customer Product Availability Real-Time Stock Lookup & Reservation Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer inquiry about product availability via mobile app, website, phone call, or in-store associate |
| **Frequency** | ~50,000–80,000 stock lookup requests/month across all channels |
| **Volume** | 1–5 SKUs per lookup |
| **Owner** | Ecommerce Operations Manager (digital channels); Customer Service Representative (phone/in-store) |
| **Participants** | Customer, Sales Associate, Customer Service Representative, E-commerce Platform |

### Background

BuildRight Depot carries 35,000 active SKUs across 200 stores and 4 DCs. Customers frequently need to know if a specific item is available at their preferred store before making a trip — especially for bulky items (cement, plywood, tiles) where a wasted trip is costly and frustrating. Current inventory visibility is near-real-time (< 30 seconds latency per POS-013), but customers need an easy way to check availability and optionally reserve items for pickup. Key use cases: (a) contractor checking if 200 bags of cement are available at the nearest store before dispatching a truck; (b) DIY homeowner confirming a specific faucet model is in stock before driving 30 minutes to the store; (c) online shopper seeing "Available at [Store Name] — Reserve for pickup" on the product page; (d) call center agent checking stock for a phone inquiry. This workflow manages the real-time stock lookup and optional reservation process, complementing W11 (BOPIS order fulfillment) which handles the full purchase-and-pickup cycle, and W930 (back-in-stock notification) which handles out-of-stock alerts. This workflow specifically covers the inquiry and reservation (hold) function without requiring immediate payment.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Real-Time Stock Inquiry**: (a) customer initiates stock lookup via: (i) BuildRight mobile app — search by SKU, barcode scan, or product name; app shows availability at all stores within selected radius (default: 20km); (ii) website — product page shows "Check availability at your store" with store selector dropdown; (iii) phone call to customer service (W259) — agent looks up SKU in system; (iv) in-store — Sales Associate checks via handheld RF device or store tablet; (b) system queries real-time inventory: for each store within range, displays: (i) current available-to-promise (ATP) quantity (on-hand minus reserved for existing orders); (ii) stock status indicator: ● In Stock (≥ display threshold), ○ Low Stock (1–3 units), ◌ Out of Stock; (iii) aisle/section location within the store (e.g., "Aisle 3, Bay 7 — Plumbing"); (iv) next expected replenishment date (from supply planning module); (c) for high-demand items with limited stock, system shows "X other customers are viewing this item at [Store]" to create urgency | System / Customer | automated | < 3 seconds |
| 2 | **Reservation Request & Stock Hold**: (a) if item is in stock, customer can choose to reserve: (i) select quantity and store; (ii) choose reservation duration: 2 hours (free), 4 hours (free), end of today (free), or until store closing tomorrow (PHP 50 reservation fee, refundable upon purchase); (iii) provide name and mobile number for notification; (b) system creates a stock reservation: (i) ATP quantity reduced by reserved amount (visible to other customers as "X reserved"); (ii) customer receives SMS confirmation with reservation ID, item, quantity, store name, and hold expiration time; (iii) store receiving desk and customer service counter receive reservation notification; (c) reservation limits per customer: max 5 reservations active at any time, max 10 units per SKU per reservation, max reservation value of PHP 100,000 | Customer / System | Ecommerce Operations Manager | 1–2 min |
| 3 | **Reservation Fulfillment & Expiry Management**: (a) customer arrives at store and presents reservation ID (SMS on phone) at customer service counter; (b) CSR verifies reservation: (i) reservation ID matches active reservation; (ii) customer name/ID matches; (iii) reservation has not expired; (c) CSR directs customer to the item's aisle location or retrieves from backroom if pre-staged; (d) customer proceeds to POS for purchase — reservation ID scanned, hold released, inventory deducted; (e) if customer does not arrive before expiration: (i) system automatically releases the reservation; (ii) ATP quantity restored; (iii) customer receives SMS notification: "Your reservation for [Item] at [Store] has expired. The item is now available to other customers."; (iv) if reservation fee was paid (PHP 50): fee forfeited and recorded as miscellaneous revenue | System / Customer Service Representative | Customer Service Representative | 3–5 min at pickup |
| 4 | **Stock Lookup Analytics & Demand Signal Capture**: (a) system captures all stock lookup events (whether reserved or not) as demand signals: (i) items frequently searched but out of stock → potential lost sales, flagged to Category Manager for assortment review (W679); (ii) stores frequently searched for items they don't carry → potential assortment gap; (iii) items with high lookup-to-reservation conversion but low reservation-to-purchase conversion → possible store-level fulfillment issues; (b) analytics dashboard updated daily for Category Managers and Supply Planners; (c) data feeds into demand forecasting (W31) as a leading indicator | System | Category Manager | automated |

### System Touchpoints
- Real-time inventory module — ATP calculation across all locations
- Mobile app — stock lookup, reservation request
- Website — product page availability check
- Customer service module (W259) — agent-assisted lookup
- RF handheld devices — in-store associate lookup
- Reservation management module — hold creation, tracking, expiry
- SMS gateway — reservation confirmation and expiry notifications
- POS system — reservation ID scanning, hold release
- Demand signal analytics — lost sale tracking, search-to-conversion funnels
- Supply planning module (W31) — demand signal feed

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Inventory accuracy dependency**: Stock lookups are only as good as inventory data; if physical stock doesn't match system stock (accuracy target ≥ 97%), customers will have a poor experience
- **Gaming by customers**: Customers may reserve items speculatively to "hold" stock while shopping around competitors; the 2–4 hour free hold window and PHP 50 next-day fee mitigate this
- **ATP calculation complexity**: ATP must account for: on-hand stock, existing reservations, pending BOPIS orders, pending transfer orders, and incoming replenishment — any calculation error leads to over-promising
- **Store associate awareness**: If store associates are not aware of reservations, they may sell reserved stock to walk-in customers before the reserving customer arrives; system must prevent this through POS-level ATP deduction
- **Mobile app performance in low-signal areas**: Philippine provinces may have poor mobile data coverage; app must cache recent lookups and show last-known availability with timestamp

### Staffing Implication
- **Customer Service Representative**: Reservation pickup handling adds 3–5 minutes per pickup; at ~10–15 pickups/store/week, this represents ~1 hour/week — minimal impact
- **No permanent incremental headcount** — the service is primarily digital and automated

### Time Estimate
- Stock lookup: < 3 seconds (automated)
- Reservation creation: 1–2 min (customer self-service)
- Pickup: 3–5 min (in-store)
- Expiry management: automated
- **Total per customer interaction**: 4–7 min (customer time); minimal staff time

## W1122. Customer Project Material Delivery Photo Documentation & Proof Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Delivery of project materials to a customer's construction site or home, especially for B2B/trade accounts and staged deliveries |
| **Frequency** | ~8,000–12,000 project deliveries/month requiring photo documentation (primarily B2B/trade, high-value, and staged deliveries) |
| **Volume** | 5–15 photos per delivery |
| **Owner** | Delivery Driver / Logistics Coordinator |
| **Participants** | Delivery Driver, Customer (Site Representative), Logistics Coordinator, Trade Account Manager |

### Background

BuildRight Depot delivers materials to construction sites and homes for both B2C (home delivery per W19) and B2B (project deliveries per W164, W980) customers. Material deliveries to construction sites carry unique risks that standard delivery proof (signature on delivery receipt) does not adequately address: (a) **Dispute risk**: Customer claims not all items were delivered ("I ordered 500 bags of cement but only received 450") — without photographic evidence, BuildRight must absorb the shortage cost; (b) **Damage in transit**: Materials damaged during unloading at site (cement bags torn, tiles chipped, lumber scratched) — without before/after photos, it's unclear whether damage occurred during BuildRight's handling or the customer's; (c) **Staged delivery reconciliation**: For project accounts with 5–10 staged deliveries over months (W164), photographic proof of each stage provides an auditable trail for milestone billing (W165); (d) **Site condition documentation**: Photos of the delivery location (driveway accessibility, unloading area condition, existing structures) protect BuildRight from claims of property damage during delivery; (e) **Insurance claims**: If materials are damaged by weather or theft after delivery but before installation, delivery photos prove the materials were delivered in good condition, supporting the customer's insurance claim (W858). This workflow establishes a systematic photo documentation protocol for project material deliveries, complementing W811 (wholesale delivery proof & POD reconciliation) and W592 (ecommerce delivery tracking & POD management).

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pre-Delivery Preparation & Delivery Order Assignment**: (a) Logistics Coordinator assigns delivery to driver with delivery order details: (i) customer name, trade account number (if applicable); (ii) delivery address and site contact person/number; (iii) itemized material list with quantities; (iv) special delivery instructions (e.g., "Enter through gate on south side," "Unload inside garage," "Forklift delivery — ensure site has compacted surface"); (v) whether photo documentation is required: mandatory for all B2B/trade deliveries, B2C deliveries > PHP 20,000, and all staged project deliveries; (b) driver reviews delivery order on handheld tablet and plans route | Logistics Coordinator / Driver | Logistics Coordinator | 10–15 min |
| 2 | **On-Site Arrival & Condition Documentation**: (a) upon arrival at delivery site, driver photographs: (i) **Site approach photo**: truck at the delivery location, showing the site entrance and surrounding area (establishes delivery was made to the correct address); (ii) **Unloading area condition photo**: the area where materials will be placed, showing pre-existing conditions (existing damage, puddles, obstructions) — this protects BuildRight from claims of property damage; (iii) **Material on truck photo**: all materials visible on the truck before unloading, establishing the "before" condition of goods in BuildRight's custody; (b) photos are timestamped and GPS-tagged by the tablet camera (verifying location and time of arrival); (c) if site conditions are unfavorable (e.g., muddy, no access, no one to receive), driver contacts Logistics Coordinator for instructions before unloading | Driver | Logistics Coordinator | 5 min |
| 3 | **Unloading & Material Placement Documentation**: (a) driver unloads materials at the designated location; (b) during/after unloading, driver photographs: (i) **Material offloaded — grouped photo**: all materials placed at the delivery point, arranged so individual items/quantities are visible; (ii) **Close-up of material condition**: representative close-ups showing that cement bags are intact, tile boxes are sealed, lumber is undamaged, paint cans are unopened; (iii) **Quantity verification photo**: for counted items (bags, boxes, bundles), a photo showing the count — e.g., a row of 50 cement bags clearly showing the full count; (iv) **Special items photo**: any high-value or fragile items (power tools, glass, appliances) photographed individually with serial number visible if applicable; (v) **Placement photo**: materials in their final resting position, showing proximity to structures and weather protection (if covered/uncovered); (c) all photos automatically uploaded to cloud storage in real-time via driver's tablet (4G/LTE connection) | Driver | Logistics Coordinator | 10–15 min |
| 4 | **Customer Sign-Off & Digital POD**: (a) customer's site representative reviews the delivery: (i) verifies item count matches delivery order; (ii) inspects material condition; (b) if everything is correct: (i) site representative signs digital POD on driver's tablet (stylus or finger signature); (ii) system captures signature image, signer name, signer role (foreman, homeowner, site engineer), and timestamp; (iii) system generates digital delivery receipt with: item list, quantities, photos, signature, GPS coordinates, timestamp; (iv) receipt emailed to customer and Trade Account Manager; (v) receipt stored in document management (W255) linked to the delivery order and sales order; (c) if there are discrepancies: (i) driver photographs the discrepancy (e.g., 2 broken tile boxes); (ii) discrepancy noted on POD with quantity short/damaged; (iii) system triggers a shortage/damage investigation per W91 (damaged goods disposition) and W500 (transfer order in-transit damage claim); (iv) driver does not leave until discrepancy is documented and acknowledged by both parties | Driver / Customer Site Representative | Logistics Coordinator | 5–10 min |
| 5 | **Post-Delivery Photo Archive & Analytics**: (a) all delivery photos archived in cloud storage: (i) organized by delivery order number, date, and customer account; (ii) retained for 7 years (BIR requirement for transaction documentation); (iii) accessible to: Logistics Coordinator (operations), Trade Account Manager (customer service), Finance (billing dispute resolution), Legal (liability claims); (b) monthly delivery documentation compliance report: (i) % of required deliveries with complete photo documentation (target: ≥ 98%); (ii) common photo quality issues (blurry, missing categories, no GPS tag); (iii) dispute resolution effectiveness: % of delivery disputes resolved using photo evidence vs. requiring further investigation; (iv) average photos per delivery and average file size (for storage planning); (c) photo analytics used for: (i) driver performance scoring (documentation completeness); (ii) site risk assessment (difficult access sites flagged for future delivery planning); (iii) damage trend analysis (specific routes or handling methods causing more damage) | System / Logistics Coordinator | Logistics Manager | 1–2 hours/month |

### System Touchpoints
- Delivery order management module (W19) — order assignment, item list
- Driver handheld tablet — camera, GPS, timestamping
- Cloud photo storage — real-time upload, 7-year retention
- Digital POD module — signature capture, receipt generation
- Document management (W255) — delivery receipt archival
- Delivery tracking module (W592) — real-time delivery status
- Customer notification module — email delivery confirmation with photos
- Shortage/damage investigation module (W91, W500) — discrepancy handling
- Driver performance module — documentation compliance scoring
- BI analytics (W880) — compliance reporting

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Driver photo compliance**: Drivers may rush or skip photo documentation under time pressure; mandatory photo categories must be enforced by the tablet app (cannot complete delivery without all required photos)
- **Photo quality**: Poor lighting (early morning/late evening deliveries), rain (camera lens drops), or shaky hands produce unusable photos; photo quality check before submission is recommended
- **Storage cost**: 8,000–12,000 deliveries × 5–15 photos × 3–5 MB per photo = ~120–900 GB/month of photo storage; cloud storage cost must be budgeted (~PHP 50,000–150,000/month)
- **Customer privacy concerns**: Photographing a customer's home or construction site may raise privacy concerns; photo policy should be communicated in delivery terms and conditions, and photos should focus on materials, not residential interiors
- **Network connectivity**: Remote Philippine construction sites may have poor 4G/LTE signal; tablet must cache photos for upload when connectivity is restored

### Staffing Implication
- **Delivery Driver**: Photo documentation adds 15–20 minutes per delivery; at 5–8 deliveries/day, this adds 1–2 hours to the driver's daily schedule — factored into delivery route planning
- **Logistics Coordinator**: Monthly compliance review adds 1–2 hours/month
- **No permanent incremental headcount** — photo documentation reduces dispute resolution time (estimated saving of 10–15 hours/month chain-wide in dispute investigation)

### Time Estimate
- Pre-delivery preparation: 10–15 min
- On-site arrival photos: 5 min
- Unloading & material photos: 10–15 min
- Customer sign-off: 5–10 min
- **Total additional time per delivery**: 20–30 min (beyond standard delivery time)

---

*End of Additional Operational Workflows — Batch 10 (W1103–W1122)*

## W1124. Customer Construction Material Compatibility Cross-Reference & Substitution Advisory

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer inquiry about product compatibility, or system identifies out-of-stock item requiring substitution recommendation |
| **Frequency** | ~8,000–12,000 compatibility queries/month across all stores (peak during summer renovation season Mar–May) |
| **Volume** | 1–5 product pairs per query |
| **Owner** | Sales Associate (Department-specific) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate, Department Supervisor, Customer |

### Background

Home improvement and construction projects require materials that are technically compatible: (a) tile adhesive must match tile type (ceramic, porcelain, natural stone, large format); (b) paint primer must be compatible with surface material (concrete, wood, metal, previously painted); (c) electrical wire gauge must match circuit breaker amperage; (d) plumbing pipe material must match fitting type (PVC, PPR, copper, galvanized); (e) lumber span tables must match structural load requirements. Customers — especially DIYers (55% of revenue) — frequently purchase incompatible combinations that lead to project failures, product returns, and customer dissatisfaction. This workflow provides a structured compatibility advisory service at the store level, supported by an ERP-based cross-reference matrix and trained staff. It complements W279 (product substitution rules) by extending it to customer-facing advisory, and W971 (power tool battery compatibility checker) by broadening it to all product categories.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Need Identification**: (a) customer approaches sales associate with project description or product list; (b) sales associate identifies the project type: bathroom renovation, electrical installation, plumbing repair, roofing, painting, etc.; (c) determines customer skill level: professional contractor, experienced DIYer, or first-time DIYer; (d) captures key project parameters: room size, surface material, load requirements, environmental conditions (indoor/outdoor, wet/dry area) | Sales Associate | Sales Associate | 3–5 min |
| 2 | **Compatibility Cross-Reference Lookup**: (a) sales associate scans or searches primary product in ERP mobile app or in-store kiosk; (b) system displays compatibility matrix: required complementary products (adhesive, primer, connector, fastener), compatible brands/models, and incompatibility warnings; (c) system highlights common mismatch errors (e.g., "Using mastic adhesive with large-format porcelain tile — recommend modified thin-set mortar instead"); (d) for electrical and plumbing: system applies Philippine building code requirements (National Structural Code of the Philippines, Philippine Electrical Code) to validate specifications; (e) if primary product is out-of-stock, system suggests verified substitutes per W279 with compatibility confirmation | Sales Associate / System | Department Supervisor | 3–5 min |
| 3 | **Customer Advisory & Bundle Recommendation**: (a) sales associate presents compatibility-verified product selection to customer; (b) explains why certain combinations are required (e.g., "This waterproofing membrane requires this specific primer for proper adhesion — using a different primer will void the manufacturer warranty"); (c) offers complete bundle: all required complementary materials (adhesive, grout, spacers, waterproofing, tools) with bundle pricing per W910; (d) for complex projects (full bathroom renovation, electrical panel upgrade), recommends consultation with in-store design consultant (W148) or pro desk specialist (W112); (e) provides printed or emailed project material list with compatibility notes for future reference | Sales Associate | Sales Associate | 5–8 min |
| 4 | **Post-Sale Follow-Up & Issue Tracking**: (a) system logs compatibility advisory as part of customer's purchase history; (b) if customer returns with compatibility-related product failure (e.g., tile delamination due to wrong adhesive), the advisory record is referenced to determine if correct guidance was provided; (c) compatibility issues reported to merchandising team for product data improvement (W50 PIM); (d) recurring compatibility confusion flagged for better product labeling, shelf signage, or package bundling | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 2–3 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Product compatibility cross-reference matrix (ERP master data module, linked to W298 product attribute templates)
- Product substitution rules engine (W279)
- Mobile ERP app / in-store kiosk — customer-facing compatibility lookup
- Bundle pricing engine (W910)
- PIM system (W50) — product relationship and attribute data
- Customer purchase history module — advisory logging
- Returns module (W12) — compatibility failure analysis

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Data accuracy**: Compatibility matrix must be maintained by merchandising team with vendor input; outdated data can lead to incorrect recommendations
- **Liability**: Providing compatibility advice creates implied warranty risk; disclaimers must be clear that recommendations are advisory and customers should verify with licensed professionals for structural, electrical, and plumbing work
- **Training depth**: Sales associates need periodic training on new products and compatibility rules; high turnover (~15–20%) means continuous training investment
- **Edge cases**: Unusual substrate conditions (e.g., painting over previously oil-painted surfaces, tiling over existing tiles) require expert judgment beyond system recommendations

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate**: Compatibility queries add ~10–15 min per interaction; at ~40–60 queries/store/week, this represents ~7–15 hours/week — distributed across 12 sales associates per store, ~1 hour/week each
- **Department Supervisor**: Complex escalation queries add ~2–3 hours/week per supervisor
- **No permanent incremental headcount** — improved attach rate (estimated 15–25% increase in complementary product sales with active advisory) justifies staff time

### Time Estimate
- Need identification: 3–5 min
- Cross-reference lookup: 3–5 min
- Advisory & bundle: 5–8 min
- Post-sale logging: 2–3 min
- **Total per query**: 13–21 min

## W1126. Customer Bulk Cement & Sand Order Direct-to-Site Delivery Tracking

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer places bulk order for cement, sand, gravel, or aggregates requiring direct-to-construction-site delivery |
| **Frequency** | ~2,000–3,000 bulk DSD orders/month across all stores |
| **Volume** | 1–5 deliveries per order; ~50–500 bags of cement or 1–10 cubic meters of sand/gravel per delivery |
| **Owner** | Department Supervisor (Lumber & Building Materials) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate, Receiving Clerk, Delivery Partner (3PL), Customer |

### Background

Cement, sand, gravel, and aggregates are fundamental construction materials that are bulky, heavy, and uneconomical to double-handle through BuildRight's DC network. These items are delivered direct-to-site (DSD) from vendor or local quarry to the customer's construction site, representing ~8–10% of receipt count but a significant portion of COGS value. Bulk DSD orders present unique tracking challenges: (a) deliveries often go to informal construction sites without standard addresses; (b) cement bags are counted manually at point of delivery; (c) sand and gravel are measured by truck volume (cubic meters) with potential for short delivery; (d) customer may not be present at delivery site to receive; (e) delivery timing is critical for construction schedules — delayed cement delivery can halt concrete pouring schedules; (f) proof of delivery documentation is essential for invoicing and dispute resolution. This workflow complements W18 (DSD receiving at store) by focusing on customer-facing direct-to-site delivery, and W980 (construction site delivery scheduling) by adding bulk material-specific tracking.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Bulk Order Intake & Delivery Scheduling**: (a) customer (typically contractor or project account) requests bulk cement/sand/gravel delivery; specifies: delivery address (or GPS coordinates for construction sites), delivery date/time window, quantity (bags of cement, cubic meters of sand/gravel), product specifications (cement brand/grade, sand type — washed, fine, coarse); (b) sales associate enters order in ERP as DSD sales order with delivery scheduling; (c) system validates customer credit limit (W888 credit hold check) for project/trade accounts; (d) delivery fee calculated based on distance from nearest source (vendor depot or quarry) and volume; (e) order confirmed with customer: delivery date, time window (4-hour), driver contact number, and delivery instructions | Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |
| 2 | **Vendor/Querry Coordination & Dispatch**: (a) ERP sends purchase/delivery order to cement vendor or sand/gravel supplier; (b) for BuildRight-managed delivery: 3PL truck dispatched from vendor depot with delivery manifest; (c) for vendor-managed delivery: vendor dispatches directly with BuildRight tracking requirement; (d) system sends delivery confirmation SMS/email to customer with: driver name, plate number, estimated arrival time, delivery quantity, and site contact instructions; (e) GPS tracking activated for BuildRight-managed deliveries via fleet telematics (W199) | Supply Chain Coordinator (HQ) / 3PL | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 3 | **On-Site Delivery Verification**: (a) driver arrives at construction site, contacts customer's site representative; (b) for cement: site representative counts bags unloaded against delivery manifest; (c) for sand/gravel: volume verified by truck measurement (standard truck volumes: 1 cu.m., 3 cu.m., 6 cu.m., 10 cu.m.); (d) driver photographs delivery: loaded truck before unloading, unloading process, delivered material on-site, and customer's site representative; (e) site representative signs delivery receipt on driver's mobile device (digital POD); (f) if short delivery or quality issue: discrepancy noted on digital POD with photos; (g) GPS coordinates and timestamp auto-captured by delivery app | Delivery Driver / Customer Site Rep | Department Supervisor | 15–30 min |
| 4 | **Delivery Confirmation & Invoicing**: (a) delivery app syncs POD data to ERP in near-real-time; (b) system matches delivery quantity to sales order: full delivery → auto-invoice generated and sent to customer; partial delivery → system creates backorder for remaining quantity per W56; (c) for COD customers: payment collected by driver (cash) or via mobile payment (GCash) at delivery; (d) for trade/project accounts: invoice added to account with agreed payment terms; (e) delivery exception (shortage, damage, refusal) triggers customer service follow-up within 4 hours | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 5–10 min |
| 5 | **Monthly DSD Performance Review**: (a) monthly report generated: on-time delivery rate, delivery accuracy (quantity match rate), customer complaint rate, average delivery lead time by region; (b) vendor DSD performance reviewed per W44; (c) 3PL delivery partner performance reviewed per W242; (d) delivery fee accuracy reviewed and adjusted quarterly | Supply Chain Coordinator (HQ) | VP Supply Chain | 2–3 hours/month |

### System Touchpoints
- ERP sales order module — DSD order creation with delivery scheduling
- Credit management module (W888) — credit limit check
- Fleet telematics / GPS tracking (W199) — real-time delivery tracking
- Mobile delivery app — digital POD capture with GPS and photos
- Invoice auto-generation module — delivery-triggered billing
- Backorder management (W56) — partial delivery processing
- 3PL performance module (W242) — delivery partner scoring
- Customer notification engine — SMS/email delivery status updates

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Informal site addresses**: Many Philippine construction sites lack formal addresses; GPS coordinates and landmark descriptions are essential
- **Volume measurement disputes**: Sand and gravel delivered by volume is inherently imprecise; customer may claim short delivery; photographic evidence is critical
- **Weather delays**: Heavy rain makes construction site roads impassable; delivery may need to be rescheduled with < 4 hours notice
- **Cash handling risk**: COD deliveries in remote areas with large cash amounts (PHP 50,000–200,000 for bulk orders) create security risk; mobile payment adoption should be encouraged
- **Site access**: Construction sites may have limited truck access (narrow roads, low overhead clearance, weight-restricted bridges); pre-delivery site assessment recommended for first-time delivery locations

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate**: Order intake adds ~10–15 min per bulk order; at ~10–15 orders/store/week, ~2–4 hours/week — absorbed by existing 12 sales associates
- **Department Supervisor**: Delivery exception handling adds ~2–3 hours/week during peak construction season
- **Supply Chain Coordinator (HQ)**: 1 coordinator manages DSD vendor coordination across all stores — existing role
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Order intake & scheduling: 10–15 min
- Vendor coordination & dispatch: 5–10 min
- On-site delivery verification: 15–30 min
- Confirmation & invoicing: 5–10 min
- **Total per order**: 35–65 min (store-side); delivery transit time varies by distance

## W1129. Customer Interior Design Material Board Curation & Mood Board Assembly Service

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer requests design consultation for renovation project, or walks in with design inspiration (magazine photo, Pinterest board, contractor plan) |
| **Frequency** | ~3,000–5,000 material board requests/month across all stores (peak during summer renovation season) |
| **Volume** | 1 material board per request (typically covers 1–2 rooms) |
| **Owner** | Sales Associate (Design-trained) / Design Consultant (W148) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate / Design Consultant, Customer, Department Supervisors (relevant departments) |

### Background

Home renovation customers often struggle to visualize how different materials (tiles, paint, fixtures, countertops, cabinets, hardware) will look together in their finished space. Professional interior designers create "material boards" (also called mood boards or design boards) — physical assemblies of material samples showing the proposed combination of finishes, colors, and textures for a room. BuildRight Depot's extensive product range across tiles, paint, plumbing fixtures, lighting, hardware, and countertops makes it uniquely positioned to offer this service. The material board serves as: (a) a visualization tool for the customer to approve the design direction before purchasing; (b) a shopping list of coordinated products that ensures aesthetic consistency; (c) a specification reference for contractors executing the renovation; (d) an upselling vehicle — customers who see a complete coordinated design buy more complementary products than those purchasing individual items. This workflow complements W148 (design consultancy), W211 (3D rendering), W999 (tile sample loan), and W903 (material sample loan) by focusing on the physical material board curation process.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Customer Design Consultation & Style Profiling**: (a) customer describes renovation project: room type (bathroom, kitchen, living room, bedroom), design style preference (modern minimalist, industrial, tropical Filipino, Mediterranean, Scandinavian), budget range, and existing elements to keep; (b) design-trained sales associate or design consultant reviews customer's inspiration materials (photos, magazine clippings, phone images); (c) associate uses in-store design kiosk or tablet to browse BuildRight's product catalog filtered by customer's style, budget, and room type; (d) initial color palette established: 2–3 primary colors, 1–2 accent colors | Sales Associate / Design Consultant | Department Supervisor | 15–25 min |
| 2 | **Material Selection & Sample Gathering**: (a) associate guides customer through relevant departments to select physical samples: tiles (floor and wall) — 2–3 options per surface; paint — color swatches or mixed sample pots; countertop material (granite, quartz, laminate) — sample chips; cabinet hardware (handles, knobs) — physical samples; plumbing fixtures (faucet, shower head) — display models or catalog photos; lighting fixtures — catalog or display samples; (b) for each material, system shows: price per unit/sqm, availability, lead time, and complementary product suggestions; (c) customer selects preferred option for each material category; (d) associate gathers physical samples (tile chips, paint swatches, material chips) | Sales Associate / Design Consultant | Sales Associate | 20–40 min |
| 3 | **Material Board Assembly & Documentation**: (a) associate assembles physical material board on store-provided foam board (A3 size): tiles arranged as they would appear (floor tile at bottom, wall tile above, accent tile as border), paint swatches showing wall color and trim, countertop sample, hardware samples placed on countertop, fixture photos pinned alongside; (b) associate photographs completed material board for digital record; (c) system generates product list linked to material board: each item with SKU, quantity needed (based on room dimensions), unit price, and estimated total; (d) digital material board saved to customer's account for future access and sharing with contractor | Sales Associate / Design Consultant | Sales Associate | 15–20 min |
| 4 | **Quotation Generation & Sales Conversion**: (a) system calculates total project cost based on room dimensions and selected materials; (b) quotation generated per W542 with itemized material list and room-specific quantities; (c) bundle discount offered if customer purchases complete material board package: 5–10% off total vs. individual item pricing per W910; (d) if customer approves: sales order created with scheduled delivery or will-call per W773; (e) if customer takes material board home to decide: associate schedules 48-hour follow-up call per W744; (f) material board retained by customer as reference; physical samples returned per W903 loan policy if not purchased | Sales Associate / System | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Product catalog module — filtered browse by style, room, budget
- Room dimension calculator — quantity estimation based on room measurements
- Bundle pricing engine (W910) — complete package discount
- Quotation generation module (W542) — project quotation
- Customer account module — saved material boards and project lists
- CRM module — design consultation history
- Inventory module — real-time stock and lead time for selected items

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Sample inventory**: Physical tile chips, paint swatches, and material samples are consumable; replenishment must be managed per W903
- **Time investment**: 45–100 minutes per material board session requires dedicated staff time; may not be feasible during peak weekend hours without scheduling
- **Non-conversion risk**: Customer may use the material board as a reference to purchase from competitors or online; offering bundle discount and same-day availability mitigates this
- **Design liability**: Material board is advisory, not a professional interior design service; disclaimers must be clear that color accuracy depends on lighting conditions and actual product may vary from samples
- **Space requirements**: In-store design consultation area needs dedicated space with good lighting, sample storage, and work surface — competing with selling floor space

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Design-trained)**: 1–2 associates per store trained in basic design consultation; ~15–20 material board sessions/week during peak season = ~15–25 hours/week — covered by design-trained associates during assigned consultation hours
- **Design Consultant (HQ)**: Complex projects escalated to 2 HQ-based consultants who visit stores by appointment — existing roles under W148
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Style profiling: 15–25 min
- Material selection: 20–40 min
- Board assembly: 15–20 min
- Quotation & conversion: 10–15 min
- **Total per session**: 60–100 min

## W1131. Customer Construction Project Milestone Photo Documentation & Progress Tracking Portal

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Customer enrolls project in BuildRight's project tracking portal, or project milestone delivery is scheduled |
| **Frequency** | ~500–800 active tracked projects at any time; ~2,000–3,000 milestone photo uploads/month |
| **Volume** | 3–8 photos per milestone; 5–10 milestones per project |
| **Owner** | Sales Associate (Project Liaison) |
| **Participants** | Sales Associate (Project Liaison), Customer, Contractor, Delivery Partner |

### Background

BuildRight Depot's project/trade customers (30% of revenue) and corporate accounts (10%) often manage multi-week or multi-month construction projects with phased material deliveries. Both the customer and BuildRight benefit from systematic photo documentation at each project milestone: (a) the customer gets a visual record of construction progress and material installation for their own records and for social media sharing (driving word-of-mouth referrals); (b) BuildRight gets verification that delivered materials were correctly used (reducing fraudulent damage claims), insights into project progress (triggering timely next-phase material orders), and marketing content (with customer consent — "Built with BuildRight" project showcase). This workflow establishes a digital project tracking portal where milestone photos are uploaded, linked to material orders, and used to trigger proactive sales follow-up. It complements W905 (project photo gallery & social proof platform), W793 (project close-out), and W918 (project budget tracking).

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Project Enrollment & Portal Setup**: (a) when a trade/project customer places their first project order, Sales Associate offers enrollment in BuildRight's Project Tracker; (b) customer creates account on BuildRight mobile app or web portal; (c) project profile created: project name, location, scope (bathroom renovation, house construction, commercial fit-out), estimated timeline, assigned store, project liaison; (d) milestone schedule defined based on project scope: demolition, plumbing rough-in, electrical rough-in, masonry, tiling, painting, fixture installation, final walkthrough; (e) customer grants consent for "Built with BuildRight" photo usage in marketing (opt-in) | Sales Associate (Project Liaison) | Customer | 10–15 min |
| 2 | **Milestone Photo Capture & Upload**: (a) at each material delivery or project milestone, designated party (customer, contractor, or BuildRight delivery driver) photographs progress: overall room/site photo showing work completed, close-up of installed BuildRight materials (tiles, paint, fixtures), before/after comparison at key milestones; (b) photos uploaded to BuildRight Project Tracker via mobile app with timestamp and GPS metadata; (c) system auto-tags photos with relevant project milestone based on delivery schedule; (d) customer can add notes and annotations to photos | Customer / Contractor / Delivery Driver | Customer | 5–10 min per milestone |
| 3 | **System-Triggered Next-Phase Recommendation**: (a) when milestone photos show completion of a phase (e.g., tiling complete), system triggers next-phase material recommendation: grout and sealant for tile phase, paint and primer for painting phase, fixtures and accessories for installation phase; (b) notification sent to customer via app: "Your tiling looks great! Next, you'll need grout and sealant. [View Recommended Products]"; (c) project liaison reviews notification and follows up with proactive call per W744; (d) system estimates remaining material needs based on project scope and completed milestones | System / Sales Associate | Sales Associate | Automated (5 min review) |
| 4 | **Project Completion & Content Curation**: (a) when customer marks project complete, system generates project summary: timeline, total material cost, before/after photos, products used; (b) customer invited to write a review per W510 and share project on social media with #BuiltWithBuildRight hashtag; (c) with customer consent, project featured on BuildRight's website gallery (W905) and social media; (d) project liaison sends completion congratulations and W914 incentive if applicable; (e) project record archived in customer's account for future reorder per W969 | System / Sales Associate | Department Supervisor | 10–15 min |

### System Touchpoints
- Customer mobile app / web portal — project tracker interface
- Photo storage service (cloud) — milestone photo repository
- ERP order module — material delivery schedule linked to milestones
- Recommendation engine (W200 AI-driven personalization) — next-phase product suggestions
- Customer notification engine — milestone alerts and recommendations
- Social media integration — #BuiltWithBuildRight content aggregation
- CRM module — project history and reorder capability

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Customer adoption**: Getting busy contractors to upload photos requires a compelling value proposition; potential incentives include loyalty points per upload, project completion discount, or free next-phase delivery
- **Photo quality**: User-submitted photos may be poor quality, poorly lit, or unrepresentative; system should accept all uploads and let marketing team curate
- **Privacy concerns**: Construction site photos may show identifiable people, neighboring properties, or sensitive information; consent and privacy review required before marketing use
- **Platform maintenance**: Project tracker requires ongoing IT support, mobile app updates, and cloud storage costs

### Staffing Implication
- **Sales Associate (Project Liaison)**: Portal enrollment adds ~10 min per new project; milestone review adds ~5 min per milestone; at ~50 active projects per store at any time = ~3–5 hours/week — absorbed by existing project liaison role
- **Marketing Team (HQ)**: 1 content curator manages gallery and social media from project photos — existing role
- **No permanent incremental headcount**

### Time Estimate
- Project enrollment: 10–15 min
- Photo upload: 5–10 min per milestone
- Next-phase review: 5 min
- Project completion: 10–15 min
- **Total per project lifecycle**: 60–90 min (spread over weeks/months)

## W1136. Customer Product Knowledge Video Library & How-To Tutorial Content Management

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Trigger** | Content creation schedule (monthly), new product launch, seasonal topic (e.g., waterproofing before rainy season), or customer FAQ trend |
| **Frequency** | ~20–30 new videos/quarter; continuous content management |
| **Volume** | Library target: 200–300 videos within Year 1; ~50,000–100,000 monthly views |
| **Owner** | Marketing Content Manager (HQ) |
| **Participants** | Marketing Content Manager, Category Managers, Sales Associates (on-camera talent), IT Digital Team, Vendor Marketing Partners |

### Background

BuildRight Depot's customer base includes a large DIY segment (55% of revenue) that often lacks technical knowledge for home improvement projects. Common barriers to purchase include: "I don't know how to install this," "I'm not sure which product is right for my project," and "What tools do I need?" A comprehensive video library addressing these knowledge gaps serves multiple purposes: (a) reduces purchase hesitation by building customer confidence; (b) decreases product returns caused by incorrect usage or wrong product selection; (c) drives website traffic and SEO rankings (complementing W563 SEO & digital merchandising); (d) provides shareable content for social media (complementing W142 social media management); (e) supports in-store sales associates who can show videos to customers on tablets during consultation; (f) differentiates BuildRight from competitors who don't provide educational content. Video content categories include: product selection guides, installation tutorials, tool usage basics, project planning guides, safety tips, and product comparison reviews.

### Steps

| # | Activity | Role (R) | Role (A) | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Content Calendar & Topic Planning**: (a) Marketing Content Manager develops quarterly content calendar aligned with: seasonal relevance (waterproofing in May, aircon sizing in March, Christmas lights in October); new product launches (W564, W1128); customer FAQ trends from call center (W259) and in-store feedback; search analytics (most-searched product categories on buildright.com.ph); vendor co-marketing opportunities; (b) each video planned with: topic, target length (2–8 minutes), target audience (DIY beginner, experienced DIYer, professional), products featured, filming location (store, HQ studio, customer project site), vendor involvement (co-branded content) | Marketing Content Manager | CMO | 2–3 hours/quarter |
| 2 | **Video Production**: (a) filming: in-store product demonstrations, step-by-step installation tutorials, tool comparison reviews; (b) talent: Sales Associates with strong product knowledge and camera presence (identified during training sessions); Category Managers for expert commentary; vendor product specialists for co-branded content; (c) production quality: smartphone or professional camera, external microphone for clear audio, good lighting (ring lights for indoor, reflectors for outdoor), simple editing (titles, overlays, chapter markers); (d) branding: BuildRight logo watermark, intro/outro bumper, "Available at BuildRight Depot" call-to-action overlay; (e) average production time: 4–8 hours per video (including filming, editing, review, revision) | Marketing Content Manager / Videographer | Marketing Content Manager | 4–8 hours/video |
| 3 | **Content Review & Compliance**: (a) legal review: ensure no misleading claims, proper disclaimers ("Consult a licensed professional for structural/electrical/plumbing work"), trademark compliance; (b) product accuracy: Category Manager verifies product information, specifications, and pricing; (c) safety review: all tutorials involving power tools, chemicals, or structural work include safety warnings and PPE demonstrations; (d) DTI compliance: no deceptive advertising per Consumer Act RA 7394; (e) accessibility: Filipino and English subtitles/captions for all videos | Marketing Content Manager / Legal | CMO | 1–2 hours/video |
| 4 | **Content Publishing & Distribution**: (a) videos published on: BuildRight YouTube channel, buildright.com.ph video library, BuildRight mobile app (in product detail pages and dedicated "How-To" section), in-store tablets (for sales associate reference), Facebook and Instagram (short-form clips); (b) SEO optimization: keyword-rich titles, descriptions, and tags per W563; (c) product page integration: relevant videos embedded in product detail pages on ecommerce site; (d) notification: subscribers notified of new content via email and app push notification | Marketing Content Manager / IT Digital Team | CMO | 30–60 min/video |
| 5 | **Performance Tracking & Content Refresh**: (a) monthly analytics review: views, watch time, engagement rate (likes, comments, shares), click-through to product pages, attributable sales; (b) top-performing videos: promoted more heavily and used as templates for future content; (c) underperforming videos: assessed for topic relevance, thumbnail quality, title optimization; revised or retired; (d) outdated content: products discontinued, pricing changed, or techniques superseded — videos updated or removed; (e) customer feedback: video comments and in-store feedback used to identify new topic opportunities | Marketing Content Manager | CMO | 2–3 hours/month |

### System Touchpoints
- Content management system (CMS) — video hosting and publishing
- Ecommerce platform — product page video embedding
- YouTube Analytics / Google Analytics — view tracking and engagement metrics
- CRM module — video engagement tracked in customer profile
- SEO module (W563) — search optimization
- Social media management platform (W142) — distribution
- Mobile app content management (W615) — app video delivery
- POS mobile tablet — in-store video reference for associates

### Pain Points / Risks
- **Production cost**: Professional-quality video production costs PHP 15,000–50,000 per video; 20–30 videos/quarter = PHP 300,000–1,500,000/year
- **Talent availability**: Sales Associates are not professional presenters; on-camera coaching and multiple takes increase production time
- **Content shelf life**: Product changes, price updates, and seasonal relevance limit video lifespan; quarterly review needed
- **Vendor content control**: Co-branded videos with vendors require vendor approval, which can delay publishing
- **Language considerations**: Philippine market is bilingual (Filipino/English); producing content in both languages doubles production effort

### Staffing Implication
- **Marketing Content Manager (HQ)**: Video content management adds ~15–20 hours/week to existing role — partially absorbed, may need 1 additional content specialist if library scales beyond 300 videos
- **Videographer (HQ)**: 1 dedicated videographer/editor for ongoing production — new hire or outsourced production partner
- **Sales Associates**: On-camera talent is voluntary and compensated with recognition points; ~2–4 hours/quarter per participating associate
- **Potential incremental headcount**: 1 Content Specialist if video library scales significantly

### Time Estimate
- Content planning: 2–3 hours/quarter
- Video production: 4–8 hours/video
- Review & compliance: 1–2 hours/video
- Publishing: 30–60 min/video
- Performance tracking: 2–3 hours/month
- **Total per video**: 6–12 hours end-to-end
